Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 1–2 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His saying, ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. (1) On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she was nursing, and every pregnant woman will drop her load, and you will see people as drunkards, but they are not drunkards; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe. (2)﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: May He, exalted is His remembrance, say: O mankind, beware of the punishment of your Lord by obeying Him, so obey Him and do not disobey Him, for indeed His punishment, for whoever He punishes on the Day of Resurrection, is severe.

Then He, exalted is His praise, described the terror of the signs of that Day and its beginning, saying: ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing.﴾

The people of knowledge differed concerning the time of the occurrence of the convulsion which He, exalted is His praise, described as severe. Some of them said: it occurs in this world before the Day of Resurrection.

Mention of those who said that:
• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾, he said: Before the Hour.
• Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sallat narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudaynah narrated to us, from Ata', from Amir, ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾, he said: This is in the world, before the Day of Resurrection.
• Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour﴾, he said: Its convulsion is its signs. The verses ﴿On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she was nursing, and every pregnant woman will drop her load, and you will see people as drunkards, but they are not drunkards﴾.
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Ata', from Amir, ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾, he said: This is in the world, among the signs of the Hour.

A report has been transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) in a manner similar to what these men said, in a chain of which there is some weakness [[Perhaps the meaning of "there is weakness in its chain" is that it contains two unknown men from the Ansar.]], and it is this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi al-Madani, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from a man of the Ansar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the Trumpet and gave it to Israfil, and he places it at his mouth, gazing with his eye towards the Throne, awaiting when he will be commanded. Abu Hurayrah said: O Messenger of Allah, and what is the Trumpet? He said: A horn. He said: And what is it like? He said: A great horn, into which three blasts will be blown: the first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of swooning, and the third is the blast of rising for the Lord of the worlds. Allah, mighty and majestic, will command Israfil with the first blast, and he will say: Blow the blast of terror. So the people of the heavens and the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills. Allah will command him and he will prolong and extend it, without pause, and this is what Allah refers to when He says: ﴿And these do not await but a single cry, with no respite﴾. Then Allah will set the mountains moving, and they will become like a mirage, and the earth will be shaken with its people, a violent shaking; and this is what Allah refers to when He says: ﴿On the Day the quaker quakes, followed by the follower; hearts that Day will be trembling﴾. The earth will become like a ship that is sinking in the sea, struck by the waves, capsizing with its people, or like a lamp hung from the Throne, swayed by the winds, and the people will sway upon its back. The nursing mothers will forget, the pregnant women will drop their loads, the children will turn white-haired, and the devils will fly off fleeing until they reach the horizons, but the angels will meet them and strike their faces, so they will turn back, and the people will turn away fleeing, calling out to one another; and this is what Allah refers to when He says: ﴿The Day of Calling Out, the Day you turn back fleeing; you will have no protector from Allah, and whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾. While they are in that state, suddenly the earth will split from one end to the other, and they will see a tremendous thing, and such distress will seize them as only Allah knows. Then they will look at the sky, and behold, it will be like molten brass; then its sun will be eclipsed, its moon will be eclipsed, and its stars will scatter; then it will be stripped away from them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And the dead know nothing of any of that." Abu Hurayrah said: "Then who is it that Allah excepted when He says ﴿So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills﴾?" He said: "Those are the martyrs. The terror reaches only the living; those are alive with their Lord, being provided for. Allah protects them from the terror of that Day and grants them security. And it is the punishment of Allah which He sends upon the worst of His creation, and it is what He refers to when He says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ ... up to His saying ﴿but the punishment of Allah is severe﴾."

And this view which we have mentioned from Alqamah and al-Sha'bi, and those we mentioned it from, is a view which would have been valid were it not for the arrival of authentic reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) contrary to it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is most knowledgeable of the meanings of Allah's revelation and its sending down.

The correct view on this matter is what the report from him has established as sound.

Mention of the transmission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in accordance with what we have mentioned: Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to me, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard my father narrate from Qatadah, from a companion of his who narrated to him, from Imran ibn Husayn, who said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was on one of his expeditions, and he had lengthened the journey for his companions, he called out with this verse: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾. He said: So they urged their mounts until they were around the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "Do you know what day that is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "That is the Day when Adam will be called, and his Lord will say to him: Send forth the company of the Fire: from every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine to the Fire." He said: So the people were struck dumb, and not a single laughing face was seen among them. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Be diligent and rejoice, for with you are two creations which have never been in any people except that they multiplied them: whoever perished from the children of Adam, and whoever perished from the children of Iblis, and Ya'juj and Ma'juj." He said: "Rejoice, for you among the people are but like the white mark on the flank of a camel, or like the spot on the foreleg of a beast."

• Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Abi Abdullah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Imran ibn Husayn, from the Prophet (ﷺ). And Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us; and Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Hisham, all together, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Imran ibn Husayn, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with the like of it.
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah, from al-Ala' ibn Ziyad, from Imran, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in a similar manner.
• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: "It reached me that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from the expedition of al-Usrah, with his companions, after he had approached Medina, he recited ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. On the Day you see it﴾ ... the verse, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know what day that is?" It was said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." Then he mentioned something similar, except that he added: "There were never two messengers except that between them there was an interval of ignorance, and those are the people of the Fire; and you are among two creations, none of the people of the earth can count them except that they outnumber them, and they are Ya'juj and Ma'juj, and they are the people of the Fire; and the number is completed from the hypocrites."
• Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: It is said to Adam: "Bring forth the company of the Fire." He says: "And what is the company of the Fire?" It is said: "From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine." At that moment the young will turn white-haired, the pregnant will drop her load, and you will see people as drunkards, but they are not drunkards, but the punishment of Allah is severe. He said: We said: "Then where is the one who will be saved, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Rejoice, for one of you will be with a thousand of Ya'juj and Ma'juj." Then he said: "I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise," so we exclaimed Allahu akbar and praised Allah. Then he said: "I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise," so we exclaimed Allahu akbar and praised Allah. Then he said: "I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. Your likeness among the people is only like the white hair in a black ox, or the black hair in a white ox."
• Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will say to Adam on the Day of Resurrection..." and then he mentioned something similar.
• Isa ibn Uthman ibn Isa al-Ramli narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Isa narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the gathering, and said: Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection, O Adam, and he will say: Here I am at Your service, and goodness is in Your hands. He will say: Send forth a company to the Fire." Then he mentioned something similar.
• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: "﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ ... up to ﴿the punishment of Allah is severe﴾ ... the verse was revealed upon the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was on a journey, so he raised his voice with it until his companions gathered around him, and he said: "Do you know what day this is? This is the Day when Allah says to Adam: O Adam, arise and send forth the company of the Fire, from every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine!" That was hard upon the Muslims, so the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Be steadfast and moderate, and rejoice, for by Him in whose hand is my soul, you among the people are only like the white mark on the flank of a camel, or the spot on the foreleg of a beast; and indeed with you are two creations, which have never been in anything except that they multiplied it: Ya'juj and Ma'juj, and whoever perished of the disbelieving jinn and mankind."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying Ibn Thawr narrated, from Ma'mar, from Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun, who said: I entered upon Ibn Mas'ud in the treasury, and he said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Would you be content to be a quarter of the people of Paradise?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Would you be content to be a third of the people of Paradise?" We said: "Yes." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. I will inform you of that: no one enters Paradise except a Muslim soul, and the small number of Muslims among the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection is like the black hair in a white ox, or the white hair in a black ox."
• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾: "This is the Day of Resurrection."

The word zalzalah is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "I shook the earth with so-and-so" (zalzaltu bi-fulan al-ard), azalziluha, zalzalatan and zilzalan, with the zay in kasra, as from zilzal, as Allah said: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its shaking﴾. Likewise the verbal noun of every regular verb when it comes in the pattern fi'lan is with the initial letter kasra, like waswasa, wasawsatan and wiswasan. But if it is a noun, it is with the initial letter fatha, al-zalzal and al-wasmas, the latter being what whispers into a person. As the poet said:

"The ignorant, the misguided, knows that Time has in it adversity and quaking."[[The verse is evidence that the quadriliteral doubled verbal noun when it comes in the pattern "fa'lal" is with a kasra on the first letter; if the first letter is given a fatha, it is a name of the verbal noun, not the verbal noun itself, as in the verse. In (Lisan al-Arab: zalzal), it says: al-zalzalah and al-zalzal (with fatha) are the shaking of a thing; one says zalzalahu zalzalatan and zalzalan (with kasra in the second). They have said: al-fi'lal (with fatha) and al-zilzal (with kasra) are regular in all verbal nouns of the doubled verb. The noun is al-zalzal (with fatha). And there is no fa'lal with the first letter fatha in speech except in the doubled form, such as al-salsal and al-zalzal. Abu Ishaq said: al-zilzal (with kasra) is the verbal noun, and al-zalzal (with fatha) is the noun; likewise al-wiswas is the verbal noun and al-wawas is the noun. End.]]

And His saying ﴿On the Day you see it﴾: He, exalted is His praise, says: On the Day you, O mankind, see the convulsion of the Hour, every nursing mother will be made to forget, from its magnitude, the child she is nursing. By His saying ﴿tadhhalu﴾ He means: forgets and leaves off from the severity of its distress. It is said: dhahaltu 'an kadha adhhalu 'anhu dhuhulan, and dhahiltu also, which is rare; the eloquent form is with fatha on the ha'. As for the imperfect, the ha' is fatha in both dialects, nothing else has been heard. And from it is the poet's saying:

"His heart has become sober, O Azz, or nearly forgets."[[This is the opening line of a poem by Kuthayyir ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Khuza'i, famous as "Kuthayyir of Azzah," in praise of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan; its second hemistich is: "and he is about to desire separation or change."]]

(Diwan edition, Algeria, 2:28) Its commentator said: "His heart became sober" (ṣaḥā qalbuhu). In al-Iqtiḍab, it is said: Ibn Qutayba said: "The sky became clear (aṣḥat al-samāʾ) and the one who blamed him (al-ʿādhila) became sober (ṣaḥā) from intoxication." As for the sky, one says only aṣḥat with the alif; as for intoxication, one says only ṣaḥā without the alif; and as for recovery from love, I have heard only ṣaḥā without the alif, like intoxication. It is evidence for the verb "tadhhalu" (to be distracted) in its past form, which has two dialects: opening the ha' and its kasra, and the first is the more eloquent of the two dialects. In (Lisan al-ʿArab: dh-h-l) it says: In the Mighty Revelation: "the day when every nursing mother will be distracted" (yawma tadhhalu kullu murḍiʿatin), meaning: she will forget her child. Ibn Sayyida said: dhahila al-shayʾ, dhahila ʿanhu, and dhahilahu, and dhahila (with kasra) yadhhalu dhahlan and dhuhulan: he left it deliberately, or was heedless of it, or forgot it due to preoccupation. It is said: al-dhahl is forgetfulness and the heart's ease and release from attachment. One says: adhhalahu al-amr and dhahalahu ʿanhu. End.

As for when it is intended that the terror made him forget and distracted him, one says: adhhalahu hadhā al-amr ʿan kadhā yudhhiluhu idhhālan. Regarding the presence of the ha' in His words "every nursing mother" (kullu murḍiʿatin), there is disagreement among the grammarians of Arabic. Some of the Kufan grammarians used to say: when the ha' is affirmed in murḍiʿa, it refers to the mother of the nursing child; when it is dropped, it refers to a woman who has a child she is nursing, because the action is intended with her. They said: if the attribute were intended as a descriptive term, it would be said murḍiʿ. He said: likewise every mufʿil or fāʿil that applies to a female and not a male is without ha', such as muqrib, mūqir, mushdin, ḥāmil, and ḥāʾiḍ. [Consider this matter and consult the Lisan, for it is more detailed.]

Abu Jaʿfar said: This view is, in my opinion, more correct in this matter, because it is the custom of the Arabs to drop the feminine ha' from every fāʿil and mufʿil when they describe a feminine noun with it, even if the masculine has no share in it. When they intend to report about her that she will do it and has not yet done it, they affirm the feminine ha' to distinguish between the attribute and the action. Among it is the saying of al-Aʿshā about what is occurring and had not yet occurred:

Ayā jāratā bīnī fa-innaka ṭāliqah... kadhāka umūru al-nāsi ghādin wa ṭāriqah

[The verse is by Aʿshā ibn Qays ibn Thaʿlaba, from a qasida he composed for his wife al-Hazaniyya (his Diwan, Cairo edition with the commentary of Dr. Muhammad Husayn, p. 263), and the narration in it is: "yā jāratī" (O my neighbor). Its commentator said: "the neighbor" here is his wife. Bīnī: i.e., separate from me. Ghādin and ṭāriqa: "ghādin" is used in the sense of plural, and "ṭāriqa" is feminine in the sense of a group. The ghādī is one who comes to his enemy in the morning. The ṭāriq is one who knocks, i.e., comes at night. Ṣāḥib al-Lisan (ṭ-l-q) recited it and said: Ibn al-Aʿrabi said: "ṭuliqtu" (with damma on the lam) from divorce is better, and "ṭaliqtu" (with fatḥa on the lam) is permissible. All of them say: "imraʾa ṭāliq" without ha'. As for the saying of al-Aʿshā: "ayā jāratanā bīnī fa-innaka ṭāliqah", al-Layth said: he intended: "ṭāliqa ghadan" (divorced tomorrow). Another said: he said ṭāliqa in terms of the action, because it is said: "hā qad ṭuliqat", so he built the adjective upon the verb. The divorce of a woman is her separation from her husband; and "imraʾa ṭāliq" is one of the women "ṭalq", and "ṭāliqa" is one of the women "ṭawāliq". He recited al-Aʿshā's verse: "ajāratanā bīnī fa-innaka ṭāliqah"... the verse.]

As for what is an attribute, such as the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

Fa-mithluki ḥublā qad ṭaraqtu wa murḍiʿun... fa-alhaytuhā ʿan dhī tamāʾima muḥwil

[The verse is from the Mu'allaqa of Imru' al-Qays ibn Hujr al-Kindi (Mukhtar al-Shiʿr al-Jahili, with commentary by Mustafa al-Saqqa, Mustafa al-Babi al-Halabi and sons edition, p. 25). Its commentator said: "ṭaraqtu": I came to. "Al-tamāʾim": amulets hung on the child. "Muḥwil": i.e., a year has passed for him; it is said "aḥwala al-ṣabiyy" so he is "muḥwil"; it is narrated as "mughīl", which is the one whose mother nurses him while she is pregnant; it is said "aghālat al-mar'a waladahā", so she is "mughīl" (with kasra on the ghayn), and "aghlaytuhu" so she is "mughīl" (with sukun on the ghayn and kasra on the yāʾ); she gave him ghīl, which is the milk of a pregnant woman, and the child is "mughāl" and "mughīl". The evidence in the verse is that "murḍiʿ" is without ha'. It is among the attributes specific to women and not men, and so it is sufficient without the ha' which enters attributes to distinguish male from female. As for His words, exalted is He, "the day when every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed", with the ha' in "murḍiʿa", what is meant is the woman who has a child she is nursing; she is engaged in the action, so the action is intended here, and the attribute then follows the action in masculine and feminine forms; one says "arḍaʿat" or "tarḍaʿu al-umm waliydahā", so she is "murḍiʿa" to him. As for a female whose nature is to be a nursing one but who is not engaged in the act, she is called "murḍiʿ" without the feminine ha', because this is an attribute specific to females, so there is no need for the ha' to distinguish.]

Sometimes they affirm the ha' in both cases and sometimes they drop it in both, but the eloquent of their speech is what I have described.

So the interpretation of the speech, then, is: "On the day you, people, see the quaking of the Hour, every mother who nurses her child will forget and abandon what she nursed," as:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "On the day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed": "She will abandon her child because of the distress that has descended upon her."
- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Bakr, from al-Hasan, regarding "every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed": "She is distracted from her children without weaning." "And every pregnant woman will deliver her burden": "The pregnant women will cast what is in their wombs before completion." "And every pregnant woman will deliver her burden": means: every pregnant woman will miscarry from the severity of that distress.

* *

As for His words, "And you see the people as drunk" (wa tarā al-nāsa sukārā):

The reciters of the major cities recited "wa tarā al-nāsa sukārā" in the address to a single person, as if He said: "And you see, O Muhammad, the people at that time as drunk, and they are not drunk." It was also narrated from Abu Zurʿa ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarir "wa tura al-nāsa" with damma on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the nūn of al-nās, from the saying of one who says: "urīta, turā", which seeks the noun and the predicate, like "ẓanna" and its sisters.

The correct recitation in this regard, in our view, is what the reciters of the major cities follow, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters.

The reciters differed in reciting His words "sukārā". The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa recited "sukārā wa mā hum bi-sukārā". The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited "wa tarā al-nāsa sakrā wa mā hum bi-sakrā".

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that both are widely transmitted recitations among the reciters of the major cities, close in meaning; whichever of the two a reciter recites, he is correct. The meaning of the speech: "And you see the people, O Muhammad, from the greatness of the distress and its severity that has befallen them, as drunk from terror, and they are not drunk from wine."

Ahl al-ta'wil (the exegetes) said likewise.

Those who said that: al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Bakr, from al-Hasan, regarding "And you see the people as drunk" — "from fear" — "and they are not drunk" — "from drink."

- al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words "and they are not drunk": "they are not drunk from wine," "but the punishment of God is severe."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "And you see the people as drunk, and they are not drunk": "They have not drunk wine." He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "But the punishment of God is severe," meaning: but they have become drunk from fear of God's punishment upon witnessing what they witnessed of the distress of that day and its great terror, along with their knowledge of the severity of God's punishment.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 1–2 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His saying, ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. (1) On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she was nursing, and every pregnant woman will drop her load, and you will see people as drunkards, but they are not drunkards; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe. (2)﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: May He, exalted is His remembrance, say: O mankind, beware of the punishment of your Lord by obeying Him, so obey Him and do not disobey Him, for indeed His punishment, for whoever He punishes on the Day of Resurrection, is severe.

Then He, exalted is His praise, described the terror of the signs of that Day and its beginning, saying: ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing.﴾

The people of knowledge differed concerning the time of the occurrence of the convulsion which He, exalted is His praise, described as severe. Some of them said: it occurs in this world before the Day of Resurrection.

Mention of those who said that:
• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾, he said: Before the Hour.
• Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sallat narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudaynah narrated to us, from Ata', from Amir, ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾, he said: This is in the world, before the Day of Resurrection.
• Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour﴾, he said: Its convulsion is its signs. The verses ﴿On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she was nursing, and every pregnant woman will drop her load, and you will see people as drunkards, but they are not drunkards﴾.
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Ata', from Amir, ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾, he said: This is in the world, among the signs of the Hour.

A report has been transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) in a manner similar to what these men said, in a chain of which there is some weakness [[Perhaps the meaning of "there is weakness in its chain" is that it contains two unknown men from the Ansar.]], and it is this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi al-Madani, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from a man of the Ansar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the Trumpet and gave it to Israfil, and he places it at his mouth, gazing with his eye towards the Throne, awaiting when he will be commanded. Abu Hurayrah said: O Messenger of Allah, and what is the Trumpet? He said: A horn. He said: And what is it like? He said: A great horn, into which three blasts will be blown: the first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of swooning, and the third is the blast of rising for the Lord of the worlds. Allah, mighty and majestic, will command Israfil with the first blast, and he will say: Blow the blast of terror. So the people of the heavens and the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills. Allah will command him and he will prolong and extend it, without pause, and this is what Allah refers to when He says: ﴿And these do not await but a single cry, with no respite﴾. Then Allah will set the mountains moving, and they will become like a mirage, and the earth will be shaken with its people, a violent shaking; and this is what Allah refers to when He says: ﴿On the Day the quaker quakes, followed by the follower; hearts that Day will be trembling﴾. The earth will become like a ship that is sinking in the sea, struck by the waves, capsizing with its people, or like a lamp hung from the Throne, swayed by the winds, and the people will sway upon its back. The nursing mothers will forget, the pregnant women will drop their loads, the children will turn white-haired, and the devils will fly off fleeing until they reach the horizons, but the angels will meet them and strike their faces, so they will turn back, and the people will turn away fleeing, calling out to one another; and this is what Allah refers to when He says: ﴿The Day of Calling Out, the Day you turn back fleeing; you will have no protector from Allah, and whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾. While they are in that state, suddenly the earth will split from one end to the other, and they will see a tremendous thing, and such distress will seize them as only Allah knows. Then they will look at the sky, and behold, it will be like molten brass; then its sun will be eclipsed, its moon will be eclipsed, and its stars will scatter; then it will be stripped away from them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And the dead know nothing of any of that." Abu Hurayrah said: "Then who is it that Allah excepted when He says ﴿So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills﴾?" He said: "Those are the martyrs. The terror reaches only the living; those are alive with their Lord, being provided for. Allah protects them from the terror of that Day and grants them security. And it is the punishment of Allah which He sends upon the worst of His creation, and it is what He refers to when He says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ ... up to His saying ﴿but the punishment of Allah is severe﴾."

And this view which we have mentioned from Alqamah and al-Sha'bi, and those we mentioned it from, is a view which would have been valid were it not for the arrival of authentic reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) contrary to it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is most knowledgeable of the meanings of Allah's revelation and its sending down.

The correct view on this matter is what the report from him has established as sound.

Mention of the transmission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in accordance with what we have mentioned: Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to me, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard my father narrate from Qatadah, from a companion of his who narrated to him, from Imran ibn Husayn, who said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was on one of his expeditions, and he had lengthened the journey for his companions, he called out with this verse: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾. He said: So they urged their mounts until they were around the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "Do you know what day that is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "That is the Day when Adam will be called, and his Lord will say to him: Send forth the company of the Fire: from every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine to the Fire." He said: So the people were struck dumb, and not a single laughing face was seen among them. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Be diligent and rejoice, for with you are two creations which have never been in any people except that they multiplied them: whoever perished from the children of Adam, and whoever perished from the children of Iblis, and Ya'juj and Ma'juj." He said: "Rejoice, for you among the people are but like the white mark on the flank of a camel, or like the spot on the foreleg of a beast."

• Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Abi Abdullah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Imran ibn Husayn, from the Prophet (ﷺ). And Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us; and Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Hisham, all together, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Imran ibn Husayn, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with the like of it.
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah, from al-Ala' ibn Ziyad, from Imran, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in a similar manner.
• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: "It reached me that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from the expedition of al-Usrah, with his companions, after he had approached Medina, he recited ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. On the Day you see it﴾ ... the verse, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know what day that is?" It was said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." Then he mentioned something similar, except that he added: "There were never two messengers except that between them there was an interval of ignorance, and those are the people of the Fire; and you are among two creations, none of the people of the earth can count them except that they outnumber them, and they are Ya'juj and Ma'juj, and they are the people of the Fire; and the number is completed from the hypocrites."
• Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: It is said to Adam: "Bring forth the company of the Fire." He says: "And what is the company of the Fire?" It is said: "From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine." At that moment the young will turn white-haired, the pregnant will drop her load, and you will see people as drunkards, but they are not drunkards, but the punishment of Allah is severe. He said: We said: "Then where is the one who will be saved, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Rejoice, for one of you will be with a thousand of Ya'juj and Ma'juj." Then he said: "I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise," so we exclaimed Allahu akbar and praised Allah. Then he said: "I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise," so we exclaimed Allahu akbar and praised Allah. Then he said: "I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. Your likeness among the people is only like the white hair in a black ox, or the black hair in a white ox."
• Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will say to Adam on the Day of Resurrection..." and then he mentioned something similar.
• Isa ibn Uthman ibn Isa al-Ramli narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Isa narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the gathering, and said: Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection, O Adam, and he will say: Here I am at Your service, and goodness is in Your hands. He will say: Send forth a company to the Fire." Then he mentioned something similar.
• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: "﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ ... up to ﴿the punishment of Allah is severe﴾ ... the verse was revealed upon the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was on a journey, so he raised his voice with it until his companions gathered around him, and he said: "Do you know what day this is? This is the Day when Allah says to Adam: O Adam, arise and send forth the company of the Fire, from every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine!" That was hard upon the Muslims, so the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Be steadfast and moderate, and rejoice, for by Him in whose hand is my soul, you among the people are only like the white mark on the flank of a camel, or the spot on the foreleg of a beast; and indeed with you are two creations, which have never been in anything except that they multiplied it: Ya'juj and Ma'juj, and whoever perished of the disbelieving jinn and mankind."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying Ibn Thawr narrated, from Ma'mar, from Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun, who said: I entered upon Ibn Mas'ud in the treasury, and he said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Would you be content to be a quarter of the people of Paradise?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Would you be content to be a third of the people of Paradise?" We said: "Yes." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. I will inform you of that: no one enters Paradise except a Muslim soul, and the small number of Muslims among the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection is like the black hair in a white ox, or the white hair in a black ox."
• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾: "This is the Day of Resurrection."

The word zalzalah is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "I shook the earth with so-and-so" (zalzaltu bi-fulan al-ard), azalziluha, zalzalatan and zilzalan, with the zay in kasra, as from zilzal, as Allah said: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its shaking﴾. Likewise the verbal noun of every regular verb when it comes in the pattern fi'lan is with the initial letter kasra, like waswasa, wasawsatan and wiswasan. But if it is a noun, it is with the initial letter fatha, al-zalzal and al-wasmas, the latter being what whispers into a person. As the poet said:

"The ignorant, the misguided, knows that Time has in it adversity and quaking."[[The verse is evidence that the quadriliteral doubled verbal noun when it comes in the pattern "fa'lal" is with a kasra on the first letter; if the first letter is given a fatha, it is a name of the verbal noun, not the verbal noun itself, as in the verse. In (Lisan al-Arab: zalzal), it says: al-zalzalah and al-zalzal (with fatha) are the shaking of a thing; one says zalzalahu zalzalatan and zalzalan (with kasra in the second). They have said: al-fi'lal (with fatha) and al-zilzal (with kasra) are regular in all verbal nouns of the doubled verb. The noun is al-zalzal (with fatha). And there is no fa'lal with the first letter fatha in speech except in the doubled form, such as al-salsal and al-zalzal. Abu Ishaq said: al-zilzal (with kasra) is the verbal noun, and al-zalzal (with fatha) is the noun; likewise al-wiswas is the verbal noun and al-wawas is the noun. End.]]

And His saying ﴿On the Day you see it﴾: He, exalted is His praise, says: On the Day you, O mankind, see the convulsion of the Hour, every nursing mother will be made to forget, from its magnitude, the child she is nursing. By His saying ﴿tadhhalu﴾ He means: forgets and leaves off from the severity of its distress. It is said: dhahaltu 'an kadha adhhalu 'anhu dhuhulan, and dhahiltu also, which is rare; the eloquent form is with fatha on the ha'. As for the imperfect, the ha' is fatha in both dialects, nothing else has been heard. And from it is the poet's saying:

"His heart has become sober, O Azz, or nearly forgets."[[This is the opening line of a poem by Kuthayyir ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Khuza'i, famous as "Kuthayyir of Azzah," in praise of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan; its second hemistich is: "and he is about to desire separation or change."]]

(Diwan edition, Algeria, 2:28) Its commentator said: "His heart became sober" (ṣaḥā qalbuhu). In al-Iqtiḍab, it is said: Ibn Qutayba said: "The sky became clear (aṣḥat al-samāʾ) and the one who blamed him (al-ʿādhila) became sober (ṣaḥā) from intoxication." As for the sky, one says only aṣḥat with the alif; as for intoxication, one says only ṣaḥā without the alif; and as for recovery from love, I have heard only ṣaḥā without the alif, like intoxication. It is evidence for the verb "tadhhalu" (to be distracted) in its past form, which has two dialects: opening the ha' and its kasra, and the first is the more eloquent of the two dialects. In (Lisan al-ʿArab: dh-h-l) it says: In the Mighty Revelation: "the day when every nursing mother will be distracted" (yawma tadhhalu kullu murḍiʿatin), meaning: she will forget her child. Ibn Sayyida said: dhahila al-shayʾ, dhahila ʿanhu, and dhahilahu, and dhahila (with kasra) yadhhalu dhahlan and dhuhulan: he left it deliberately, or was heedless of it, or forgot it due to preoccupation. It is said: al-dhahl is forgetfulness and the heart's ease and release from attachment. One says: adhhalahu al-amr and dhahalahu ʿanhu. End.

As for when it is intended that the terror made him forget and distracted him, one says: adhhalahu hadhā al-amr ʿan kadhā yudhhiluhu idhhālan. Regarding the presence of the ha' in His words "every nursing mother" (kullu murḍiʿatin), there is disagreement among the grammarians of Arabic. Some of the Kufan grammarians used to say: when the ha' is affirmed in murḍiʿa, it refers to the mother of the nursing child; when it is dropped, it refers to a woman who has a child she is nursing, because the action is intended with her. They said: if the attribute were intended as a descriptive term, it would be said murḍiʿ. He said: likewise every mufʿil or fāʿil that applies to a female and not a male is without ha', such as muqrib, mūqir, mushdin, ḥāmil, and ḥāʾiḍ. [Consider this matter and consult the Lisan, for it is more detailed.]

Abu Jaʿfar said: This view is, in my opinion, more correct in this matter, because it is the custom of the Arabs to drop the feminine ha' from every fāʿil and mufʿil when they describe a feminine noun with it, even if the masculine has no share in it. When they intend to report about her that she will do it and has not yet done it, they affirm the feminine ha' to distinguish between the attribute and the action. Among it is the saying of al-Aʿshā about what is occurring and had not yet occurred:

Ayā jāratā bīnī fa-innaka ṭāliqah... kadhāka umūru al-nāsi ghādin wa ṭāriqah

[The verse is by Aʿshā ibn Qays ibn Thaʿlaba, from a qasida he composed for his wife al-Hazaniyya (his Diwan, Cairo edition with the commentary of Dr. Muhammad Husayn, p. 263), and the narration in it is: "yā jāratī" (O my neighbor). Its commentator said: "the neighbor" here is his wife. Bīnī: i.e., separate from me. Ghādin and ṭāriqa: "ghādin" is used in the sense of plural, and "ṭāriqa" is feminine in the sense of a group. The ghādī is one who comes to his enemy in the morning. The ṭāriq is one who knocks, i.e., comes at night. Ṣāḥib al-Lisan (ṭ-l-q) recited it and said: Ibn al-Aʿrabi said: "ṭuliqtu" (with damma on the lam) from divorce is better, and "ṭaliqtu" (with fatḥa on the lam) is permissible. All of them say: "imraʾa ṭāliq" without ha'. As for the saying of al-Aʿshā: "ayā jāratanā bīnī fa-innaka ṭāliqah", al-Layth said: he intended: "ṭāliqa ghadan" (divorced tomorrow). Another said: he said ṭāliqa in terms of the action, because it is said: "hā qad ṭuliqat", so he built the adjective upon the verb. The divorce of a woman is her separation from her husband; and "imraʾa ṭāliq" is one of the women "ṭalq", and "ṭāliqa" is one of the women "ṭawāliq". He recited al-Aʿshā's verse: "ajāratanā bīnī fa-innaka ṭāliqah"... the verse.]

As for what is an attribute, such as the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

Fa-mithluki ḥublā qad ṭaraqtu wa murḍiʿun... fa-alhaytuhā ʿan dhī tamāʾima muḥwil

[The verse is from the Mu'allaqa of Imru' al-Qays ibn Hujr al-Kindi (Mukhtar al-Shiʿr al-Jahili, with commentary by Mustafa al-Saqqa, Mustafa al-Babi al-Halabi and sons edition, p. 25). Its commentator said: "ṭaraqtu": I came to. "Al-tamāʾim": amulets hung on the child. "Muḥwil": i.e., a year has passed for him; it is said "aḥwala al-ṣabiyy" so he is "muḥwil"; it is narrated as "mughīl", which is the one whose mother nurses him while she is pregnant; it is said "aghālat al-mar'a waladahā", so she is "mughīl" (with kasra on the ghayn), and "aghlaytuhu" so she is "mughīl" (with sukun on the ghayn and kasra on the yāʾ); she gave him ghīl, which is the milk of a pregnant woman, and the child is "mughāl" and "mughīl". The evidence in the verse is that "murḍiʿ" is without ha'. It is among the attributes specific to women and not men, and so it is sufficient without the ha' which enters attributes to distinguish male from female. As for His words, exalted is He, "the day when every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed", with the ha' in "murḍiʿa", what is meant is the woman who has a child she is nursing; she is engaged in the action, so the action is intended here, and the attribute then follows the action in masculine and feminine forms; one says "arḍaʿat" or "tarḍaʿu al-umm waliydahā", so she is "murḍiʿa" to him. As for a female whose nature is to be a nursing one but who is not engaged in the act, she is called "murḍiʿ" without the feminine ha', because this is an attribute specific to females, so there is no need for the ha' to distinguish.]

Sometimes they affirm the ha' in both cases and sometimes they drop it in both, but the eloquent of their speech is what I have described.

So the interpretation of the speech, then, is: "On the day you, people, see the quaking of the Hour, every mother who nurses her child will forget and abandon what she nursed," as:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "On the day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed": "She will abandon her child because of the distress that has descended upon her."
- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Bakr, from al-Hasan, regarding "every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed": "She is distracted from her children without weaning." "And every pregnant woman will deliver her burden": "The pregnant women will cast what is in their wombs before completion." "And every pregnant woman will deliver her burden": means: every pregnant woman will miscarry from the severity of that distress.

* *

As for His words, "And you see the people as drunk" (wa tarā al-nāsa sukārā):

The reciters of the major cities recited "wa tarā al-nāsa sukārā" in the address to a single person, as if He said: "And you see, O Muhammad, the people at that time as drunk, and they are not drunk." It was also narrated from Abu Zurʿa ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarir "wa tura al-nāsa" with damma on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the nūn of al-nās, from the saying of one who says: "urīta, turā", which seeks the noun and the predicate, like "ẓanna" and its sisters.

The correct recitation in this regard, in our view, is what the reciters of the major cities follow, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters.

The reciters differed in reciting His words "sukārā". The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa recited "sukārā wa mā hum bi-sukārā". The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited "wa tarā al-nāsa sakrā wa mā hum bi-sakrā".

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that both are widely transmitted recitations among the reciters of the major cities, close in meaning; whichever of the two a reciter recites, he is correct. The meaning of the speech: "And you see the people, O Muhammad, from the greatness of the distress and its severity that has befallen them, as drunk from terror, and they are not drunk from wine."

Ahl al-ta'wil (the exegetes) said likewise.

Those who said that: al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Bakr, from al-Hasan, regarding "And you see the people as drunk" — "from fear" — "and they are not drunk" — "from drink."

- al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words "and they are not drunk": "they are not drunk from wine," "but the punishment of God is severe."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "And you see the people as drunk, and they are not drunk": "They have not drunk wine." He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "But the punishment of God is severe," meaning: but they have become drunk from fear of God's punishment upon witnessing what they witnessed of the distress of that day and its great terror, along with their knowledge of the severity of God's punishment.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 3:

The interpretation of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And among the people is one who disputes about Allah without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil﴾ (22:3).

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿And among the people is one who disputes about Allah without knowledge﴾, that he said: al-Nadr ibn al-Harith [[Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kaladah had studied medicine and philosophy with his father in al-Hira.]]. By His statement ﴿one who disputes about Allah without knowledge﴾ He means one who argues about Allah, claiming that Allah is unable to bring back to life one who has decayed and become dust, without any knowledge he possesses, but out of ignorance of what he is saying. ﴿And he follows﴾ in his saying that and his disputing about Allah without knowledge ﴿every rebellious devil﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 4:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is decreed concerning him that whoever takes him as an ally, he will mislead him and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: it was decreed concerning the Devil. So the meaning of ﴿kutiba﴾ (it was decreed) here is "qudiya" (it was judged), and the pronoun in His saying "alayhi" (concerning him) refers to the Devil.

As reported:

* Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿It is decreed concerning him that whoever takes him as an ally﴾ he said: It was decreed concerning the Devil that whoever follows the Devil from among the creation of God.

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of God ﴿It is decreed concerning him that whoever takes him as an ally﴾ he said: "The Devil" – he followed him.

* al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, ﴿that whoever takes him as an ally﴾, he said: he followed him.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿for indeed he misleads him﴾

It means: indeed the Devil misleads him, that is, he misleads whoever takes him as an ally. The pronoun in "yudillahu" (he misleads him) refers to "man" (whoever) in His saying ﴿whoever takes him as an ally﴾. The meaning of the statement is: it was decreed upon the Devil that he would mislead his followers and not guide them to the truth.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿and guides him to the punishment of the Blaze﴾

It means: he drives whoever follows him to the punishment of blazing Hell, and his driving him to it is through his calling them to obey him and to disobey the Most Merciful. That is his guiding of whoever follows him to the punishment of Hell.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 5:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, [consider that] We created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed, that We may make clear to you. And We settle in the wombs whatever We will for a specified term; then We bring you out as a child; then [We let you reach] your maturity (ashudd)﴾.

This is a proof from God against the one He mentioned among the people who argue about God without knowledge, following the rebellious devil, and a reminder to him of the point of error in his statement and his denial of what he denied of his Lord's power. He says: O mankind, if you are in doubt about Our power to resurrect you from your graves after your death and decay, out of your magnifying of that, then indeed in Our originating the creation of your father Adam (ﷺ) from dust, then Our producing you from the sperm-drop of Adam, then Our turning you through states, one state after another, from sperm-drop to clot, then from clot to lump of flesh, is a lesson and an admonition for you, by which you may take heed. Thus you will know that the One who is able to do that is not incapable of restoring you after your annihilation, just as you were living before annihilation.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of His words "formed and unformed" (mukhallaqa wa ghayr mukhallaqa). Some of them said: it is an attribute of the sperm-drop. He said: the meaning of that is: "We created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, formed and unformed." They said: as for the formed, it is what became a well-proportioned creation; and as for the unformed, it is what the wombs expelled of the drops and cast out before it became a creation.

Those who said that: Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Abu Mu'awiya related to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from ʿAmir, from ʿAlqama, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: When the sperm-drop falls into the womb, God sends an angel who says: "O Lord, formed or unformed?" If He says "unformed," the wombs expel it as blood; and if He says "formed," he says: "O Lord, what is the description of this sperm-drop: male or female? What is its provision, what is its term? Is it wretched or happy?" He said: It is said to him: "Go to the Mother of the Book and copy from it the description of this sperm-drop!" He said: the angel goes and copies it, and it does not leave him until he reaches the last of its description.

Others said: the meaning of that is: complete and incomplete.

Those who said that: Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Sulayman related to us, he said: Abu Hilal related to us, from Qatada, concerning God's words "formed and unformed," he said: complete and incomplete.

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Qatada, "formed and unformed," and he mentioned the same.

Others said: the meaning of that is: the lump of flesh, pictured as a human and not pictured; so when it is shaped, it is formed, and when it is not shaped, it is unformed.

Those who said that: Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam related to us, from ʿAnbasa, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, concerning His words "formed," he said: the miscarriage. "Formed and unformed."

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, he said: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's words "formed and unformed," he said: the miscarriage, created and uncreated.

* al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly.

* Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, he said: Dawud related to us, from ʿAmir, that he said concerning the sperm-drop and the lump of flesh, when they are reversed in the fourth creation, it is a formed soul; and if she expels it before that, it is unformed.

* He said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, from Hammad ibn Abi Salama, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu al-ʿAliya, concerning "formed and unformed," he said: the miscarriage.

The most correct of the sayings concerning this, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: "formed" means pictured in a complete creation, and "unformed" means the miscarriage before the completion of its creation. This is because "formed" and "unformed" are descriptions of the lump of flesh and the sperm-drop after it has become a lump of flesh; nothing remains for it, until it becomes a well-proportioned creation, except the shaping; and that is what is meant by His words "formed and unformed": formed into a well-proportioned creation, and unformed in that the mother casts it out as a lump of flesh without being shaped and without the spirit being breathed into it.

* *

As for His words "that We may make clear to you":

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We made of the lump of flesh a formed, complete one and a miscarried, incomplete one, that We may make clear to you Our power over what We will, and make you know Our originating of your creation.

* *

As for His words "And We settle in the wombs whatever We will for a specified term":

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: whomever We have written for survival and life until a term and an end, We settle him in his mother's womb until his appointed time, which We have set for him to remain in her womb; so she does not miscarry him, and he does not come out of her until he reaches his term. Then, when the time of his coming out of her womb arrives, We permit him to come out of it, and he comes out.

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said about that. Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, he said: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words "And We settle in the wombs whatever We will for a specified term," he said: the completion.

* al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words "And We settle in the wombs whatever We will for a specified term," he said: The specified term is its remaining in the womb until it comes out.

* *

As for His words "Then We bring you out as a child":

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Then We bring you out of your mothers' wombs when you reach the term We decreed for your coming out, as children, young ones. He used the singular "child" (tifl), though it describes all of them, because it is a verbal noun, like "adl and zawr.

* *

As for His words "Then [We let you reach] your maturity":

He says: then [We let you reach] the completion of your intellects and the culmination of your strength through your lifespan.

I have already mentioned the disagreement of those who differed concerning the ashudd, and the correct view of it according to us, with its evidences, in what has passed, in a way that makes its repetition in this place unnecessary.

"5"

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And among you is one who is taken in death, and among you is one who is returned to the most abject age, so that he knows nothing after knowing. And you see the earth lifeless; but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells and puts forth every lovely kind﴾.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And among you, O people, is one who dies before reaching his maturity, and among you is one who is granted a delayed term in his life and lives until he becomes decrepit, so he is returned, after the end of his youth and reaching the utmost of his maturity, to the most abject age, which is senility, until he returns to the state of his childhood, not understanding anything after his first understanding.

The meaning of the speech is: and among you is one returned to the most abject age after reaching his maturity, ﴿so that he knows nothing after knowing﴾ that he once knew, ﴿anything﴾.

* *

As for His words "And you see the earth lifeless":

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And you see the earth, O Muhammad, dry, its traces of plants and crops effaced. The root of "hamud" is effacement and obliteration, and it is said of it: the earth became lifeless (hamidat al-ard tahmud humudan); and from it is the saying of al-A'sha Maymun ibn Qays:

"Qutayla said: why is your body so wan, and I see your garments worn and decayed (hummadan)?" [[The verse belongs to A'sha ibn Qays ibn Tha'laba (his Diwan, Cairo edition with the commentary of Dr. Muhammad Husayn, p. 227). It is from a qasida he composed for Khosrow when he wanted hostages from them, when al-Harith ibn Wa'la raided some of the countryside. In it the narration reads "sa'iyan" in place of "shahiban." He said in its commentary: sa'i: one who makes whoever sees him feel bad. Hamada the garment: it tore from the length of folding; the observer looks at it and thinks it sound, but when he touches it, it crumbles from decay. Similarly in (Lisan al-Arab: hamada): "And you see the earth lifeless": that is, dry, having dust. A lifeless land: shrivelled, with no plant in it except the dry and broken, and drought has rendered it lifeless. End.]]

And "hummad" is the plural of "hamid," as "rukka" is the plural of "raki'."

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said about that. Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words "And you see the earth lifeless," he said: there is no plant in it.

* *

As for His words "But when We send down water upon it":

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: when We send down upon this lifeless earth, in which there is no plant, rain from the sky, it stirs, meaning: it moves with plants, "and swells," meaning: it increases the plants by the coming of the rain.

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said about that. Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, "it stirs and swells," he said: its swelling was recognized by the rain.

* al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, "it stirs and swells," he said: it became beautiful, and the rain was recognized in its swelling.

Some of them used to say: the meaning of that is: when We send down water upon it, it stirs, and the meaning is directed to the crop, although the speech is in the form of a report about the earth. The readers of the cities read "wa rabat" in the sense of rabw, which is growth and increase.

Abu Ja'far the reader used to read it "wa rabaʾat" with a hamza.

I was told from al-Farra', from Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Tamimi, from him, but that is an error, because there is no sense of "rabb" here; rather, "rabaʾa" with a hamza means to keep watch, from "al-rabiʾa" (lookout), and there is no sense of watching in this place. The sound reading is what the readers of the cities hold.

* *

As for His words "And it puts forth every lovely kind":

He, may His majesty be praised, says: And this lifeless earth put forth, by that rain, every kind of lovely thing, meaning by "bahij" the beauty, which is goodliness.

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said about that. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, "and it puts forth every lovely kind," he said: goodly.

* al-Hasan related to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, similarly.

The Interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and because He gives life to the dead, and because He is over all things Competent. (6) And because the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it, and because Allah will resurrect those who are in the graves.﴾ (7)

He, the Exalted, means by His words "That": this which I have mentioned to you, O people, of Our originating your creation in the wombs of your mothers, and Our describing your conditions before birth and after it, as a child, a middle-aged man, and a decrepit old man; and of Our drawing your attention to Our action upon the lifeless earth through what We send down upon it of rain. [This is] so that you may believe and affirm that the One who did that is Allah, who is the Truth without doubt, and that whatever else you worship of idols and images is false, because they are unable to do any of that. And so that you may know that the power by which He made these wondrous things is not beyond Him to use to give life to the dead after their perishing and their decay into dust, and that the One who does that is Able to do whatever He wills and desires, and nothing He wills is beyond Him. And so that you may be certain, by this, that the Hour which I promised you, in which I will raise the dead from their graves, is inevitably coming. ﴿There is no doubt in it﴾: he says, there is no doubt about its coming and its occurrence. ﴿And that Allah will resurrect those who are in the graves﴾: then those in them of the dead will be living, brought to the place of reckoning. So do not doubt that, nor dispute about it.

* *

The Interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And among the people is one who disputes concerning Allah without knowledge or guidance or an illuminating Book. (8)﴾

He, the Exalted, says: among the people is one who argues about the Oneness of Allah and His being singled out for divinity, without knowledge on his part of what he argues with. ﴿Nor guidance﴾: he says, without any clarification accompanying what he says, nor any proof. ﴿Nor an illuminating Book﴾: he says, without a Book from Allah that has come to him to establish the soundness of what he says. ﴿Illuminating﴾: he says, one that gives light concerning his proof. Rather, he says what he says out of ignorance, by conjecture and supposition. It is mentioned that this verse and the one after it were meant about al-Nadr ibn al-Harith of the Banu 'Abd al-Dar.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 9–10:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Turning aside in his arrogance, to lead astray from the way of God. For him, in this world, is disgrace, and We shall make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the Burning.﴾ (9) ﴿That is for what your hands have sent ahead, and because God is not in the least unjust to His servants.﴾ (10)

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: This one who disputes concerning God without knowledge is disputing ﴿turning aside in his arrogance [thāniya ʿiṭfihi]﴾.

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning for which he is described as "turning his side," and what is intended by describing him with it. Some of them said: He is described this way because of his pride and swaggering. It is related from the Arabs that they say: "So-and-so came to me thāniya ʿiṭfihi," meaning he came strutting out of arrogance.

Those who said this: Ali related to me, he said: Abdullah related to us, he said: Muawiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿thāniya ʿiṭfihi﴾: he says, "Arrogant within himself."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: twisting his neck.

Those who said this: Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿thāniya ʿiṭfihi﴾, he said: "His neck."

Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.

Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mamar, from Qatada, ﴿thāniya ʿiṭfihi﴾, he said: "Twisting his neck."

Al-Hasan related to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Mamar, from Qatada, the same.

Others said: The meaning of that is that he turns away from what he is called to, so he does not listen to it.

Those who said this: Muhammad ibn Saad related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿thāniya ʿiṭfihi﴾, he says: "He turns away from My remembrance."

Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿thāniya ʿiṭfihi li-yuḍilla ʿan sabīl Allāh﴾: "Twisting his head, turning away, showing his back, not wishing to hear what is said to him." And he recited: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of God will ask forgiveness for you," they twist their heads, and you see them turning away while they are arrogant. … And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly.﴾

Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿thāniya ʿiṭfihi﴾, he said: "He turns away from the truth."

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: These three sayings are close in meaning, because whoever is arrogant, it is his nature to turn away from what he is arrogant toward, to twist his neck away from it, and to turn aside.

The correct view on this matter is to say: God described this disputant concerning God without knowledge as follows: because of his arrogance, when he is called to God, he turns away from the one calling him, twists his neck away from him, and does not listen to what is said to him, out of arrogance.

* *

As for His saying ﴿li-yuḍilla ʿan sabīl Allāh﴾ (to lead astray from the way of God):

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: This polytheist disputes concerning God without knowledge, turning away from the truth out of arrogance, in order to hinder the believers in God from their religion which He has guided them to, and to make them slip away from it. ﴿For him, in this world, is disgrace﴾: May His praise be exalted, He says: For this disputant concerning God without knowledge, in this world is disgrace, which is killing, humiliation and abasement at the hands of the believers; so God killed him at their hands on the day of Badr.

As related:

Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying ﴿in this world, disgrace﴾: he said: "Killed on the day of Badr."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and We shall make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the Burning﴾:

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We will burn him with the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

As for His saying ﴿That is for what your hands have sent ahead﴾:

May His praise be exalted, He says: It will be said to him when he is made to taste the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection: "This is the punishment We make you taste today for what your hands sent ahead in the world of sins and transgressions, and for the criminality you earned therein," ﴿and that God is not in the least unjust to the servants﴾. He says: We did that because God is not unjust to His servants, so as to punish some of His servants for a crime while forgiving the like of it from another, or to lay the sin of a sinner upon one who is not a sinner and punish him for it while pardoning the owner of the sin. Rather, He punishes no one except for his own crime, and He does not punish anyone for a sin whose like He forgives in another, except by a cause that has earned His forgiveness.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 11:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge. If good befalls him, he is reassured by it; but if an ordeal befalls him, he turns back on his face. He has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the clear loss.﴾ (11)

By His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge﴾, He means Bedouin Arabs who used to come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as emigrants from their desert dwellings. If they attained ease of livelihood after the emigration and entry into Islam, they remained upon Islam; otherwise they turned back on their heels. So Allah said, ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah﴾ in doubt, ﴿If good befalls him, he is reassured by it﴾, and it is abundance of livelihood and what resembles it of the worldly causes; he is reassured by it, meaning he settles into Islam and remains steadfast upon it. ﴿But if an ordeal befalls him﴾, and it is hardship of livelihood and what resembles it of the worldly causes, ﴿he turns back on his face﴾, meaning he apostatizes and turns back on his face, which was upon disbelief in Allah.

And those of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that: Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge﴾ ... to His saying ﴿he turns back on his face﴾, he said: "The ordeal is trial. One of them would come to Medina, which was a land of fever. If his body was healthy there, and his mare foaled a fine colt, and his wife bore a boy, he was pleased with it and reassured by it and said: 'I have not encountered anything since I was upon this religion of mine except good.' But if the fever of Medina afflicted him, his wife bore a girl, and the charity was delayed from him, Satan came to him and said: 'By Allah, I have not encountered anything since you were upon this religion of yours except evil.' And that is the ordeal."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, saying: 'Anbasa related to us, from Abu Bakr, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge﴾, he said: "On doubt."

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿on an edge﴾, he said: "On doubt. ﴿If good befalls him﴾: ease and well-being ﴿he is reassured by it﴾, he settles. ﴿And if an ordeal befalls him﴾: punishment and calamity ﴿he turns back﴾: he apostatizes ﴿on his face﴾: a disbeliever."

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

Ibn Jurayj said: "There were people from the tribes of the Arabs and from those around them, from the people of the villages, who would say: 'We will come to Muhammad ﷺ; if we find good in livelihood and sustenance, we will remain with him, and otherwise we will rejoin our families.'"

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, ﴿worships Allah on an edge﴾, he said: "Doubt. ﴿If good befalls him﴾: he says, his wealth increases and his livestock multiply, so he is reassured and says: 'Since I entered this religion of mine, nothing but good has befallen me.' ﴿But if an ordeal befalls him﴾: he says, if his wealth is lost and his livestock perish, ﴿he turns back on his face; he has lost this world and the Hereafter.﴾"

⁕ al-Hasan related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, similarly.

⁕ It was related from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge﴾, the verse: "There were people from the tribes of the Arabs and from those around Medina from the villages who would say: 'We will come to Muhammad ﷺ and consider his affair; if we find good, we will remain with him, and otherwise we will rejoin our dwellings and families.' They would come to him and say: 'We are upon your religion!' If they attained livelihood and their mares foaled and their women bore boys, they were reassured and said: 'This is a true religion.' But if provision was delayed from them, their mares slipped, and their women bore girls, they said: 'This is an evil religion,' and they turned back on their faces."

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge; if good befalls him, he is reassured by it, and if an ordeal befalls him, he turns back on his face; he has lost this world and the Hereafter﴾: "This is the hypocrite. If his worldly affairs are sound, he remains in worship, and if his worldly affairs are corrupted and altered, he turns back, and he does not remain in worship except for what is sound of his worldly affairs. And if hardship, or trial, or testing, or constraint befalls him, he abandons his religion and returns to disbelief."

* *

And His saying ﴿He has lost this world and the Hereafter﴾

He means: this one whom He, may His praise be exalted, has described has been defrauded of his world, because he did not attain his need from it by means of his worship of Allah upon doubt, and he invested in a trade and did not profit. "And the Hereafter": he means, and he has lost the Hereafter, for he is punished therein with the kindled Fire of Allah.

* *

And His saying ﴿That is the clear loss﴾

He means: his loss of this world and the Hereafter is the loss; that is, the clear destruction: he means it becomes clear to whoever reflects and ponders on it that he has lost this world and the Hereafter.

The readers differed in reading this. The readers of the major cities all read ﴿خَسِرَ الدُّنْيَا وَالآخِرَةَ﴾ in the past tense, except Humayd al-A'raj, who read ﴿خاسِرًا﴾ in the accusative as a circumstantial state, on the pattern of the active participle (fa'il).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 12:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He calls, instead of Allah, upon that which does not harm him and does not benefit him. That is the far-reaching error.﴾

His saying, exalted is He, means: And if that one who worships Allah on an edge (harf) of trial afflicts him, he apostatizes from the religion of Allah, calling instead of Allah upon gods that do not harm him if he does not worship them in this world, and do not benefit him in the Hereafter if he worships them. ﴿That is the far-reaching error﴾ means: his apostasy, calling upon these gods instead of Allah, is taking a path that is not upright, and departing from the religion of Allah into a far-off departure.

⁕ Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying, ﴿He calls, instead of Allah, upon that which does not harm him and does not benefit him﴾: he disbelieves after his faith. ﴿That is the far-reaching error.﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 13:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He calls upon one whose harm is nearer than his benefit. Wretched is the protector, and wretched is the companion.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: this one who turned on his face (al-munqalib 'ala wajhihu) when a trial befell him calls upon gods whose harm to him in the Hereafter is nearer and swifter to him than their benefit.
