Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The disbelievers have garments of fire cut out for them, and the believer enters gardens beneath which rivers flow."

* *

And His words: ﴿and boiling water will be poured over their heads﴾

He says: boiling water will be poured over their heads.

As related:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taliqani narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Saʿid ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Samh, from Ibn Juhayrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, the boiling water is poured upon their heads, and it pierces the skull until it reaches their insides, and it melts what is in their insides until it reaches their feet, and that is the ṣahr (melting). Then they are restored as they were."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Yaʿmar ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Saʿid ibn Zayd informed us, from Abu al-Samh, from Ibn Juhayrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with the like of it, except that he said: "It pierces the skull until it reaches their insides, and it melts [[yaslat fi jawfih min bab nasara: i.e., it cuts through and uproots it.]] what is in their insides."

Some of them claimed that His words ﴿and for them are hooks of iron﴾ are among the postponed (muʾakhkhar) elements whose meaning is anticipated (muqaddam). They said: The construction of the statement is: "As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire have been cut out for them, and for them are hooks of iron. Boiling water will be poured over their heads." They said: It must be so, because the angel strikes him with an iron hook until it pierces his head, then boiling water whose heat has become intense is poured into it, cutting through his belly. The report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that we mentioned indicates the opposite of what this speaker said, because he (ﷺ) informed that when boiling water is poured over their heads, it pierces the skull until it reaches their insides. This is also what the interpreters' explanation came with. If the hooks had pierced their heads before the boiling water was poured on them, the words of the Prophet (ﷺ), "Indeed the boiling water pierces the skull," would have no meaning. Rather, the matter is contrary to what this speaker said.

* *

And His words: ﴿With it, what is in their bellies and their skins will be melted﴾

He says: With the boiling water that is poured over their heads, what is in their bellies of fats is melted, and their skins are roasted by it and fall off. Ṣahr means melting. It is said of it: "I melted the fat with fire" when I melt it, I ṣahr it, ṣahran. From it is the poet's saying:

*You bring water to a stone [lāqī] cast upon a bare plain,
The sun melts it, yet it does not melt.* [[The verse is by Ibn Ahmar describing a sandgrouse chick (Lisan: ṣ-h-r). He said: "The sun ṣahrahu ṣahran" and "ṣahrahu": its heat strikes it intensely and pains its brain, and "inṣahara" is he. Ibn Ahmar describes a sandgrouse chick... the verse; i.e., the sun melts it, so it endures that. "Tarwi" means it brings water to it, as if it were a water-carrier for it; one says: "I gave my family water and they got water": I brought them water. Ṣahr: melting of fat; "ṣahara al-shahm yaṣhuruhu ṣahran": he melted it. In the revelation: "With it, what is in their bellies and their skins will be melted," i.e., melted. "Iṣṭahrahu": he melted it and ate it. "Laqī": everything cast aside and abandoned, like a lost item. "Ṣafṣaf": a smooth, level land, as in Lisan.]]

And from it is the saying of the rajaz poet:

*He melted the entrails, the roasted, the melted [mustaṣhar]* [[The verse is by al-Ajjaj ibn Ru'bah, the well-known rajaz poet (Lisan: ṣ-h-r). Al-Azhari said: al-ṣahr is melting fat, and al-ṣahārah is what melts of it; likewise al-iṣṭihār is melting, or eating its ṣahārah. Al-Ajjaj said: "He melted the entrails..." The verse is evidence, like the preceding, that ṣahr means melting.]]

And according to what we have said regarding that, the interpreters have spoken.

As related:

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿With it will be melted﴾, he said: "It is melted, a melting."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it. Ibn Jurayj said regarding ﴿With it will be melted﴾: "What was cut out for them of punishment."

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: ﴿With it, what is in their bellies will be melted﴾, he said: "With it is melted what is in their bellies."

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 18–22 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his statement: ﴿Those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them﴾ ... up to his statement: ﴿Whereby what is in their bellies will be melted, and the skins﴾. He said: They will be given to drink [something] which, when it enters their bellies, melts them, and the skins along with the bellies.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far and Harun ibn 'Antara, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Harun said: "When the people of the Fire become hungry," and Ja'far said: "When the people of the Fire become hungry, they will call for help to the tree of al-Zaqqum, and they will eat from it, and the skins of their faces will be stripped off. So if a passerby were to pass by them, he would recognize them by the skin of their faces in it. Then thirst will overcome them, and they will call for help, and they will be given relief with water like molten brass (al-muhl), which is water whose heat has reached its extreme. When they bring it near their mouths, the flesh of their faces, from which the skins have fallen, will be roasted by its heat. And ﴿whereby what is in their bellies will be melted﴾, meaning their intestines, and their skins will fall off. Then they will be struck with maces of iron, and every limb will fall into its place, and they will call out for destruction and perdition."

* *

As for His statement: ﴿And for them are maces of iron﴾:
The guardians of the Fire will strike their heads with them whenever they try to exit the Fire, until they return them into it.

* *

As for His statement: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, out of distress, they will be returned into it﴾:
He means: whenever these disbelievers, whose attributes Allah has described, wish to exit the Fire because of the distress and anguish that have befallen them, they will be returned to it.

As related by:
⁕ Mujahid ibn Musa related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn 'Awn related to us, saying: al-A'mash informed us, from Abu Zabyan, who said: "The Fire is black and dark; its flame does not give light, nor do its embers." Then he recited: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, out of distress, they will be returned into it﴾. It has been mentioned that they try to escape the Fire when Hell surges and throws those within it up to its highest gates; they wish to get out, but the guardians return them into it with maces, and when they strike them with the maces, they say to them: ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning﴾. By His statement ﴿And taste the punishment of the burning﴾ it is meant: it is said to them, "Taste the punishment of the Fire." It was also said "the punishment of the burning," and the meaning is "the burning [punishment]," just as it is said "the painful punishment," meaning "the painful [punishment]."

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Do you not see that to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the creatures, and many of mankind? But many deserve the punishment.﴾**

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ):

Have you not seen, O Muhammad, with your heart, so that you know that God is prostrated to by whoever is in the heavens, from among the angels, and whoever is on the earth, from among creation, from among the jinn and others, and the sun, the moon, and the stars in the sky, and the mountains, and the trees, and the creatures on the earth? The prostration of these is their shadows, when the sun rises upon them and when it declines. Whenever the shadow of anything shifts, that is its prostration.

As related:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Do you not see that to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the creatures﴾, he said: "These are all shadows."

As for the prostration of the sun, the moon and the stars, it is as follows.

As related:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy and Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, the two of them saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu al-ʿAliyah al-Riyahi say: "There is no star in the sky, nor sun, nor moon, but it falls prostrate before God when it sets. Then it does not move until it is permitted, and it takes its course to the right." Muhammad added: "until it returns to its place of rising."

* *

And His words: ﴿and many of mankind﴾

He says: many of the children of Adam prostrate, and they are the believers in God.

As related:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿and many of mankind﴾, he said: "The believers."

* *

And His words: ﴿but many deserve the punishment﴾

He, the Exalted, says: many of the children of Adam deserve the punishment of God, and it is incumbent upon them because of their disbelief in Him, yet even so their shadows prostrate to God.

As related:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿but many deserve the punishment﴾, and "they prostrate along with their shadows." Thus, according to this interpretation that we have mentioned from Mujahid, the words ﴿but many deserve the punishment﴾ are coordinated with His words ﴿and many of mankind﴾, and it is included among those whom God described as prostrating to Him, and His words ﴿deserve the punishment﴾ are a complement of "many." If the second "many" referred to those not included among those described as prostrating, it would be in the nominative case governed by the pronoun referring back to it in His words ﴿deserve the punishment﴾, and the meaning of the statement would then be: "and many refused prostration," because His words ﴿deserve the punishment﴾ indicate disobedience to God and refusal to prostrate, for which they deserved punishment.

18

* *

Regarding the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Whomever God humiliates, there is none to honor him. Indeed God does what He wills﴾ (17)

He, the Exalted, says: Whomever God humiliates among His creation, and so makes him wretched, ﴿there is none to honor him﴾ with happiness, by which He makes him happy, because all affairs are in the hand of God. He grants success to whom He wills in obedience to Him, forsakes whom He wills, makes wretched whom He intends, and makes happy whom He loves.

* *

And His words: ﴿Indeed God does what He wills﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed God does what He wills among His creation, humiliating whom He wills to humiliate and honoring whom He wills to honor, because the creation is His creation and the command is His command. ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾. It has been reported that some of them recited it as ﴿فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ مُكْرَمٍ﴾ (fa-ma lahu min mukramin, with the fatha on the mim of mukram), meaning: "there is none to give him honor." But that is a recitation I do not consider permissible, because of the consensus (ijma') of the authorities among the reciters against it.

* *

Regarding the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord. As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them, and boiling water will be poured over their heads. With it, what is in their bellies and their skins will be melted. And for them are hooks of iron. Every time they wish to get out of it from distress, they will be returned into it, and [they will be told], "Taste the punishment of the burning."﴾ (19–22)

The interpreters have differed concerning who is meant by these two adversaries whom God mentioned. Some of them said: one of the two groups is the people of faith, and the other group is the worshippers of idols, from among the polytheists of Quraysh who dueled on the Day of Badr.

Those who said this:

Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Hashim informed us, from Abu Mijlaz, from Qays ibn ʿUbad, who said: I heard Abu Dharr swear an oath that this verse ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾ was revealed concerning those who dueled on the Day of Badr: Hamzah, ʿAli, ʿUbaydah ibn al-Harith, ʿUtbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabiʿah, and al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah. He said: ʿAli said: "I am the first, or among the first, who will kneel in dispute before God, blessed and exalted, on the Day of Resurrection."

ʿAli ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Muʾammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Hashim, from Abu Mijlaz, from Qays ibn ʿUbad, who said: I heard Abu Dharr swear by God: "This verse was revealed concerning six men from Quraysh: Hamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, ʿUbaydah ibn al-Harith, may God be pleased with them, ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabiʿah, and al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾ ... to the end of the verse ﴿Indeed, God admits those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾ ... to the end of the verse."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Hashim, from Abu Mijlaz, from Qays ibn ʿUbad, who said: I heard Abu Dharr swear, then he mentioned something similar.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mahbub narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur ibn al-Mutamir, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, who said: "This verse was revealed concerning those who dueled on the Day of Badr: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from some of his companions, from ʿAta' ibn Yasar, who said: "These verses were revealed: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾ concerning those who dueled on the Day of Badr: Hamzah, ʿAli, ʿUbaydah ibn al-Harith, ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabiʿah, and al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah," up to His words ﴿and they were guided to the path of the Praiseworthy﴾.

He said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Hashim, from Abu Mujallaz, from Qays ibn ʿUbad, who said: "By God, this verse was revealed: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾ concerning those who went out against one another on the Day of Badr: Hamzah, ʿAli, ʿUbaydah, may God have mercy on them, Shaybah, ʿUtbah, and al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah."

Others said, among those who said one of the two groups is the faction of faith: "Rather, the other group is the People of the Book."

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾, he said: "They are the People of the Book. They said to the believers: 'We are more entitled to God and earlier in scripture than you, and our prophet came before your prophet.' The believers said: 'We are more entitled to God. We believed in Muhammad (ﷺ), and we believed in your prophet and in what God revealed of scripture. You know our scripture and our prophet, then you abandoned them and disbelieved in them out of envy.' That was their dispute concerning their Lord."

Others said: "Rather, the other group is all the disbelievers, of whatever religion they were."

Those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir, from Mujahid, and ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah, and Abu Qazaʿah, from al-Husayn, who said: "They are the disbelievers and the believers, who disputed concerning their Lord."

He narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "Like the disbeliever and the believer." Ibn Jurayj said: "Their dispute concerning which they disputed about their Lord is their dispute in this world, of the people of every religion, who see themselves as more entitled to God than others."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash narrated to us, saying: "ʿAsim and al-Kalbi both used to say concerning ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾: 'The people of polytheism and Islam, when they disputed as to which of them was better.' He said: 'Polytheism made it a religion.'"

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾, he said: "Like the believer and the disbeliever, their dispute concerning the Resurrection."

Others said: "The two adversaries whom God mentioned in this verse are Paradise and Hell."

Those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir, from ʿIkrimah, regarding ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾, he said: "They are Paradise and Hell, who disputed. Hell said: 'God created me for His punishment.' Paradise said: 'God created me for His mercy.' God has related to you of their story what you hear."

The most correct of these opinions in my view, and the most fitting to the interpretation of the verse, is the view of the one who said: "By the two adversaries is meant all the disbelievers of whatever categories of disbelief they were, and all the believers." I only said this is more correct because He, the Exalted, mentioned before this two categories of His creation: one of them, the people who obey Him by prostrating to Him, and the other, the people who disobey Him, upon whom punishment is due. He said: ﴿Do you not see that to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon﴾, then He said: ﴿and many of mankind, but many deserve the punishment﴾. Then He followed that with a description of both categories and what He will do to them, saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them﴾, and God said: ﴿Indeed, God admits those who believed and did righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. Thus it was clear by this that what lies between them is news about the two of them.

If someone says: "What do you say about what was related from Abu Dharr, that it was revealed concerning those who dueled on the Day of Badr?" It is said: "That is, God willing, as it was related from him. But a verse may be revealed due to a cause among the causes, and then be general in everything similar to that cause. This is one of those. The ones who dueled were, one of the two groups, the people of polytheism and disbelief in God, and the other the people of faith in God and obedience to Him. So every disbeliever, in the category of the polytheist group, is an adversary to the people of faith. Likewise, every believer, in the category of the faith group, is an adversary to the people of polytheism."

Thus the meaning of the statement is: "These two adversaries dispute concerning the religion of their Lord, and their dispute in that is each group's enmity toward the other and its fighting against it over its religion."

* *

And His words: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them﴾

He, the Exalted, says: As for the disbeliever in God among them, garments of fire will be cut out for him, a shirt of brass of fire.

As related:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them﴾, he said: "The disbeliever has garments of fire cut out for him, while the believer, God admits him into gardens beneath which rivers flow."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqub narrated to us, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid, regarding His words: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them﴾, he said: "Garments of brass, and nothing among vessels is hotter or more intense in heat than it."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The disbelievers have garments of fire cut out for them, and the believer enters gardens beneath which rivers flow."

* *

And His words: ﴿and boiling water will be poured over their heads﴾

He says: boiling water will be poured over their heads.

As related:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taliqani narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Saʿid ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Samh, from Ibn Juhayrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, the boiling water is poured upon their heads, and it pierces the skull until it reaches their insides, and it melts what is in their insides until it reaches their feet, and that is the ṣahr (melting). Then they are restored as they were."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Yaʿmar ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Saʿid ibn Zayd informed us, from Abu al-Samh, from Ibn Juhayrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with the like of it, except that he said: "It pierces the skull until it reaches their insides, and it melts [[yaslat fi jawfih min bab nasara: i.e., it cuts through and uproots it.]] what is in their insides."

Some of them claimed that His words ﴿and for them are hooks of iron﴾ are among the postponed (muʾakhkhar) elements whose meaning is anticipated (muqaddam). They said: The construction of the statement is: "As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire have been cut out for them, and for them are hooks of iron. Boiling water will be poured over their heads." They said: It must be so, because the angel strikes him with an iron hook until it pierces his head, then boiling water whose heat has become intense is poured into it, cutting through his belly. The report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that we mentioned indicates the opposite of what this speaker said, because he (ﷺ) informed that when boiling water is poured over their heads, it pierces the skull until it reaches their insides. This is also what the interpreters' explanation came with. If the hooks had pierced their heads before the boiling water was poured on them, the words of the Prophet (ﷺ), "Indeed the boiling water pierces the skull," would have no meaning. Rather, the matter is contrary to what this speaker said.

* *

And His words: ﴿With it, what is in their bellies and their skins will be melted﴾

He says: With the boiling water that is poured over their heads, what is in their bellies of fats is melted, and their skins are roasted by it and fall off. Ṣahr means melting. It is said of it: "I melted the fat with fire" when I melt it, I ṣahr it, ṣahran. From it is the poet's saying:

*You bring water to a stone [lāqī] cast upon a bare plain,
The sun melts it, yet it does not melt.* [[The verse is by Ibn Ahmar describing a sandgrouse chick (Lisan: ṣ-h-r). He said: "The sun ṣahrahu ṣahran" and "ṣahrahu": its heat strikes it intensely and pains its brain, and "inṣahara" is he. Ibn Ahmar describes a sandgrouse chick... the verse; i.e., the sun melts it, so it endures that. "Tarwi" means it brings water to it, as if it were a water-carrier for it; one says: "I gave my family water and they got water": I brought them water. Ṣahr: melting of fat; "ṣahara al-shahm yaṣhuruhu ṣahran": he melted it. In the revelation: "With it, what is in their bellies and their skins will be melted," i.e., melted. "Iṣṭahrahu": he melted it and ate it. "Laqī": everything cast aside and abandoned, like a lost item. "Ṣafṣaf": a smooth, level land, as in Lisan.]]

And from it is the saying of the rajaz poet:

*He melted the entrails, the roasted, the melted [mustaṣhar]* [[The verse is by al-Ajjaj ibn Ru'bah, the well-known rajaz poet (Lisan: ṣ-h-r). Al-Azhari said: al-ṣahr is melting fat, and al-ṣahārah is what melts of it; likewise al-iṣṭihār is melting, or eating its ṣahārah. Al-Ajjaj said: "He melted the entrails..." The verse is evidence, like the preceding, that ṣahr means melting.]]

And according to what we have said regarding that, the interpreters have spoken.

As related:

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿With it will be melted﴾, he said: "It is melted, a melting."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it. Ibn Jurayj said regarding ﴿With it will be melted﴾: "What was cut out for them of punishment."

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: ﴿With it, what is in their bellies will be melted﴾, he said: "With it is melted what is in their bellies."

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 18–22 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his statement: ﴿Those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them﴾ ... up to his statement: ﴿Whereby what is in their bellies will be melted, and the skins﴾. He said: They will be given to drink [something] which, when it enters their bellies, melts them, and the skins along with the bellies.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far and Harun ibn 'Antara, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Harun said: "When the people of the Fire become hungry," and Ja'far said: "When the people of the Fire become hungry, they will call for help to the tree of al-Zaqqum, and they will eat from it, and the skins of their faces will be stripped off. So if a passerby were to pass by them, he would recognize them by the skin of their faces in it. Then thirst will overcome them, and they will call for help, and they will be given relief with water like molten brass (al-muhl), which is water whose heat has reached its extreme. When they bring it near their mouths, the flesh of their faces, from which the skins have fallen, will be roasted by its heat. And ﴿whereby what is in their bellies will be melted﴾, meaning their intestines, and their skins will fall off. Then they will be struck with maces of iron, and every limb will fall into its place, and they will call out for destruction and perdition."

* *

As for His statement: ﴿And for them are maces of iron﴾:
The guardians of the Fire will strike their heads with them whenever they try to exit the Fire, until they return them into it.

* *

As for His statement: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, out of distress, they will be returned into it﴾:
He means: whenever these disbelievers, whose attributes Allah has described, wish to exit the Fire because of the distress and anguish that have befallen them, they will be returned to it.

As related by:
⁕ Mujahid ibn Musa related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn 'Awn related to us, saying: al-A'mash informed us, from Abu Zabyan, who said: "The Fire is black and dark; its flame does not give light, nor do its embers." Then he recited: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, out of distress, they will be returned into it﴾. It has been mentioned that they try to escape the Fire when Hell surges and throws those within it up to its highest gates; they wish to get out, but the guardians return them into it with maces, and when they strike them with the maces, they say to them: ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning﴾. By His statement ﴿And taste the punishment of the burning﴾ it is meant: it is said to them, "Taste the punishment of the Fire." It was also said "the punishment of the burning," and the meaning is "the burning [punishment]," just as it is said "the painful punishment," meaning "the painful [punishment]."

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Do you not see that to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the creatures, and many of mankind? But many deserve the punishment.﴾**

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ):

Have you not seen, O Muhammad, with your heart, so that you know that God is prostrated to by whoever is in the heavens, from among the angels, and whoever is on the earth, from among creation, from among the jinn and others, and the sun, the moon, and the stars in the sky, and the mountains, and the trees, and the creatures on the earth? The prostration of these is their shadows, when the sun rises upon them and when it declines. Whenever the shadow of anything shifts, that is its prostration.

As related:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Do you not see that to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the creatures﴾, he said: "These are all shadows."

As for the prostration of the sun, the moon and the stars, it is as follows.

As related:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy and Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, the two of them saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu al-ʿAliyah al-Riyahi say: "There is no star in the sky, nor sun, nor moon, but it falls prostrate before God when it sets. Then it does not move until it is permitted, and it takes its course to the right." Muhammad added: "until it returns to its place of rising."

* *

And His words: ﴿and many of mankind﴾

He says: many of the children of Adam prostrate, and they are the believers in God.

As related:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿and many of mankind﴾, he said: "The believers."

* *

And His words: ﴿but many deserve the punishment﴾

He, the Exalted, says: many of the children of Adam deserve the punishment of God, and it is incumbent upon them because of their disbelief in Him, yet even so their shadows prostrate to God.

As related:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿but many deserve the punishment﴾, and "they prostrate along with their shadows." Thus, according to this interpretation that we have mentioned from Mujahid, the words ﴿but many deserve the punishment﴾ are coordinated with His words ﴿and many of mankind﴾, and it is included among those whom God described as prostrating to Him, and His words ﴿deserve the punishment﴾ are a complement of "many." If the second "many" referred to those not included among those described as prostrating, it would be in the nominative case governed by the pronoun referring back to it in His words ﴿deserve the punishment﴾, and the meaning of the statement would then be: "and many refused prostration," because His words ﴿deserve the punishment﴾ indicate disobedience to God and refusal to prostrate, for which they deserved punishment.

18

* *

Regarding the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Whomever God humiliates, there is none to honor him. Indeed God does what He wills﴾ (17)

He, the Exalted, says: Whomever God humiliates among His creation, and so makes him wretched, ﴿there is none to honor him﴾ with happiness, by which He makes him happy, because all affairs are in the hand of God. He grants success to whom He wills in obedience to Him, forsakes whom He wills, makes wretched whom He intends, and makes happy whom He loves.

* *

And His words: ﴿Indeed God does what He wills﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed God does what He wills among His creation, humiliating whom He wills to humiliate and honoring whom He wills to honor, because the creation is His creation and the command is His command. ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾. It has been reported that some of them recited it as ﴿فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ مُكْرَمٍ﴾ (fa-ma lahu min mukramin, with the fatha on the mim of mukram), meaning: "there is none to give him honor." But that is a recitation I do not consider permissible, because of the consensus (ijma') of the authorities among the reciters against it.

* *

Regarding the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord. As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them, and boiling water will be poured over their heads. With it, what is in their bellies and their skins will be melted. And for them are hooks of iron. Every time they wish to get out of it from distress, they will be returned into it, and [they will be told], "Taste the punishment of the burning."﴾ (19–22)

The interpreters have differed concerning who is meant by these two adversaries whom God mentioned. Some of them said: one of the two groups is the people of faith, and the other group is the worshippers of idols, from among the polytheists of Quraysh who dueled on the Day of Badr.

Those who said this:

Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Hashim informed us, from Abu Mijlaz, from Qays ibn ʿUbad, who said: I heard Abu Dharr swear an oath that this verse ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾ was revealed concerning those who dueled on the Day of Badr: Hamzah, ʿAli, ʿUbaydah ibn al-Harith, ʿUtbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabiʿah, and al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah. He said: ʿAli said: "I am the first, or among the first, who will kneel in dispute before God, blessed and exalted, on the Day of Resurrection."

ʿAli ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Muʾammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Hashim, from Abu Mijlaz, from Qays ibn ʿUbad, who said: I heard Abu Dharr swear by God: "This verse was revealed concerning six men from Quraysh: Hamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, ʿUbaydah ibn al-Harith, may God be pleased with them, ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabiʿah, and al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾ ... to the end of the verse ﴿Indeed, God admits those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾ ... to the end of the verse."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Hashim, from Abu Mijlaz, from Qays ibn ʿUbad, who said: I heard Abu Dharr swear, then he mentioned something similar.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mahbub narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur ibn al-Mutamir, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, who said: "This verse was revealed concerning those who dueled on the Day of Badr: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from some of his companions, from ʿAta' ibn Yasar, who said: "These verses were revealed: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾ concerning those who dueled on the Day of Badr: Hamzah, ʿAli, ʿUbaydah ibn al-Harith, ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabiʿah, and al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah," up to His words ﴿and they were guided to the path of the Praiseworthy﴾.

He said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Hashim, from Abu Mujallaz, from Qays ibn ʿUbad, who said: "By God, this verse was revealed: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾ concerning those who went out against one another on the Day of Badr: Hamzah, ʿAli, ʿUbaydah, may God have mercy on them, Shaybah, ʿUtbah, and al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah."

Others said, among those who said one of the two groups is the faction of faith: "Rather, the other group is the People of the Book."

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾, he said: "They are the People of the Book. They said to the believers: 'We are more entitled to God and earlier in scripture than you, and our prophet came before your prophet.' The believers said: 'We are more entitled to God. We believed in Muhammad (ﷺ), and we believed in your prophet and in what God revealed of scripture. You know our scripture and our prophet, then you abandoned them and disbelieved in them out of envy.' That was their dispute concerning their Lord."

Others said: "Rather, the other group is all the disbelievers, of whatever religion they were."

Those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir, from Mujahid, and ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah, and Abu Qazaʿah, from al-Husayn, who said: "They are the disbelievers and the believers, who disputed concerning their Lord."

He narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "Like the disbeliever and the believer." Ibn Jurayj said: "Their dispute concerning which they disputed about their Lord is their dispute in this world, of the people of every religion, who see themselves as more entitled to God than others."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash narrated to us, saying: "ʿAsim and al-Kalbi both used to say concerning ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾: 'The people of polytheism and Islam, when they disputed as to which of them was better.' He said: 'Polytheism made it a religion.'"

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾, he said: "Like the believer and the disbeliever, their dispute concerning the Resurrection."

Others said: "The two adversaries whom God mentioned in this verse are Paradise and Hell."

Those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir, from ʿIkrimah, regarding ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾, he said: "They are Paradise and Hell, who disputed. Hell said: 'God created me for His punishment.' Paradise said: 'God created me for His mercy.' God has related to you of their story what you hear."

The most correct of these opinions in my view, and the most fitting to the interpretation of the verse, is the view of the one who said: "By the two adversaries is meant all the disbelievers of whatever categories of disbelief they were, and all the believers." I only said this is more correct because He, the Exalted, mentioned before this two categories of His creation: one of them, the people who obey Him by prostrating to Him, and the other, the people who disobey Him, upon whom punishment is due. He said: ﴿Do you not see that to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon﴾, then He said: ﴿and many of mankind, but many deserve the punishment﴾. Then He followed that with a description of both categories and what He will do to them, saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them﴾, and God said: ﴿Indeed, God admits those who believed and did righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. Thus it was clear by this that what lies between them is news about the two of them.

If someone says: "What do you say about what was related from Abu Dharr, that it was revealed concerning those who dueled on the Day of Badr?" It is said: "That is, God willing, as it was related from him. But a verse may be revealed due to a cause among the causes, and then be general in everything similar to that cause. This is one of those. The ones who dueled were, one of the two groups, the people of polytheism and disbelief in God, and the other the people of faith in God and obedience to Him. So every disbeliever, in the category of the polytheist group, is an adversary to the people of faith. Likewise, every believer, in the category of the faith group, is an adversary to the people of polytheism."

Thus the meaning of the statement is: "These two adversaries dispute concerning the religion of their Lord, and their dispute in that is each group's enmity toward the other and its fighting against it over its religion."

* *

And His words: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them﴾

He, the Exalted, says: As for the disbeliever in God among them, garments of fire will be cut out for him, a shirt of brass of fire.

As related:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them﴾, he said: "The disbeliever has garments of fire cut out for him, while the believer, God admits him into gardens beneath which rivers flow."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqub narrated to us, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid, regarding His words: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them﴾, he said: "Garments of brass, and nothing among vessels is hotter or more intense in heat than it."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The disbelievers have garments of fire cut out for them, and the believer enters gardens beneath which rivers flow."

* *

And His words: ﴿and boiling water will be poured over their heads﴾

He says: boiling water will be poured over their heads.

As related:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taliqani narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Saʿid ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Samh, from Ibn Juhayrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, the boiling water is poured upon their heads, and it pierces the skull until it reaches their insides, and it melts what is in their insides until it reaches their feet, and that is the ṣahr (melting). Then they are restored as they were."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Yaʿmar ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Saʿid ibn Zayd informed us, from Abu al-Samh, from Ibn Juhayrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with the like of it, except that he said: "It pierces the skull until it reaches their insides, and it melts [[yaslat fi jawfih min bab nasara: i.e., it cuts through and uproots it.]] what is in their insides."

Some of them claimed that His words ﴿and for them are hooks of iron﴾ are among the postponed (muʾakhkhar) elements whose meaning is anticipated (muqaddam). They said: The construction of the statement is: "As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire have been cut out for them, and for them are hooks of iron. Boiling water will be poured over their heads." They said: It must be so, because the angel strikes him with an iron hook until it pierces his head, then boiling water whose heat has become intense is poured into it, cutting through his belly. The report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that we mentioned indicates the opposite of what this speaker said, because he (ﷺ) informed that when boiling water is poured over their heads, it pierces the skull until it reaches their insides. This is also what the interpreters' explanation came with. If the hooks had pierced their heads before the boiling water was poured on them, the words of the Prophet (ﷺ), "Indeed the boiling water pierces the skull," would have no meaning. Rather, the matter is contrary to what this speaker said.

* *

And His words: ﴿With it, what is in their bellies and their skins will be melted﴾

He says: With the boiling water that is poured over their heads, what is in their bellies of fats is melted, and their skins are roasted by it and fall off. Ṣahr means melting. It is said of it: "I melted the fat with fire" when I melt it, I ṣahr it, ṣahran. From it is the poet's saying:

*You bring water to a stone [lāqī] cast upon a bare plain,
The sun melts it, yet it does not melt.* [[The verse is by Ibn Ahmar describing a sandgrouse chick (Lisan: ṣ-h-r). He said: "The sun ṣahrahu ṣahran" and "ṣahrahu": its heat strikes it intensely and pains its brain, and "inṣahara" is he. Ibn Ahmar describes a sandgrouse chick... the verse; i.e., the sun melts it, so it endures that. "Tarwi" means it brings water to it, as if it were a water-carrier for it; one says: "I gave my family water and they got water": I brought them water. Ṣahr: melting of fat; "ṣahara al-shahm yaṣhuruhu ṣahran": he melted it. In the revelation: "With it, what is in their bellies and their skins will be melted," i.e., melted. "Iṣṭahrahu": he melted it and ate it. "Laqī": everything cast aside and abandoned, like a lost item. "Ṣafṣaf": a smooth, level land, as in Lisan.]]

And from it is the saying of the rajaz poet:

*He melted the entrails, the roasted, the melted [mustaṣhar]* [[The verse is by al-Ajjaj ibn Ru'bah, the well-known rajaz poet (Lisan: ṣ-h-r). Al-Azhari said: al-ṣahr is melting fat, and al-ṣahārah is what melts of it; likewise al-iṣṭihār is melting, or eating its ṣahārah. Al-Ajjaj said: "He melted the entrails..." The verse is evidence, like the preceding, that ṣahr means melting.]]

And according to what we have said regarding that, the interpreters have spoken.

As related:

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿With it will be melted﴾, he said: "It is melted, a melting."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it. Ibn Jurayj said regarding ﴿With it will be melted﴾: "What was cut out for them of punishment."

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: ﴿With it, what is in their bellies will be melted﴾, he said: "With it is melted what is in their bellies."

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 18–22 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his statement: ﴿Those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them﴾ ... up to his statement: ﴿Whereby what is in their bellies will be melted, and the skins﴾. He said: They will be given to drink [something] which, when it enters their bellies, melts them, and the skins along with the bellies.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far and Harun ibn 'Antara, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Harun said: "When the people of the Fire become hungry," and Ja'far said: "When the people of the Fire become hungry, they will call for help to the tree of al-Zaqqum, and they will eat from it, and the skins of their faces will be stripped off. So if a passerby were to pass by them, he would recognize them by the skin of their faces in it. Then thirst will overcome them, and they will call for help, and they will be given relief with water like molten brass (al-muhl), which is water whose heat has reached its extreme. When they bring it near their mouths, the flesh of their faces, from which the skins have fallen, will be roasted by its heat. And ﴿whereby what is in their bellies will be melted﴾, meaning their intestines, and their skins will fall off. Then they will be struck with maces of iron, and every limb will fall into its place, and they will call out for destruction and perdition."

* *

As for His statement: ﴿And for them are maces of iron﴾:
The guardians of the Fire will strike their heads with them whenever they try to exit the Fire, until they return them into it.

* *

As for His statement: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, out of distress, they will be returned into it﴾:
He means: whenever these disbelievers, whose attributes Allah has described, wish to exit the Fire because of the distress and anguish that have befallen them, they will be returned to it.

As related by:
⁕ Mujahid ibn Musa related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn 'Awn related to us, saying: al-A'mash informed us, from Abu Zabyan, who said: "The Fire is black and dark; its flame does not give light, nor do its embers." Then he recited: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, out of distress, they will be returned into it﴾. It has been mentioned that they try to escape the Fire when Hell surges and throws those within it up to its highest gates; they wish to get out, but the guardians return them into it with maces, and when they strike them with the maces, they say to them: ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning﴾. By His statement ﴿And taste the punishment of the burning﴾ it is meant: it is said to them, "Taste the punishment of the Fire." It was also said "the punishment of the burning," and the meaning is "the burning [punishment]," just as it is said "the painful punishment," meaning "the painful [punishment]."

The Almighty says: As for those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and obeyed them in what Allah commanded them of righteous deeds, Allah will admit them into gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow, and they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls.

The reciters differed over the recitation (qira'at) of His words: ﴿وَلُؤْلُؤًا﴾ ("and pearls"). The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the reciters of Kufa read it in the accusative (naṣb), with the Qur'anic phrase ﴿وَلُؤْلُؤًا﴾ in the same form as in Surah al-Malaika (Surah 35), meaning: they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, coordinating pearls with the position (mawḍi') of the bracelets. This is because the bracelets, although in the genitive (khafḍ) owing to the preposition min, are in meaning in the accusative. They said: it is written with an alif in the codex (muṣḥaf), and that is evidence for the soundness of the reading in the accusative. The majority of the reciters of Iraq and the two cities (al-Baṣrah and al-Kufa, or as commonly designated) read ﴿وَلُؤْلُؤٍ﴾ in the genitive, coordinating it with the apparent grammatical case (i'rab) of the bracelets.

Those who read it in this way differed concerning the reason for the alif written in it. Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' is reported to have said: it is written with an alif just as it is written in قالوا and كالوا. Al-Kisa'i said: they wrote the alif in it for the hamza, because the hamza is one of the letters.

My view on this is that both are well-known recitations, each of which has been read by scholars among the reciters, having the same meaning and being sound in Arabic usage; so whichever of them the reciter reads, he is correct.

* *

And His words: ﴿وَلِبَاسُهُمْ فِيهَا حَرِيرٌ﴾ ("and their clothing therein is silk").

He says: their garments which touch their skins therein are garments of silk.

* *

His words: ﴿وَهُدُوا إِلَى الطَّيِّبِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ﴾ ("and they were guided to good speech").

The Almighty says: their Lord guided them in this world to the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

As follows:

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd, regarding His words ﴿وَهُدُوا إِلَى الطَّيِّبِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ﴾, said: They were guided to good speech: "There is no god but Allah," "Allah is greatest," and "Praise be to Allah." Allah said: ﴿إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ وَالْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ﴾ ("To Him ascend good words, and righteous deeds raise them up").

* Ali narrated to us, he said: Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿وَهُدُوا إِلَى الطَّيِّبِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ﴾, he said: They were inspired (ulhimu).

* *

And His words: ﴿وَهُدُوا إِلَى صِرَاطِ الْحَمِيدِ﴾ ("and they were guided to the path of the Praiseworthy").

His glorious praise says: their Lord guided them in this world to the way of the Praiseworthy Lord. His way is His religion, the religion of Islam, which He legislated for His creatures and commanded them to follow. Al-Ḥamīd is a form (fa'īl) transferred from the passive participle (maf'ūl) to it, and its meaning is that He is praised by His friends among His creatures; then it was transferred from maḥmūd (praised) to ḥamīd (praiseworthy).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 25 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Indeed, those who have disbelieved and avert [people] from the way of Allah and from al-Masjid al-Haram, which We made for the people - equally [for] the residing therein and the visitor. And whoever intends therein deviation [from the truth] through wrongdoing - We will make him taste of a painful punishment.﴾

His, may He be remembered, says: Indeed, those who denied the Oneness of Allah, rejected His messengers, and disbelieved in what came to them from their Lord, ﴿and avert [people] from the way of Allah﴾, meaning: they prevent people from entering the religion of Allah, and from al-Masjid al-Haram, which Allah made for the people, those who believe in Him, all of them, without singling out some of them over others. ﴿Equally [for] the residing therein and the visitor﴾, meaning: it is equal in what is obligatory upon him of honouring the sanctity of al-Masjid al-Haram, performing his rites there, and lodging there wherever he wishes, the residing therein (al-'Akif), who is the one who stays there permanently; and the visitor (al-Bad), who is the one who comes to it from elsewhere.

The commentators differed in the interpretation of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: equal are the one residing therein, who is the one who stays there, and the visitor, in that neither of them has more right to a dwelling there than the other.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Ibn Sabit, who said: When the pilgrims came to Mecca, none of the people of Mecca had more right to his dwelling than they did, and whoever found space would lodge there. Theft spread among them, and each person stole from his own side. A man built a door, and 'Umar sent to him: "Have you made a door against the pilgrims of the House of Allah?" He said: "No, I only made it to secure their belongings." This is His words: ﴿equally [for] the residing therein and the visitor﴾. He said: the visitor there is like the resident; no one has more right to his dwelling than another, unless someone has already preceded to a dwelling.

- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, who said: I said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "I perform i'tikaf in Mecca." He said: "You are an 'akif." And he recited: ﴿equally [for] the residing therein and the visitor﴾.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from one whom he mentioned, from Abu Salih: ﴿equally [for] the residing therein and the visitor﴾ - the 'akif: its people; the bad: the one who comes to the dwelling; equal.

- 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿equally [for] the residing therein and the visitor﴾: it means the people of Mecca and others alight in al-Masjid al-Haram.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿equally [for] the residing therein and the visitor﴾: "The one residing therein is the one who stays in Mecca; and the visitor is the one who comes to it from elsewhere; they are equal in the houses."

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿equally [for] the residing therein and the visitor﴾: equal in it are its people and non-people.

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, the like of it.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿equally [for] the residing therein and the visitor﴾: the people of Mecca and others are equal in the dwellings.

Others said something similar to what we have said regarding it.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His words: ﴿equally [for] the residing therein﴾: the resident, ﴿and the visitor﴾: the one from abroad; equal in the right of Allah upon both of them therein.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿equally [for] the residing therein﴾: the resident, ﴿and the visitor﴾: the one from abroad.

- He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumayla narrated to us, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from Mujahid and 'Ata', regarding: ﴿equally [for] the residing therein﴾: "both of them said: its people; ﴿and the visitor﴾: those who come to it from other than its people; they are equal in its sanctity."

What we have chosen as our view on this is because Allah, may He be remembered, mentioned at the beginning of the verse the prevention, by those who disbelieved in Him, of those among the believers who wished to perform their rites in the Sacred Precinct from al-Masjid al-Haram, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who have disbelieved and avert [people] from the way of Allah and from al-Masjid al-Haram﴾. Then He, may His praise be exalted, described al-Masjid al-Haram, saying: ﴿which We made for the people﴾, so He informed that He made it for all the people. Thus, the disbelievers in Him prevent those believers in Him who wish to come to it. Then He said: ﴿equally [for] the residing therein and the visitor﴾. It is therefore known that His information about the equality of the resident and the visitor therein is, in meaning, that which begins the information about the disbelievers, that they prevent the believers in Him from it. That undoubtedly refers to their circumambulation, performance of their rites there, and staying, not information about their ownership of it or non-ownership. It was said: ﴿Indeed, those who have disbelieved and avert [people] from the way of Allah﴾, so He joined "yasuddun" (they avert), which is in the present/future form, to "kafaru" (they disbelieved), which is in the past form, because the averting is in the sense of a description of them and of continuity. When that is the meaning of the speech, it can only be expressed by the noun form or the present tense, not by the past tense. Given that, the meaning of the speech is: indeed, those who disbelieved have as their attribute the averting from the way of Allah. This is like the saying of Allah: ﴿those who believe and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of Allah﴾.

As for His words: ﴿equally [for] the residing therein﴾, the readers of the regional cities read "sawa'un" (equal) in the nominative, with "al-'akifu" and "al-'akifu bihi", and the verb "ja'alnahu" operates on the attached pronoun (ha') and the lam in His words "lil-nas" (for the people), then the speech resumes with "sawa'" (equal). This is how the Arabs treat "sawa'" when it comes after a particle with which the speech has been completed. They say: "Marartu bi-rajulin sawa'un 'indahu al-khayru wa-al-sharr" (I passed by a man, to whom good and evil are equal). The genitive is also permissible in this, but the nominative is preferred, because "sawa'" in their usage is one unit, as if they said: "Marartu bi-rajulin wahidin 'indahu al-khayru wa-al-sharr" (I passed by a man, one, to whom good and evil...). As for one who reads it in the genitive, he directs it to "mu'tadil" (balanced), to whom good and evil are alike. Whoever says that about "sawa'" and resumes with it in the nominative does not say it of "mu'tadil", because "mu'tadil" is an explicit verb, while "sawa'" is a verbal noun (masdar); moving it into the verb form is like moving "hasb" in their saying: "Marartu bi-rajulin hasbuka min rajulin" (I passed by a man, enough for you from a man) into the verb form. It has been reported from some readers that he read it in the accusative, operating "ja'alnahu" upon it, and although this has a basis in Arabic, it is a reading I do not permit, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers against it.

* *

His words: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation [from the truth] through wrongdoing - We will make him taste of a painful punishment.﴾

His, may He be remembered, says: And whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing, We will make him taste of a painful punishment, namely, that he inclines in the Sacred House to wrongdoing. The preposition "bi" was introduced in His words "bi-ilhadin" (through deviation), and its meaning is as I have said, just as it was introduced in His words: ﴿grows with the oil [ tanbutu bi-l-duhni]﴾, meaning: it grows oil, as the poet said:

*In a valley of Yemen, whose upper part grows the thorn-bush (shatt), and whose lower part [grows] with the markh and the shabhan*

Meaning: its lower part grows the markh and the shabhan. And as the poet of Banu Tha'laba said:

*Our spears have guaranteed the provision of our dependants, between the cooking-pots and the bare, unhaired she-camel.*

The meaning of the verses: Allah made our food in our wealth, a provision which will never run out. They are huge like hills; we slaughter them with our swords for guests, and none of them is driven away by a terrified or raiding person. Their rumps guarantee our cooking-pots (that they will be emptied), due to their fatness and abundance of flesh, and their udders guarantee us pure, clear milk. (See the Diwan, Cairo edition, p. 230, with the commentary of Dr. Muhammad Husayn.) In al-Lisan there is another version of the verse, attributed to the poet, under "jurd" (bare), he said: "albin wa-jard, la raghwa" (milk and bare, without foam); the poet said: *Our spears have guaranteed its rumps...*, and on these two versions there is no evidence in the verse, because the author cited it only as evidence for the superfluous "bi" in His words "bi-rizq" (for provision), and there is no superfluous "bi" in these two versions. He made the "bi" in "bi-rizq" equivalent to the "bi" in the verse: "wa-man yurid fihi bi-ilhadin bi-zulmin", i.e., on the assumption: "wa-man yurid fihi ilhadan bi-zulmin."

Meaning: "Our spears guaranteed the provision of our dependants," according to the view of some Basran grammarians. As for some Kufan grammarians, he would say: the "bi" was introduced into it, because its interpretation is: "and whoever intends, by deviating therein through wrongdoing." He would say: the introduction of "bi" before "an" (that) is easier than before "ilhad" and the like, because "an" often implies the prepositions with it and functions like a condition, so it admits the introduction and omission of the governing preposition, since the case-ending does not appear in it; whereas in the verbal nouns (masadir) the nominative and genitive are visible. He said: Abu al-Jarrah recited to me:

*When they were pleased with drinking, he shook the staff for them, a stingy man, to whom at the giving there is a snorting [ nahim ].*

This verse is among the evidences of al-Farra', pupil of al-Kisa'i, and these two are the two leaders of the Kufan grammarians; it is one of what Abu al-Jarrah, one of the Bedouins from whom he took the language, recited to him (see it in Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra', folio 10 of the University photocopy). "Al-nahim," as in (al-Lisan: nahm), is a sound like a growl; it is said to be a sound above a roar; al-nahim is a sound of threat and rebuke. The pronoun in "lahа" (for her) probably refers to the camels that wished to drink; when they were almost reaching the water, a man with a harsh, loud voice shook the staff for them and drove them away from it. The evidence in the verse is that the superfluous "bi" in His words "bi-l-shurbi" (with drinking) governs a pure verbal noun, and al-Farra' holds that its governing of a deduced verbal noun with "an" or "ma" is better than governing a pure verbal noun. Al-Farra' said: His words "wa-man yurid fihi bi-ilhadin bi-zulmin" - the "bi" entered upon "ilhad," because its interpretation is: "and whoever intends by deviating therein through wrongdoing," and the introduction of "bi" with "an" is easier than with "ilhad" and the like, because "an" often omits the prepositions with it (he means the prepositional particles), so it admits the introduction and omission of the governing preposition, since the case-ending does not appear in it; whereas in pure verbal nouns the nominative and genitive appear in them. Abu al-Jarrah recited to me: "When they were pleased with drinking..." the verse.

And al-Imru' al-Qays said:

*Has there not come to her, while events are numerous, that Imru' al-Qays ibn Tamlik was Bayqara?*

This verse is by Imru' al-Qays ibn Hujr (al-'Iqd al-Thamin li-l-Awlad, p. 130), and it is not in the recension of the Diwan of Imru' al-Qays by al-A'lam al-Shantamari. The verse is evidence, like the previous one, that the "bi" in His words "bi-anna" (that) is superfluous before the deduced verbal noun in the nominative, and it is better there than before a pure verbal noun because the case-ending is hidden with it. It is among al-Farra's evidences in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, which he cited together with the previous evidence (see Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra', folio 310). He said: He introduced "bi" before "an," and it is in the nominative position, as he introduced it before "ilhad bi-zulm," which is in the accusative position. He said: They have also introduced "bi" before "ma" when they intended by it the verbal noun, as the poet said:

*Has it not come to you, while the news spreads, about what the she-camels of Banu Ziyad encountered?*

This verse is by Qays ibn Zuhayr al-'Absi, as in (al-Nawadir by Abu Zayd al-Ansari, p. 203). The "ya'" was not dropped in His words "ya'tika" (comes to you) for the jussive, out of necessity. The verse is among al-Farra's evidences in (Ma'ani al-Qur'an, p. 310) that they may introduce the superfluous particle before the deduced verbal noun with "ma" and what follows it. He said: They have introduced it before "ma" when they intended "an," which is less resembling nouns than "ma." And I heard a Bedouin from Rabi'a, and I asked him about something, and he said: "arjū bi-dhālika" (I hope for that), meaning "arjū dhāka" (I hope for that).

He said: It is less before "ma" than before "an," because "an" is less resembling nouns than "ma." He said: I heard a Bedouin from Rabi'a, and I asked him about something, and he said: "arjū bi-dhāka," meaning "arjū dhāka."

The commentators differed regarding the meaning of the wrongdoing with which whoever intends deviation in al-Masjid al-Haram, Allah makes him taste the painful punishment. Some of them said: it is associating partners with Allah and worshipping others alongside Him, i.e., with respect to the House.

Those who said that:

- 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿and whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing﴾: he says: through shirk.

- 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿and whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing﴾: it is that one worships other than Allah therein.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, saying: ﴿and whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing﴾: it is shirk; whoever associates in the House of Allah, Allah punishes him.

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, the like of it.

Others said: it is making lawful what is forbidden therein, or committing it.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿and whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing, We will make him taste of a painful punishment﴾: he means that you make lawful from what is forbidden what Allah has forbidden you, whether by tongue or killing, so you wrong one who does not wrong you, and kill one who does not kill you. When he does that, a painful punishment becomes due to him.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing﴾: he said: he does an evil deed therein.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- Abu Kurayb and Nasr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi narrated to us, both saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Murra, from 'Abd Allah, who said: No man intends an evil deed and it is recorded against him; and if a man, after making it clear, intended to kill a man in this House, Allah would make him taste a painful punishment.

- Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Murra, from 'Abd Allah, Mujahid said, Yazid said, Shu'ba told us, raising it (to the Prophet), and I do not raise it for you, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿and whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing, We will make him taste of a painful punishment﴾: he said: if a man intended therein an evil deed, and after it was made clear, Allah would make him taste a painful punishment.

- al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding His words: ﴿and whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing﴾: he said: a man may intend a sin in Mecca while he is in another land and has not committed it, and it is recorded against him.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿and whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing, We will make him taste of a painful punishment﴾: he said: the deviation is wrongdoing in the Sacred Precinct.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that wrongdoing is making lawful the sanctuary deliberately.

Those who said that:

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿through deviation through wrongdoing﴾: he said: the one who intends to make it lawful deliberately; it is said, shirk.

Others said: rather, that is the hoarding of food in Mecca.

Those who said that:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 25 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, regarding His words ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation by wrongdoing – We will make him taste a painful punishment﴾: "They are those who hoard food in Makkah."

Others said: Rather, it refers to everything forbidden of action, even the saying of a speaker: "No, by Allah," and "Yes, by Allah."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: He had two tents, one in the non-sacred territory (al-hill) and the other in the sacred territory (al-haram). When he wished to rebuke his family, he rebuked them in the non-sacred territory. When he was asked about that, he said: "We used to be told that among deviation therein is for a man to say: 'No, by Allah,' and 'Yes, by Allah.'"

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Abu Rab'i, from al-A'mash, who said: Abdullah ibn Amr used to say: "No, by Allah," and "Yes, by Allah," are deviation therein.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of the sayings we have mentioned in interpreting this is the view we have reported from Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas, that by wrongdoing in this passage is meant every act of disobedience to Allah. This is because Allah, by His words ﴿by wrongdoing﴾, expressed it generally and did not restrict it to one kind of wrongdoing over another, either by report or by reason, so it remains on its general meaning. Given that, the meaning of the statement is: whoever intends in the Sacred Mosque to incline toward wrongdoing, disobeying Allah therein, We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection a painful punishment.

It has been reported that some reciters (qurra', sing. qari') used to recite it as ﴿wa man yaridu fihi﴾ with the ya vowelled with a fatha, meaning: "whoever brings it (yaridahu) with deviation," from wa radtu al-makan, aridu. But this is a reading which, in my view, is not permissible to recite, because it contradicts what the proofs of the reciters have agreed upon, and because it is far from the eloquent speech of the Arabs. This is because yarid is a transitive verb, said of oneself: "he comes to such a place or such a town," and one does not say "yarid fi makan kadha." Some people knowledgeable in the speech of the Arabs have claimed that the tribe of Tayy say "raghibtu fika," meaning "raghibtu bika" (I desired you). It is mentioned that one of them recited to him a verse:

"And I am averse to her, away from Laqit and his kin,
But as for Sinbis, I am not averse (to her)."

Meaning: "wa arghabu biha" (and I am eager for her). If that is sound as we have mentioned, then it is permissible in ordinary speech, but as for reciting it that way, it is not permissible, for the reasons I have described.

[The verse has already been cited earlier in the same manner, in (13:189), and it is one of al-Farra's evidences in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, folio 161 and folio 310 of the University's microfilm copy (that some Arabs place "fi" in the position of "ba'", saying "adkhalaka Allahu bi-l-janna" meaning "fi al-janna"). Al-Farra said in (p. 310): "It may be permissible in the dialect of the Ta'iyy, for they say 'raghibtu fika,' meaning 'raghibtu bika.' One of them recited to me: 'wa arghabu fiha 'an Laqit...' The verse… meaning his daughter." End.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 26:

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] when We settled for Abraham the site of the House, [saying], "Do not associate anything with Me and purify My House for those who circumambulate and those who stand [in prayer] and those who bow and prostrate."﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), informing him of the greatness of what his people, the Quraysh in particular and not others of all of His creation, have been bestowed with, through their worship in His sanctuary, and of the House which He commanded His intimate friend Abraham (ﷺ) to build and to purify from afflictions, doubts and polytheism: "And mention, O Muhammad, how We initiated this House, which your people worship in other than Me, when We settled for Our friend Abraham," meaning by His words "settled": We made the site of the House suitable for him.

As follows:

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Mamar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And [mention] when We settled for Abraham the site of the House﴾, he said: Allah placed the House with Adam (ﷺ) when Adam was sent down to the earth. Its descent was in the land of India, and his head was in the sky and his feet were on the earth. The angels feared him, so he was reduced to sixty cubits. When Adam missed the voices of the angels and their glorification, he complained of that to Allah, and Allah said: "O Adam, I have sent down for you a House which will be circumambulated as My Throne is circumambulated, and prayed beside as My Throne is prayed around. So set out towards it!" He went out towards it, and his strides were lengthened for him, so that between every two steps there was a desert. Those deserts remained so until Adam reached the House, circumambulated it, and so did those after him of the prophets.

⁕ Musa narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When Allah charged Abraham and Ishmael that they should purify My House for those who circumambulate, Abraham set out until he came to Mecca. He and Ishmael stood up and took up the spades, not knowing where the House was. Then Allah sent a wind called the wind of al-Khajuj, which has two wings and a head in the form of a serpent.
