It swept away for them what was around the Kaʿbah, down to the foundation of the first House, and they followed it with the spades, digging, until they laid the foundation. That is the time when He says: ﴿And [mention] when We settled for Abraham the site of the House﴾.

By "the House" is meant the Kaʿbah. ﴿Do not associate anything with Me﴾ in your worship of Me, ﴿and purify My House﴾ which I built, from the worship of idols.

As follows:

⁕ Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿and purify My House﴾, he said: from polytheism.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from ʿAta, from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, who said: from afflictions and doubts.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Mamar, from Qatadah: ﴿purify My House﴾ [addressed to the two of them], he said: from polytheism and the worship of idols.

* *

And His words: ﴿for those who circumambulate﴾

That is, for those who circumambulate, and "those who stand" means those who pray while standing in their prayer.

As follows:

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumayla narrated to us, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from ʿAta, regarding His words: ﴿and purify My House for those who circumambulate and those who stand﴾, he said: those who stand in prayer.

⁕ al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Mamar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿and those who stand﴾, he said: those who stand and pray.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Mamar, from Qatadah, the same.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿and those who stand and those who bow and prostrate﴾: the one who stands, bows and prostrates is the one who prays, and the one who circumambulates is the one who goes around it.

* *

And His words: ﴿and those who bow and prostrate﴾

He says: those who bow and prostrate in their prayer around the House.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 27–29 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And proclaim to mankind the Hajj; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every deep, distant pass﴾ (22:27), ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah on known days over the beasts of livestock He has provided for them. So eat from them and feed the miserable, the poor﴾ (22:28), ﴿then let them end their state of unkemptness, fulfil their vows, and circumambulate the Ancient House﴾ (22:29).

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We also committed to him (Ibrahim) that he proclaim to mankind the Hajj. By His words ﴿And proclaim﴾ He means: inform and call out to mankind that they should perform the Hajj to the Sacred House of Allah, O people. ﴿They will come to you on foot﴾ means: people will come to the House you have been commanded to make Hajj to, walking on their feet. ﴿And on every lean camel﴾ means: and riding upon every lean camel, which are the emaciated camels. ﴿They will come from every deep, distant pass﴾ means: these lean camels will come from every deep pass, that is, from every distant road, place and path. It was also said: "they will come" (yatīna, feminine plural), using the plural because by "every lean camel" is meant the she-camels, and the word "kull" (every) carries the sense of plurality, which is why it was said "yatīna." Al-Farra' claimed that this is rare in the speech of the Arabs: "I passed by every man standing (qā'imīn)." He said: "and it is correct; and God's words ﴿and on lean camels they will come﴾ point to the soundness of its permissibility."

It is related that when God commanded Ibrahim, may God's blessings be upon him, to proclaim the Hajj, he stood upon his station (maqam) and called out: "O people, indeed God has prescribed for you the Hajj, so perform the Hajj to His Ancient House."

The manner of Ibrahim's proclamation has been disputed. Some of them said: he called out with it, as follows:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Ibrahim finished building the House, it was said to him: ﴿Proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾. He said: "My Lord, and will my voice reach?" He said: "Proclaim, and upon Me is the delivery." So Ibrahim called out: "O people, the Hajj to the Ancient House has been prescribed for you, so perform it." He said: "His voice was heard between the heaven and the earth. Do you not see people coming from the farthest parts of the earth, responding with the talbiyah?"

- Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl ibn Ghazwan al-Dabbi related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Ibrahim built the House, God revealed to him: "Proclaim among the people the Hajj." He said: Ibrahim said: "Indeed your Lord has taken a House, and has commanded you to perform its Hajj." So there responded to him whatever heard him of stone, tree, hillock, earth, or anything: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: Ibn Waqid related to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾: He said: Ibrahim, the friend of God, stood upon the stone and called out: "O people, the Hajj has been prescribed for you." So he made heard whoever was in the loins of men and the wombs of women, and there responded to him whoever believed and whom God had foreknown would perform the Hajj until the Day of Resurrection: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk."

- Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Proclaim among the people the Hajj; they will come to you on foot﴾. He said: It settled in the heart of every male and female.

- Ibn Humayd related to me, he said: Hakkam related to us, from 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When Ibrahim finished building the House, God revealed to him that he proclaim among the people the Hajj. He said: So he went out and called out among the people: "O people, indeed your Lord has taken a House, so perform its Hajj." Then no one heard him that day, of humankind, jinn, trees, hillocks, earth, mountains, water, or anything, except that it said: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk."

- Hakkam related to us, from 'Anbasa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Ibrahim stood upon the station when he was commanded to proclaim among the people the Hajj.

- Al-Qasim related to me, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾: He said: Ibrahim stood upon his station and said: "O people, respond to your Lord." They said: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk." So whoever performs Hajj today is among those who responded to Ibrahim on that day.

- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy related to us, from Dawud, from 'Ikrimah ibn Khalid al-Makhzumi, who said: When Ibrahim, peace be upon him, finished building the House, he stood upon the station and called out a call that the people of the earth heard: "Indeed your Lord has built for you a House, so perform its Hajj." Dawud said: "So I hope that whoever performs Hajj today is responding to Ibrahim, peace be upon him." [[The text of this last phrase appears thus in the original; perhaps its original form was: "So I hope that everyone who performs Hajj today, his Hajj is a response to Ibrahim's."]]

- Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz related to me, he said: Hajjaj related to us, he said: Hammad related to us, from Abu 'Asim al-Ghanawi, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Do you know how the talbiyah was?" I said: "And how was the talbiyah?" He said: When Ibrahim was commanded to proclaim among the people the Hajj, the mountains lowered their heads for him, and the towns were raised up, and he called out among the people.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾: Ibrahim said: "How shall I say it, my Lord?" He said: "Say: O people, respond to your Lord." He said: And it settled in the heart of every believer.

Others said concerning this, that:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Salamah, from Mujahid, who said: It was said to Ibrahim: "Proclaim among the people the Hajj." He said: "My Lord, how shall I say it?" He said: "Say: Labbayka Allahumma labbayk." He said: So that was the first talbiyah.

Ibn 'Abbas used to say: By "the people" in this place is meant: the people of the qiblah (the Muslims).

The narration for this: Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾: By "the people" is meant the people of the qiblah. Have you not heard that He said: ﴿Indeed the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed ... [up to His words] ... and whoever enters it is safe﴾ (3:96–97)? [He means:] whoever among mankind enters it, those among whom the proclamation was made and upon whom the Hajj was prescribed, is safe. So honour the sacred things of God, for they are of the piety of hearts.

As for His words ﴿They will come to you on foot and on every lean camel﴾, the people of interpretation said concerning it what we have said.

Al-Qasim related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿They will come to you on foot﴾ means: walking.

- He said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Arta'ah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "I have no regret over anything that escaped me except that I did not perform Hajj on foot. I heard God say: ﴿They will come to you on foot﴾."

- He said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Ibrahim and Isma'il performed Hajj walking.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿They will come to you on foot﴾, he said: upon their feet.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And on every lean camel﴾: He said: the camels.

- Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿And on every lean camel﴾: He said: the camels.

- Nasr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi related to me, he said: al-Muharibi related to us, from 'Umar ibn Dharr, who said: Mujahid said: "They used not to ride, so God revealed: ﴿They will come to you on foot and on every lean camel﴾." He said: So He commanded them to take provisions, and permitted them to ride and to trade.

* *

And His words ﴿from every deep, distant pass﴾:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿from every deep, distant pass﴾, meaning: from a distant place.

- Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿from every deep pass﴾: distant.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿deep pass﴾: a distant place.

- Al-Hasan related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, the same.

* *

And His words: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of the benefits mentioned by God in this place. Some of them said: they are trade and the benefits of this world.

Those who said this: Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam related to us, he said: 'Amr ibn 'Asim related to us, from Abu Razin, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾, he said: they are the markets.

- Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Abu Tumaylah related to us, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir ibn al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: trade.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Ahmad related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from 'Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Abu Razin, regarding His words ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾: he said: their markets.

- He said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Waqid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾, he said: trade.

- 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, he said: Ishaq informed us, from Sufyan, from Waqid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the same.

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Waqid, from Sa'id, the same.

- al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Sinan related to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Razin: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾, he said: the markets.

Others said: they are the reward in the Hereafter and trade in this world.

Those who said this: Ibn Bashshar and Suwar ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, both said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾, he said: trade, and what pleases God of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter.

- 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, he said: Ishaq related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

- 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, he said: Ishaq informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾: he said: the reward in the Hereafter and trade in this world.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

Others said: rather, they are pardon and forgiveness.

Those who said this: Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾, he said: pardon.

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Abu Tumaylah related to me, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali said: forgiveness.

The most correct of the sayings is the saying of the one who said: What is meant is: that they may witness benefits for themselves, from the deed that pleases God, and from trade. This is because God made general for them the benefits of everything that the season (mawsim) witnesses, and what comes to Makkah during the days of the season of benefits of this world and the Hereafter, and He did not specify any of those benefits for them by report or by reason. So it is general in the benefits described.

* *

And His words: ﴿and mention the name of Allah on known days over the beasts of livestock He has provided for them﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: that they may mention the name of God over the sacrificial animals and camels, cows and sheep He has provided for them, on known days, which, according to some of the people of interpretation, are the days of tashriq (the days after the Eid). According to others, they are the ten days. According to others: the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr) and the days of tashriq.

We have already mentioned the disagreement of the people of interpretation concerning this with the narrations, and we explained which is more correct among them in Surat al-Baqarah, so that suffices instead of repeating it in this place, though I will mention some of it here as well.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and mention the name of Allah on known days﴾: meaning the days of tashriq.

- I was told from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak regarding His words ﴿known days﴾: meaning the days of tashriq; ﴿over the beasts of livestock He has provided for them﴾: meaning the sacrificial animals.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿on known days﴾, he said: the ten days; and "the counted days" (al-ma'dudat): the days of tashriq.

* *

And His words: ﴿So eat from them﴾

He says: eat from the beasts of livestock over which you have mentioned the name of God, O people, there. This command from God, may His praise be exalted, is a command of permission, not a command of obligation, because there is no disagreement among all the proof that whoever slaughters his offering or his camel there, if he does not eat from his offering or his camel, he has not neglected any duty that was obligatory upon him; so it is known thereby that it is not obligatory.

Report from some of the scholars who said this: Suwar ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', regarding His words ﴿So eat from them and feed the miserable, the poor﴾: he said: He did not regard eating from them as obligatory.

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, he said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Husayn informed us, from Mujahid, that he said: It is a concession: if he wishes he eats, and if he wishes he does not eat, and it is like His words: ﴿And when you have come out of the state of ihram, then hunt﴾ (5:2) and ﴿And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse in the land﴾ (62:10). He means His words: ﴿So eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar﴾ (22:36).

- He said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, regarding His words ﴿So eat from them﴾: he said: It is a concession; if he wishes he eats, and if he wishes he does not eat.

- He said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Hajjaj informed us, from 'Ata', regarding His words ﴿So eat from them﴾: he said: It is a concession; if he wishes he eats, and if he wishes he does not eat.

- 'Ali ibn Sahl related to me, he said: Zayd related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Husayn, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿So eat from them﴾: he said: It is only a concession.

* *

And His words: ﴿and feed the miserable, the poor﴾

He says: and feed from what you slaughter or sacrifice there, from your offerings and camels, the miserable (ba'is), who is the one afflicted with the harm of hunger, disability and need; and the poor (faqir) is the one who has nothing.

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said concerning its interpretation.

Those who said this: Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His words ﴿So eat from them and feed the miserable, the poor﴾: meaning: the disabled poor.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from a man, from Mujahid: ﴿the miserable, the poor﴾: he who stretches out his hands to you.

- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿the miserable, the poor﴾: he is the one who is content (qani').

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Umar ibn 'Ata' informed me, from 'Ikrimah, who said: The miserable (ba'is): the one compelled, upon whom is misery; and the poor (faqir): the one who abstains (mutta'affif).

- He said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿the miserable﴾: he who extends his hands.

* *

And His words: ﴿then let them end their state of unkemptness﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: then let them complete what is incumbent upon them of the rites of their Hajj: shaving the hair, trimming the moustache, throwing the pebbles at the jamarat, and circumambulating the House.

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said concerning this.

Those who said this: Ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, he said: Yazid related to me, he said: al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar informed us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that he said: ﴿then let them end their state of unkemptness﴾: he said: what they are in the state of Hajj.

- Humayd ibn Mas'adah related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: al-Ash'ath related to me, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: Tafath: all the rites.

- He said: Hushaym related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Malik informed us, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said, regarding His words ﴿then let them end their state of unkemptness﴾: He said: Tafath: shaving the head, taking from the two moustaches, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, cutting the nails, taking from the sideburns, throwing the pebbles at the jamarat, and standing at 'Arafah and Muzdalifah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 27–29 (part 2 of 2):

• Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, who said: "al-tafath" is the hair and the nails.

• Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Khalid, from ʿIkrimah, the like of it.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Ṣakhr informed me, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, that he used to say concerning this verse: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾: the throwing of the pebbles (ramy al-jimar), the slaughtering of the sacrificial animal, the taking from the moustache, the beard and the nails, and the circumambulation of the House and of al-Safa and al-Marwah.

• Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujahid, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾. He said: It is shaving the head, and he mentioned other things of the Hajj. Shuʿbah said: I do not remember them.

• He said: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujahid, the like of it.

• Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾. He said: shaving the head, shaving the pubic area, clipping the nails, trimming the moustache, throwing the pebbles, and trimming the beard.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it, except that he did not say in his narration: and trimming the beard.

• Naṣr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥman al-Azdi narrated to me, saying: al-Muḥaribi narrated to us, saying: I heard a man asking Ibn Juraij about His saying: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾. He said: taking from the beard, from the moustache, cutting the nails, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic area, and throwing the pebbles.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Manṣur informed us, from al-Ḥasan, and Juwaybir informed us, from al-Ḍaḥḥak, that both of them said: shaving the head.

• I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say concerning His saying: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾: he means shaving the head.

• Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: al-tafath: shaving the head and clipping the nail.

• Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾. He says: their rites (nusuk).

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾: al-tafath: their sanctity (ḥurum).

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾. He said: By al-tafath is meant the removal of their state of ihram: shaving the head, wearing garments, clipping the nails, and the like.

• Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from ʿAṭaʾ ibn al-Sa’ib, who said: al-tafath: shaving the hair, clipping the nails, taking from the moustache, shaving the pubic area, and the whole matter of the Hajj.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And let them fulfil their vows﴾.
He says: and let them fulfil to Allah what they vowed of offerings, camels, and other things.
The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said.

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying: ﴿And let them fulfil their vows﴾: the slaughtering of the camels they vowed.

• Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And let them fulfil their vows﴾: the vow of the Hajj and the offering, and whatever a person vows of a thing that occurs in the Hajj.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: ﴿And let them fulfil their vows﴾. He said: the vow of the Hajj and the offering, and whatever a person vows upon himself of a thing that occurs in the Hajj.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾.
He says: and let them circumambulate the Sacred House of Allah.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of His saying: ﴿al-ʿatīq﴾ in this place. Some of them said: it is said of the Sacred House of Allah because Allah freed it (aʿtaqahu) from tyrants, so that they could not reach its destruction and demolition.

Mention of those who said that: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhri, that Ibn al-Zubayr said: The House was only named the Ancient House because Allah freed it from tyrants.

• al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Zubayr, the like of it.

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muʾammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: It was only named al-ʿAtīq because it was freed from tyrants.

• He said: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾. He said: It was freed from tyrants.

• Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His saying: ﴿the Ancient House﴾. He said: Allah freed it from tyrants, meaning the Kaʿbah.

Others said: It was called ʿatīq because no one of mankind has ever owned it.

Mention of those who said that: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muʾammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿUbayd, from Mujahid, who said: The Ancient House was only named so because no one has any claim over it.

Others said: It was named so for its antiquity.

Mention of those who said that: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿the Ancient House﴾: al-ʿatīq means the old, because it is old, as one says: an ancient sword, because it was the first house set down for mankind, built by Adam, and he was the first to build it; then Allah settled its place for Ibrahim after the Flood, and Ibrahim and Isma'il built it.

Abu Jaʿfar said: For all of these sayings which we have mentioned from those we have attributed them to, concerning His saying: ﴿the Ancient House﴾, there is a sound aspect; however, what Ibn Zayd said is the most apparent of its meanings. Yet what has been narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr is more worthy of soundness, if what:

• Muḥammad ibn Sahl al-Bukhari narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth informed me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥman ibn Khalid ibn Musafir, from al-Zuhri, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUrwah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The House was only named the Ancient House because Allah freed it from tyrants, so that it was never overcome by anyone."

• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: al-Zuhri said: We have been informed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The House was only named the Ancient House because Allah freed it," and then he mentioned the like of it.

By the circumambulation which Allah, may His praise be exalted, commanded the pilgrim to perform around His Ancient House in this verse is meant the circumambulation of ifadah, which is performed after the standing at ʿArafah, either on the Day of Sacrifice or after it; there is no disagreement among the people of interpretation about this.

Mention of the narration from some who said that: ʿAmr ibn Saʿid al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: al-Ansari narrated to us, from Ashʿath, from al-Ḥasan: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾. He said: the circumambulation of ziyarah.

• Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, saying: al-Ashʿath narrated to us, that al-Ḥasan said concerning His saying: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾: the obligatory circumambulation.

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾: meaning the visiting of the House.

• Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Ḥajjaj and ʿAbd al-Malik, from ʿAṭaʾ, concerning His saying: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾. He said: the circumambulation of the Day of Sacrifice.

• Abu ʿAbd al-Raḥman al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, saying: I asked Zuhayr about the saying of Allah: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾. He said: the circumambulation of farewell.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of these letters. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited "ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا تَفَثَهُمْ وَلْيُوفُوا نُذُورَهُمْ وَلْيَطَّوَّفُوا" with the lam quiescent (sukun) in all of them, seeking lightness, just as they did with huwa when preceded by a waw, so they said "وَهْوَ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ" and made the ha quiescent; and they do likewise with the lam of the imperative when preceded by one of the conjunctive particles such as waw, fa’ and thumma. The majority of the readers of Basra recited in the same way, except that Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla used to vocalize the lam with kasra in His saying: ﴿thumma l-yaqḍū﴾ specifically, because pausing on thumma without continuing to liyaqḍū is good, whereas pausing on the waw and the fa’ is not permissible. This reason which Abu ʿAmr gave for his reading is a good reason from the standpoint of analogy; nevertheless, most of the readers hold to its sukun.

The most correct of the sayings in this matter in my view is that the sukun in the lam of "liyaqḍū" and the kasra are two well-known recitations and two current dialects, so whichever one the reader recites is correct. However, the kasra in it specifically is more analogous, for the reason we have mentioned from Abu ʿAmr, because whoever recites "وَهْوَ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ" makes the ha quiescent after waw and fa’, but vocalizes it in His saying: ﴿thumma huwa yawma l-qiyāmati mina l-muḥḍarīn﴾. It is therefore obligatory for him to do the same in "thumma l-yaqḍū tafathahum", vocalizing the lam to kasra with thumma, even though he makes it quiescent in His saying: ﴿wa-l-yūfū nudhūrahum﴾. It has also been mentioned from Abu ʿAbd al-Raḥman al-Sulami and al-Ḥasan al-Basri that they vocalized it after thumma and waw, which is a well-known dialect; nevertheless, most readers hold to its sukun after waw and fa’, and it is the more famous and more eloquent of the two dialects among the Arabs, so reciting with it is more pleasing to me than with the kasra.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 27–29 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And proclaim to mankind the Hajj; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every deep, distant pass﴾ (22:27), ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah on known days over the beasts of livestock He has provided for them. So eat from them and feed the miserable, the poor﴾ (22:28), ﴿then let them end their state of unkemptness, fulfil their vows, and circumambulate the Ancient House﴾ (22:29).

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We also committed to him (Ibrahim) that he proclaim to mankind the Hajj. By His words ﴿And proclaim﴾ He means: inform and call out to mankind that they should perform the Hajj to the Sacred House of Allah, O people. ﴿They will come to you on foot﴾ means: people will come to the House you have been commanded to make Hajj to, walking on their feet. ﴿And on every lean camel﴾ means: and riding upon every lean camel, which are the emaciated camels. ﴿They will come from every deep, distant pass﴾ means: these lean camels will come from every deep pass, that is, from every distant road, place and path. It was also said: "they will come" (yatīna, feminine plural), using the plural because by "every lean camel" is meant the she-camels, and the word "kull" (every) carries the sense of plurality, which is why it was said "yatīna." Al-Farra' claimed that this is rare in the speech of the Arabs: "I passed by every man standing (qā'imīn)." He said: "and it is correct; and God's words ﴿and on lean camels they will come﴾ point to the soundness of its permissibility."

It is related that when God commanded Ibrahim, may God's blessings be upon him, to proclaim the Hajj, he stood upon his station (maqam) and called out: "O people, indeed God has prescribed for you the Hajj, so perform the Hajj to His Ancient House."

The manner of Ibrahim's proclamation has been disputed. Some of them said: he called out with it, as follows:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Ibrahim finished building the House, it was said to him: ﴿Proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾. He said: "My Lord, and will my voice reach?" He said: "Proclaim, and upon Me is the delivery." So Ibrahim called out: "O people, the Hajj to the Ancient House has been prescribed for you, so perform it." He said: "His voice was heard between the heaven and the earth. Do you not see people coming from the farthest parts of the earth, responding with the talbiyah?"

- Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl ibn Ghazwan al-Dabbi related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Ibrahim built the House, God revealed to him: "Proclaim among the people the Hajj." He said: Ibrahim said: "Indeed your Lord has taken a House, and has commanded you to perform its Hajj." So there responded to him whatever heard him of stone, tree, hillock, earth, or anything: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: Ibn Waqid related to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾: He said: Ibrahim, the friend of God, stood upon the stone and called out: "O people, the Hajj has been prescribed for you." So he made heard whoever was in the loins of men and the wombs of women, and there responded to him whoever believed and whom God had foreknown would perform the Hajj until the Day of Resurrection: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk."

- Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Proclaim among the people the Hajj; they will come to you on foot﴾. He said: It settled in the heart of every male and female.

- Ibn Humayd related to me, he said: Hakkam related to us, from 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When Ibrahim finished building the House, God revealed to him that he proclaim among the people the Hajj. He said: So he went out and called out among the people: "O people, indeed your Lord has taken a House, so perform its Hajj." Then no one heard him that day, of humankind, jinn, trees, hillocks, earth, mountains, water, or anything, except that it said: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk."

- Hakkam related to us, from 'Anbasa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Ibrahim stood upon the station when he was commanded to proclaim among the people the Hajj.

- Al-Qasim related to me, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾: He said: Ibrahim stood upon his station and said: "O people, respond to your Lord." They said: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk." So whoever performs Hajj today is among those who responded to Ibrahim on that day.

- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy related to us, from Dawud, from 'Ikrimah ibn Khalid al-Makhzumi, who said: When Ibrahim, peace be upon him, finished building the House, he stood upon the station and called out a call that the people of the earth heard: "Indeed your Lord has built for you a House, so perform its Hajj." Dawud said: "So I hope that whoever performs Hajj today is responding to Ibrahim, peace be upon him." [[The text of this last phrase appears thus in the original; perhaps its original form was: "So I hope that everyone who performs Hajj today, his Hajj is a response to Ibrahim's."]]

- Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz related to me, he said: Hajjaj related to us, he said: Hammad related to us, from Abu 'Asim al-Ghanawi, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Do you know how the talbiyah was?" I said: "And how was the talbiyah?" He said: When Ibrahim was commanded to proclaim among the people the Hajj, the mountains lowered their heads for him, and the towns were raised up, and he called out among the people.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾: Ibrahim said: "How shall I say it, my Lord?" He said: "Say: O people, respond to your Lord." He said: And it settled in the heart of every believer.

Others said concerning this, that:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Salamah, from Mujahid, who said: It was said to Ibrahim: "Proclaim among the people the Hajj." He said: "My Lord, how shall I say it?" He said: "Say: Labbayka Allahumma labbayk." He said: So that was the first talbiyah.

Ibn 'Abbas used to say: By "the people" in this place is meant: the people of the qiblah (the Muslims).

The narration for this: Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾: By "the people" is meant the people of the qiblah. Have you not heard that He said: ﴿Indeed the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed ... [up to His words] ... and whoever enters it is safe﴾ (3:96–97)? [He means:] whoever among mankind enters it, those among whom the proclamation was made and upon whom the Hajj was prescribed, is safe. So honour the sacred things of God, for they are of the piety of hearts.

As for His words ﴿They will come to you on foot and on every lean camel﴾, the people of interpretation said concerning it what we have said.

Al-Qasim related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿They will come to you on foot﴾ means: walking.

- He said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Arta'ah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "I have no regret over anything that escaped me except that I did not perform Hajj on foot. I heard God say: ﴿They will come to you on foot﴾."

- He said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Ibrahim and Isma'il performed Hajj walking.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿They will come to you on foot﴾, he said: upon their feet.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And on every lean camel﴾: He said: the camels.

- Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿And on every lean camel﴾: He said: the camels.

- Nasr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi related to me, he said: al-Muharibi related to us, from 'Umar ibn Dharr, who said: Mujahid said: "They used not to ride, so God revealed: ﴿They will come to you on foot and on every lean camel﴾." He said: So He commanded them to take provisions, and permitted them to ride and to trade.

* *

And His words ﴿from every deep, distant pass﴾:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿from every deep, distant pass﴾, meaning: from a distant place.

- Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿from every deep pass﴾: distant.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿deep pass﴾: a distant place.

- Al-Hasan related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, the same.

* *

And His words: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of the benefits mentioned by God in this place. Some of them said: they are trade and the benefits of this world.

Those who said this: Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam related to us, he said: 'Amr ibn 'Asim related to us, from Abu Razin, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾, he said: they are the markets.

- Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Abu Tumaylah related to us, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir ibn al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: trade.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Ahmad related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from 'Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Abu Razin, regarding His words ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾: he said: their markets.

- He said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Waqid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾, he said: trade.

- 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, he said: Ishaq informed us, from Sufyan, from Waqid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the same.

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Waqid, from Sa'id, the same.

- al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Sinan related to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Razin: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾, he said: the markets.

Others said: they are the reward in the Hereafter and trade in this world.

Those who said this: Ibn Bashshar and Suwar ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, both said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾, he said: trade, and what pleases God of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter.

- 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, he said: Ishaq related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

- 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, he said: Ishaq informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾: he said: the reward in the Hereafter and trade in this world.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

Others said: rather, they are pardon and forgiveness.

Those who said this: Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾, he said: pardon.

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Abu Tumaylah related to me, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali said: forgiveness.

The most correct of the sayings is the saying of the one who said: What is meant is: that they may witness benefits for themselves, from the deed that pleases God, and from trade. This is because God made general for them the benefits of everything that the season (mawsim) witnesses, and what comes to Makkah during the days of the season of benefits of this world and the Hereafter, and He did not specify any of those benefits for them by report or by reason. So it is general in the benefits described.

* *

And His words: ﴿and mention the name of Allah on known days over the beasts of livestock He has provided for them﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: that they may mention the name of God over the sacrificial animals and camels, cows and sheep He has provided for them, on known days, which, according to some of the people of interpretation, are the days of tashriq (the days after the Eid). According to others, they are the ten days. According to others: the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr) and the days of tashriq.

We have already mentioned the disagreement of the people of interpretation concerning this with the narrations, and we explained which is more correct among them in Surat al-Baqarah, so that suffices instead of repeating it in this place, though I will mention some of it here as well.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and mention the name of Allah on known days﴾: meaning the days of tashriq.

- I was told from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak regarding His words ﴿known days﴾: meaning the days of tashriq; ﴿over the beasts of livestock He has provided for them﴾: meaning the sacrificial animals.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿on known days﴾, he said: the ten days; and "the counted days" (al-ma'dudat): the days of tashriq.

* *

And His words: ﴿So eat from them﴾

He says: eat from the beasts of livestock over which you have mentioned the name of God, O people, there. This command from God, may His praise be exalted, is a command of permission, not a command of obligation, because there is no disagreement among all the proof that whoever slaughters his offering or his camel there, if he does not eat from his offering or his camel, he has not neglected any duty that was obligatory upon him; so it is known thereby that it is not obligatory.

Report from some of the scholars who said this: Suwar ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', regarding His words ﴿So eat from them and feed the miserable, the poor﴾: he said: He did not regard eating from them as obligatory.

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, he said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Husayn informed us, from Mujahid, that he said: It is a concession: if he wishes he eats, and if he wishes he does not eat, and it is like His words: ﴿And when you have come out of the state of ihram, then hunt﴾ (5:2) and ﴿And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse in the land﴾ (62:10). He means His words: ﴿So eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar﴾ (22:36).

- He said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, regarding His words ﴿So eat from them﴾: he said: It is a concession; if he wishes he eats, and if he wishes he does not eat.

- He said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Hajjaj informed us, from 'Ata', regarding His words ﴿So eat from them﴾: he said: It is a concession; if he wishes he eats, and if he wishes he does not eat.

- 'Ali ibn Sahl related to me, he said: Zayd related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Husayn, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿So eat from them﴾: he said: It is only a concession.

* *

And His words: ﴿and feed the miserable, the poor﴾

He says: and feed from what you slaughter or sacrifice there, from your offerings and camels, the miserable (ba'is), who is the one afflicted with the harm of hunger, disability and need; and the poor (faqir) is the one who has nothing.

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said concerning its interpretation.

Those who said this: Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His words ﴿So eat from them and feed the miserable, the poor﴾: meaning: the disabled poor.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from a man, from Mujahid: ﴿the miserable, the poor﴾: he who stretches out his hands to you.

- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿the miserable, the poor﴾: he is the one who is content (qani').

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Umar ibn 'Ata' informed me, from 'Ikrimah, who said: The miserable (ba'is): the one compelled, upon whom is misery; and the poor (faqir): the one who abstains (mutta'affif).

- He said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿the miserable﴾: he who extends his hands.

* *

And His words: ﴿then let them end their state of unkemptness﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: then let them complete what is incumbent upon them of the rites of their Hajj: shaving the hair, trimming the moustache, throwing the pebbles at the jamarat, and circumambulating the House.

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said concerning this.

Those who said this: Ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, he said: Yazid related to me, he said: al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar informed us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that he said: ﴿then let them end their state of unkemptness﴾: he said: what they are in the state of Hajj.

- Humayd ibn Mas'adah related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: al-Ash'ath related to me, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: Tafath: all the rites.

- He said: Hushaym related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Malik informed us, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said, regarding His words ﴿then let them end their state of unkemptness﴾: He said: Tafath: shaving the head, taking from the two moustaches, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, cutting the nails, taking from the sideburns, throwing the pebbles at the jamarat, and standing at 'Arafah and Muzdalifah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 27–29 (part 2 of 2):

• Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, who said: "al-tafath" is the hair and the nails.

• Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Khalid, from ʿIkrimah, the like of it.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Ṣakhr informed me, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, that he used to say concerning this verse: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾: the throwing of the pebbles (ramy al-jimar), the slaughtering of the sacrificial animal, the taking from the moustache, the beard and the nails, and the circumambulation of the House and of al-Safa and al-Marwah.

• Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujahid, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾. He said: It is shaving the head, and he mentioned other things of the Hajj. Shuʿbah said: I do not remember them.

• He said: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujahid, the like of it.

• Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾. He said: shaving the head, shaving the pubic area, clipping the nails, trimming the moustache, throwing the pebbles, and trimming the beard.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it, except that he did not say in his narration: and trimming the beard.

• Naṣr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥman al-Azdi narrated to me, saying: al-Muḥaribi narrated to us, saying: I heard a man asking Ibn Juraij about His saying: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾. He said: taking from the beard, from the moustache, cutting the nails, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic area, and throwing the pebbles.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Manṣur informed us, from al-Ḥasan, and Juwaybir informed us, from al-Ḍaḥḥak, that both of them said: shaving the head.

• I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say concerning His saying: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾: he means shaving the head.

• Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: al-tafath: shaving the head and clipping the nail.

• Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾. He says: their rites (nusuk).

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾: al-tafath: their sanctity (ḥurum).

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾. He said: By al-tafath is meant the removal of their state of ihram: shaving the head, wearing garments, clipping the nails, and the like.

• Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from ʿAṭaʾ ibn al-Sa’ib, who said: al-tafath: shaving the hair, clipping the nails, taking from the moustache, shaving the pubic area, and the whole matter of the Hajj.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And let them fulfil their vows﴾.
He says: and let them fulfil to Allah what they vowed of offerings, camels, and other things.
The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said.

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying: ﴿And let them fulfil their vows﴾: the slaughtering of the camels they vowed.

• Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And let them fulfil their vows﴾: the vow of the Hajj and the offering, and whatever a person vows of a thing that occurs in the Hajj.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: ﴿And let them fulfil their vows﴾. He said: the vow of the Hajj and the offering, and whatever a person vows upon himself of a thing that occurs in the Hajj.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾.
He says: and let them circumambulate the Sacred House of Allah.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of His saying: ﴿al-ʿatīq﴾ in this place. Some of them said: it is said of the Sacred House of Allah because Allah freed it (aʿtaqahu) from tyrants, so that they could not reach its destruction and demolition.

Mention of those who said that: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhri, that Ibn al-Zubayr said: The House was only named the Ancient House because Allah freed it from tyrants.

• al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Zubayr, the like of it.

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muʾammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: It was only named al-ʿAtīq because it was freed from tyrants.

• He said: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾. He said: It was freed from tyrants.

• Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His saying: ﴿the Ancient House﴾. He said: Allah freed it from tyrants, meaning the Kaʿbah.

Others said: It was called ʿatīq because no one of mankind has ever owned it.

Mention of those who said that: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muʾammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿUbayd, from Mujahid, who said: The Ancient House was only named so because no one has any claim over it.

Others said: It was named so for its antiquity.

Mention of those who said that: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿the Ancient House﴾: al-ʿatīq means the old, because it is old, as one says: an ancient sword, because it was the first house set down for mankind, built by Adam, and he was the first to build it; then Allah settled its place for Ibrahim after the Flood, and Ibrahim and Isma'il built it.

Abu Jaʿfar said: For all of these sayings which we have mentioned from those we have attributed them to, concerning His saying: ﴿the Ancient House﴾, there is a sound aspect; however, what Ibn Zayd said is the most apparent of its meanings. Yet what has been narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr is more worthy of soundness, if what:

• Muḥammad ibn Sahl al-Bukhari narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth informed me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥman ibn Khalid ibn Musafir, from al-Zuhri, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUrwah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The House was only named the Ancient House because Allah freed it from tyrants, so that it was never overcome by anyone."

• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: al-Zuhri said: We have been informed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The House was only named the Ancient House because Allah freed it," and then he mentioned the like of it.

By the circumambulation which Allah, may His praise be exalted, commanded the pilgrim to perform around His Ancient House in this verse is meant the circumambulation of ifadah, which is performed after the standing at ʿArafah, either on the Day of Sacrifice or after it; there is no disagreement among the people of interpretation about this.

Mention of the narration from some who said that: ʿAmr ibn Saʿid al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: al-Ansari narrated to us, from Ashʿath, from al-Ḥasan: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾. He said: the circumambulation of ziyarah.

• Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, saying: al-Ashʿath narrated to us, that al-Ḥasan said concerning His saying: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾: the obligatory circumambulation.

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾: meaning the visiting of the House.

• Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Ḥajjaj and ʿAbd al-Malik, from ʿAṭaʾ, concerning His saying: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾. He said: the circumambulation of the Day of Sacrifice.

• Abu ʿAbd al-Raḥman al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, saying: I asked Zuhayr about the saying of Allah: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾. He said: the circumambulation of farewell.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of these letters. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited "ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا تَفَثَهُمْ وَلْيُوفُوا نُذُورَهُمْ وَلْيَطَّوَّفُوا" with the lam quiescent (sukun) in all of them, seeking lightness, just as they did with huwa when preceded by a waw, so they said "وَهْوَ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ" and made the ha quiescent; and they do likewise with the lam of the imperative when preceded by one of the conjunctive particles such as waw, fa’ and thumma. The majority of the readers of Basra recited in the same way, except that Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla used to vocalize the lam with kasra in His saying: ﴿thumma l-yaqḍū﴾ specifically, because pausing on thumma without continuing to liyaqḍū is good, whereas pausing on the waw and the fa’ is not permissible. This reason which Abu ʿAmr gave for his reading is a good reason from the standpoint of analogy; nevertheless, most of the readers hold to its sukun.

The most correct of the sayings in this matter in my view is that the sukun in the lam of "liyaqḍū" and the kasra are two well-known recitations and two current dialects, so whichever one the reader recites is correct. However, the kasra in it specifically is more analogous, for the reason we have mentioned from Abu ʿAmr, because whoever recites "وَهْوَ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ" makes the ha quiescent after waw and fa’, but vocalizes it in His saying: ﴿thumma huwa yawma l-qiyāmati mina l-muḥḍarīn﴾. It is therefore obligatory for him to do the same in "thumma l-yaqḍū tafathahum", vocalizing the lam to kasra with thumma, even though he makes it quiescent in His saying: ﴿wa-l-yūfū nudhūrahum﴾. It has also been mentioned from Abu ʿAbd al-Raḥman al-Sulami and al-Ḥasan al-Basri that they vocalized it after thumma and waw, which is a well-known dialect; nevertheless, most readers hold to its sukun after waw and fa’, and it is the more famous and more eloquent of the two dialects among the Arabs, so reciting with it is more pleasing to me than with the kasra.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 27–29 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And proclaim to mankind the Hajj; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every deep, distant pass﴾ (22:27), ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah on known days over the beasts of livestock He has provided for them. So eat from them and feed the miserable, the poor﴾ (22:28), ﴿then let them end their state of unkemptness, fulfil their vows, and circumambulate the Ancient House﴾ (22:29).

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We also committed to him (Ibrahim) that he proclaim to mankind the Hajj. By His words ﴿And proclaim﴾ He means: inform and call out to mankind that they should perform the Hajj to the Sacred House of Allah, O people. ﴿They will come to you on foot﴾ means: people will come to the House you have been commanded to make Hajj to, walking on their feet. ﴿And on every lean camel﴾ means: and riding upon every lean camel, which are the emaciated camels. ﴿They will come from every deep, distant pass﴾ means: these lean camels will come from every deep pass, that is, from every distant road, place and path. It was also said: "they will come" (yatīna, feminine plural), using the plural because by "every lean camel" is meant the she-camels, and the word "kull" (every) carries the sense of plurality, which is why it was said "yatīna." Al-Farra' claimed that this is rare in the speech of the Arabs: "I passed by every man standing (qā'imīn)." He said: "and it is correct; and God's words ﴿and on lean camels they will come﴾ point to the soundness of its permissibility."

It is related that when God commanded Ibrahim, may God's blessings be upon him, to proclaim the Hajj, he stood upon his station (maqam) and called out: "O people, indeed God has prescribed for you the Hajj, so perform the Hajj to His Ancient House."

The manner of Ibrahim's proclamation has been disputed. Some of them said: he called out with it, as follows:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Ibrahim finished building the House, it was said to him: ﴿Proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾. He said: "My Lord, and will my voice reach?" He said: "Proclaim, and upon Me is the delivery." So Ibrahim called out: "O people, the Hajj to the Ancient House has been prescribed for you, so perform it." He said: "His voice was heard between the heaven and the earth. Do you not see people coming from the farthest parts of the earth, responding with the talbiyah?"

- Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl ibn Ghazwan al-Dabbi related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Ibrahim built the House, God revealed to him: "Proclaim among the people the Hajj." He said: Ibrahim said: "Indeed your Lord has taken a House, and has commanded you to perform its Hajj." So there responded to him whatever heard him of stone, tree, hillock, earth, or anything: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: Ibn Waqid related to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾: He said: Ibrahim, the friend of God, stood upon the stone and called out: "O people, the Hajj has been prescribed for you." So he made heard whoever was in the loins of men and the wombs of women, and there responded to him whoever believed and whom God had foreknown would perform the Hajj until the Day of Resurrection: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk."

- Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Proclaim among the people the Hajj; they will come to you on foot﴾. He said: It settled in the heart of every male and female.

- Ibn Humayd related to me, he said: Hakkam related to us, from 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When Ibrahim finished building the House, God revealed to him that he proclaim among the people the Hajj. He said: So he went out and called out among the people: "O people, indeed your Lord has taken a House, so perform its Hajj." Then no one heard him that day, of humankind, jinn, trees, hillocks, earth, mountains, water, or anything, except that it said: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk."

- Hakkam related to us, from 'Anbasa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Ibrahim stood upon the station when he was commanded to proclaim among the people the Hajj.

- Al-Qasim related to me, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾: He said: Ibrahim stood upon his station and said: "O people, respond to your Lord." They said: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk." So whoever performs Hajj today is among those who responded to Ibrahim on that day.

- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy related to us, from Dawud, from 'Ikrimah ibn Khalid al-Makhzumi, who said: When Ibrahim, peace be upon him, finished building the House, he stood upon the station and called out a call that the people of the earth heard: "Indeed your Lord has built for you a House, so perform its Hajj." Dawud said: "So I hope that whoever performs Hajj today is responding to Ibrahim, peace be upon him." [[The text of this last phrase appears thus in the original; perhaps its original form was: "So I hope that everyone who performs Hajj today, his Hajj is a response to Ibrahim's."]]

- Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz related to me, he said: Hajjaj related to us, he said: Hammad related to us, from Abu 'Asim al-Ghanawi, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Do you know how the talbiyah was?" I said: "And how was the talbiyah?" He said: When Ibrahim was commanded to proclaim among the people the Hajj, the mountains lowered their heads for him, and the towns were raised up, and he called out among the people.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾: Ibrahim said: "How shall I say it, my Lord?" He said: "Say: O people, respond to your Lord." He said: And it settled in the heart of every believer.

Others said concerning this, that:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Salamah, from Mujahid, who said: It was said to Ibrahim: "Proclaim among the people the Hajj." He said: "My Lord, how shall I say it?" He said: "Say: Labbayka Allahumma labbayk." He said: So that was the first talbiyah.

Ibn 'Abbas used to say: By "the people" in this place is meant: the people of the qiblah (the Muslims).

The narration for this: Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾: By "the people" is meant the people of the qiblah. Have you not heard that He said: ﴿Indeed the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed ... [up to His words] ... and whoever enters it is safe﴾ (3:96–97)? [He means:] whoever among mankind enters it, those among whom the proclamation was made and upon whom the Hajj was prescribed, is safe. So honour the sacred things of God, for they are of the piety of hearts.

As for His words ﴿They will come to you on foot and on every lean camel﴾, the people of interpretation said concerning it what we have said.

Al-Qasim related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿They will come to you on foot﴾ means: walking.

- He said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Arta'ah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "I have no regret over anything that escaped me except that I did not perform Hajj on foot. I heard God say: ﴿They will come to you on foot﴾."

- He said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Ibrahim and Isma'il performed Hajj walking.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿They will come to you on foot﴾, he said: upon their feet.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And on every lean camel﴾: He said: the camels.

- Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿And on every lean camel﴾: He said: the camels.

- Nasr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi related to me, he said: al-Muharibi related to us, from 'Umar ibn Dharr, who said: Mujahid said: "They used not to ride, so God revealed: ﴿They will come to you on foot and on every lean camel﴾." He said: So He commanded them to take provisions, and permitted them to ride and to trade.

* *

And His words ﴿from every deep, distant pass﴾:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿from every deep, distant pass﴾, meaning: from a distant place.

- Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿from every deep pass﴾: distant.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿deep pass﴾: a distant place.

- Al-Hasan related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, the same.

* *

And His words: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of the benefits mentioned by God in this place. Some of them said: they are trade and the benefits of this world.

Those who said this: Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam related to us, he said: 'Amr ibn 'Asim related to us, from Abu Razin, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾, he said: they are the markets.

- Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Abu Tumaylah related to us, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir ibn al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: trade.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Ahmad related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from 'Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Abu Razin, regarding His words ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾: he said: their markets.

- He said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Waqid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾, he said: trade.

- 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, he said: Ishaq informed us, from Sufyan, from Waqid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the same.

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Waqid, from Sa'id, the same.

- al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Sinan related to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Razin: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾, he said: the markets.

Others said: they are the reward in the Hereafter and trade in this world.

Those who said this: Ibn Bashshar and Suwar ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, both said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾, he said: trade, and what pleases God of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter.

- 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, he said: Ishaq related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

- 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, he said: Ishaq informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾: he said: the reward in the Hereafter and trade in this world.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

Others said: rather, they are pardon and forgiveness.

Those who said this: Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far: ﴿that they may witness benefits for themselves﴾, he said: pardon.

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Abu Tumaylah related to me, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali said: forgiveness.

The most correct of the sayings is the saying of the one who said: What is meant is: that they may witness benefits for themselves, from the deed that pleases God, and from trade. This is because God made general for them the benefits of everything that the season (mawsim) witnesses, and what comes to Makkah during the days of the season of benefits of this world and the Hereafter, and He did not specify any of those benefits for them by report or by reason. So it is general in the benefits described.

* *

And His words: ﴿and mention the name of Allah on known days over the beasts of livestock He has provided for them﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: that they may mention the name of God over the sacrificial animals and camels, cows and sheep He has provided for them, on known days, which, according to some of the people of interpretation, are the days of tashriq (the days after the Eid). According to others, they are the ten days. According to others: the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr) and the days of tashriq.

We have already mentioned the disagreement of the people of interpretation concerning this with the narrations, and we explained which is more correct among them in Surat al-Baqarah, so that suffices instead of repeating it in this place, though I will mention some of it here as well.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and mention the name of Allah on known days﴾: meaning the days of tashriq.

- I was told from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak regarding His words ﴿known days﴾: meaning the days of tashriq; ﴿over the beasts of livestock He has provided for them﴾: meaning the sacrificial animals.
