- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿on known days﴾, he said: the ten days; and "the counted days" (al-ma'dudat): the days of tashriq.

* *

And His words: ﴿So eat from them﴾

He says: eat from the beasts of livestock over which you have mentioned the name of God, O people, there. This command from God, may His praise be exalted, is a command of permission, not a command of obligation, because there is no disagreement among all the proof that whoever slaughters his offering or his camel there, if he does not eat from his offering or his camel, he has not neglected any duty that was obligatory upon him; so it is known thereby that it is not obligatory.

Report from some of the scholars who said this: Suwar ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', regarding His words ﴿So eat from them and feed the miserable, the poor﴾: he said: He did not regard eating from them as obligatory.

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, he said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Husayn informed us, from Mujahid, that he said: It is a concession: if he wishes he eats, and if he wishes he does not eat, and it is like His words: ﴿And when you have come out of the state of ihram, then hunt﴾ (5:2) and ﴿And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse in the land﴾ (62:10). He means His words: ﴿So eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar﴾ (22:36).

- He said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, regarding His words ﴿So eat from them﴾: he said: It is a concession; if he wishes he eats, and if he wishes he does not eat.

- He said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Hajjaj informed us, from 'Ata', regarding His words ﴿So eat from them﴾: he said: It is a concession; if he wishes he eats, and if he wishes he does not eat.

- 'Ali ibn Sahl related to me, he said: Zayd related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Husayn, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿So eat from them﴾: he said: It is only a concession.

* *

And His words: ﴿and feed the miserable, the poor﴾

He says: and feed from what you slaughter or sacrifice there, from your offerings and camels, the miserable (ba'is), who is the one afflicted with the harm of hunger, disability and need; and the poor (faqir) is the one who has nothing.

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said concerning its interpretation.

Those who said this: Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His words ﴿So eat from them and feed the miserable, the poor﴾: meaning: the disabled poor.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from a man, from Mujahid: ﴿the miserable, the poor﴾: he who stretches out his hands to you.

- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿the miserable, the poor﴾: he is the one who is content (qani').

- al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Umar ibn 'Ata' informed me, from 'Ikrimah, who said: The miserable (ba'is): the one compelled, upon whom is misery; and the poor (faqir): the one who abstains (mutta'affif).

- He said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿the miserable﴾: he who extends his hands.

* *

And His words: ﴿then let them end their state of unkemptness﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: then let them complete what is incumbent upon them of the rites of their Hajj: shaving the hair, trimming the moustache, throwing the pebbles at the jamarat, and circumambulating the House.

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said concerning this.

Those who said this: Ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, he said: Yazid related to me, he said: al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar informed us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that he said: ﴿then let them end their state of unkemptness﴾: he said: what they are in the state of Hajj.

- Humayd ibn Mas'adah related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: al-Ash'ath related to me, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: Tafath: all the rites.

- He said: Hushaym related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Malik informed us, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said, regarding His words ﴿then let them end their state of unkemptness﴾: He said: Tafath: shaving the head, taking from the two moustaches, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, cutting the nails, taking from the sideburns, throwing the pebbles at the jamarat, and standing at 'Arafah and Muzdalifah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 27–29 (part 2 of 2):

• Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, who said: "al-tafath" is the hair and the nails.

• Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Khalid, from ʿIkrimah, the like of it.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Ṣakhr informed me, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, that he used to say concerning this verse: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾: the throwing of the pebbles (ramy al-jimar), the slaughtering of the sacrificial animal, the taking from the moustache, the beard and the nails, and the circumambulation of the House and of al-Safa and al-Marwah.

• Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujahid, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾. He said: It is shaving the head, and he mentioned other things of the Hajj. Shuʿbah said: I do not remember them.

• He said: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujahid, the like of it.

• Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾. He said: shaving the head, shaving the pubic area, clipping the nails, trimming the moustache, throwing the pebbles, and trimming the beard.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it, except that he did not say in his narration: and trimming the beard.

• Naṣr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥman al-Azdi narrated to me, saying: al-Muḥaribi narrated to us, saying: I heard a man asking Ibn Juraij about His saying: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾. He said: taking from the beard, from the moustache, cutting the nails, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic area, and throwing the pebbles.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Manṣur informed us, from al-Ḥasan, and Juwaybir informed us, from al-Ḍaḥḥak, that both of them said: shaving the head.

• I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say concerning His saying: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾: he means shaving the head.

• Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: al-tafath: shaving the head and clipping the nail.

• Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾. He says: their rites (nusuk).

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾: al-tafath: their sanctity (ḥurum).

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying: ﴿Then let them end their unkemptness﴾. He said: By al-tafath is meant the removal of their state of ihram: shaving the head, wearing garments, clipping the nails, and the like.

• Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from ʿAṭaʾ ibn al-Sa’ib, who said: al-tafath: shaving the hair, clipping the nails, taking from the moustache, shaving the pubic area, and the whole matter of the Hajj.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And let them fulfil their vows﴾.
He says: and let them fulfil to Allah what they vowed of offerings, camels, and other things.
The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said.

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying: ﴿And let them fulfil their vows﴾: the slaughtering of the camels they vowed.

• Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And let them fulfil their vows﴾: the vow of the Hajj and the offering, and whatever a person vows of a thing that occurs in the Hajj.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: ﴿And let them fulfil their vows﴾. He said: the vow of the Hajj and the offering, and whatever a person vows upon himself of a thing that occurs in the Hajj.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾.
He says: and let them circumambulate the Sacred House of Allah.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of His saying: ﴿al-ʿatīq﴾ in this place. Some of them said: it is said of the Sacred House of Allah because Allah freed it (aʿtaqahu) from tyrants, so that they could not reach its destruction and demolition.

Mention of those who said that: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhri, that Ibn al-Zubayr said: The House was only named the Ancient House because Allah freed it from tyrants.

• al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Zubayr, the like of it.

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muʾammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: It was only named al-ʿAtīq because it was freed from tyrants.

• He said: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾. He said: It was freed from tyrants.

• Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa’ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His saying: ﴿the Ancient House﴾. He said: Allah freed it from tyrants, meaning the Kaʿbah.

Others said: It was called ʿatīq because no one of mankind has ever owned it.

Mention of those who said that: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muʾammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿUbayd, from Mujahid, who said: The Ancient House was only named so because no one has any claim over it.

Others said: It was named so for its antiquity.

Mention of those who said that: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿the Ancient House﴾: al-ʿatīq means the old, because it is old, as one says: an ancient sword, because it was the first house set down for mankind, built by Adam, and he was the first to build it; then Allah settled its place for Ibrahim after the Flood, and Ibrahim and Isma'il built it.

Abu Jaʿfar said: For all of these sayings which we have mentioned from those we have attributed them to, concerning His saying: ﴿the Ancient House﴾, there is a sound aspect; however, what Ibn Zayd said is the most apparent of its meanings. Yet what has been narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr is more worthy of soundness, if what:

• Muḥammad ibn Sahl al-Bukhari narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth informed me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥman ibn Khalid ibn Musafir, from al-Zuhri, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUrwah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The House was only named the Ancient House because Allah freed it from tyrants, so that it was never overcome by anyone."

• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: al-Zuhri said: We have been informed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The House was only named the Ancient House because Allah freed it," and then he mentioned the like of it.

By the circumambulation which Allah, may His praise be exalted, commanded the pilgrim to perform around His Ancient House in this verse is meant the circumambulation of ifadah, which is performed after the standing at ʿArafah, either on the Day of Sacrifice or after it; there is no disagreement among the people of interpretation about this.

Mention of the narration from some who said that: ʿAmr ibn Saʿid al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: al-Ansari narrated to us, from Ashʿath, from al-Ḥasan: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾. He said: the circumambulation of ziyarah.

• Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, saying: al-Ashʿath narrated to us, that al-Ḥasan said concerning His saying: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾: the obligatory circumambulation.

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾: meaning the visiting of the House.

• Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Ḥajjaj and ʿAbd al-Malik, from ʿAṭaʾ, concerning His saying: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾. He said: the circumambulation of the Day of Sacrifice.

• Abu ʿAbd al-Raḥman al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, saying: I asked Zuhayr about the saying of Allah: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾. He said: the circumambulation of farewell.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of these letters. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited "ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا تَفَثَهُمْ وَلْيُوفُوا نُذُورَهُمْ وَلْيَطَّوَّفُوا" with the lam quiescent (sukun) in all of them, seeking lightness, just as they did with huwa when preceded by a waw, so they said "وَهْوَ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ" and made the ha quiescent; and they do likewise with the lam of the imperative when preceded by one of the conjunctive particles such as waw, fa’ and thumma. The majority of the readers of Basra recited in the same way, except that Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla used to vocalize the lam with kasra in His saying: ﴿thumma l-yaqḍū﴾ specifically, because pausing on thumma without continuing to liyaqḍū is good, whereas pausing on the waw and the fa’ is not permissible. This reason which Abu ʿAmr gave for his reading is a good reason from the standpoint of analogy; nevertheless, most of the readers hold to its sukun.

The most correct of the sayings in this matter in my view is that the sukun in the lam of "liyaqḍū" and the kasra are two well-known recitations and two current dialects, so whichever one the reader recites is correct. However, the kasra in it specifically is more analogous, for the reason we have mentioned from Abu ʿAmr, because whoever recites "وَهْوَ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ" makes the ha quiescent after waw and fa’, but vocalizes it in His saying: ﴿thumma huwa yawma l-qiyāmati mina l-muḥḍarīn﴾. It is therefore obligatory for him to do the same in "thumma l-yaqḍū tafathahum", vocalizing the lam to kasra with thumma, even though he makes it quiescent in His saying: ﴿wa-l-yūfū nudhūrahum﴾. It has also been mentioned from Abu ʿAbd al-Raḥman al-Sulami and al-Ḥasan al-Basri that they vocalized it after thumma and waw, which is a well-known dialect; nevertheless, most readers hold to its sukun after waw and fa’, and it is the more famous and more eloquent of the two dialects among the Arabs, so reciting with it is more pleasing to me than with the kasra.

The Interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿That [is so]. And whoever honors the sacred rites of Allah, it is better for him with his Lord. And the grazing animals have been made lawful for you, except what is recited to you. So avoid the filth of the idols and avoid the word of falsehood﴾ (22:30).

The Exalted says, by His saying ﴿That﴾: this which He has commanded of the removal of the unkempt state (qada' al-tafath), the fulfilment of vows, and circumambulation of the Ancient House, is the obligation incumbent upon you, O people, in your pilgrimage. ﴿And whoever honors the sacred rites of Allah, it is better for him with his Lord﴾ means: whoever avoids what Allah has commanded him to avoid while in the state of ihram, out of glorification of the limits of Allah, refraining from violating them and from deeming them lawful, then it is better for him with his Lord in the Hereafter.

As follows:

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said, regarding His saying ﴿That, and whoever honors the sacred rites of Allah﴾: "The sacred rite (hurmah) is Makkah, the Hajj and the 'Umrah, and all that Allah has forbidden of His acts of disobedience."

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And whoever honors the sacred rites of Allah﴾: "The sacred rites are: the Sacred Mash'ar, the Sacred House, the Sacred Mosque, and the Sacred City; these are the sacred rites."

* * *

And His saying: ﴿And the grazing animals have been made lawful for you﴾

The Exalted says: Allah has made lawful for you, O people, the grazing animals, that you may eat them when you slaughter them properly; so He has not forbidden you any of them as bahirah, nor sa'ibah, nor wasilah, nor ham, nor what you have set aside from them for your gods. ﴿Except what is recited to you﴾ means: except what is recited to you in the Book of Allah, namely: carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, what has been dedicated to other than Allah, the strangled, the beaten to death, the fallen to death, the gored, what a beast of prey has eaten, and what is sacrificed on the altar stones (nusub); all of that is filth (rijs).

As follows:

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿except what is recited to you﴾, he said: "Except carrion, and what over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned."

* al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

* * *

And His saying: ﴿So avoid the filth of the idols﴾

It means: be wary of worshipping idols and of obeying Satan in their worship, for that is filth.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the like of what we have said regarding its interpretation.

Mention of those who said that: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿So avoid the filth of the idols﴾: The Exalted says: "So avoid obedience to Satan in the worship of idols."

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying ﴿the filth of the idols﴾: "The worship of idols."

* * *

And His saying: ﴿And avoid the word of falsehood﴾

The Exalted says: be wary of the speech of lying and of fabrication against Allah by your saying about the gods: ﴿We only worship them that they may bring us near to Allah in position﴾ (39:3), and your saying to the angels: they are the daughters of Allah, and similar speech; for that is lying, falsehood, and association with Allah.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the like of what we have said regarding that.

Mention of those who said that: Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying "the word of falsehood": "Lying."

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and avoid the word of falsehood, being upright for Allah, not associating others with Him﴾: meaning: fabrication against Allah and denial.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Wa'il ibn Rabi'ah, from 'Abd Allah, who said: "The false testimony is equated with shirk." And he recited: ﴿So avoid the filth of the idols and avoid the word of falsehood﴾.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Wa'il ibn Rabi'ah, who said: "False testimony was equated with shirk." Then he recited this verse: ﴿So avoid the filth of the idols and avoid the word of falsehood﴾.

* Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-'Usfuri narrated to us, from his father, from Khuraym ibn Fatik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "False testimony has been equated with associating partners with Allah," then he recited: ﴿So avoid the filth of the idols and avoid the word of falsehood﴾.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Sufyan al-'Usfuri, from Fatik ibn Fudalah, from Ayman ibn Khuraym, that the Prophet (ﷺ) stood up delivering a sermon and said: "O people, false testimony has been equated with associating partners with Allah," twice. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿So avoid the filth of the idols and avoid the word of falsehood﴾.

It is also permissible that it be intended: avoid that you, O people, become filthy through the idols by your worship of them.

If someone says: Are there among the idols any that are not filth, such that it is said: "avoid the filth of them"? It is said: all of them are filth. The meaning is not what you have understood; rather the meaning of the speech is: avoid the filth that comes from the idols, namely their worship. So what the Exalted commanded by His saying ﴿avoid the filth﴾ concerning them is to guard against worshipping them, and that worship is the filth, as Ibn 'Abbas said and as those whose statements we mentioned earlier have said.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 31:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Turning away from all false gods, devoted to God, not associating anything with Him. Whoever associates others with God, it is as though he had fallen from the sky and the birds snatched him away, or the wind hurled him down into a distant place.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: O people, avoid the worship of idols and the utterance of polytheism. Be upright before God in sincerely affirming His oneness, and in devoting obedience and worship to Him alone, exclusively and not to idols and images, not associating anything else with Him. Whoever associates anything other than God with God, his state of being far from guidance, from reaching the truth, and his ruin and his departure from his Lord, is like one who has fallen from the sky, so that the birds snatch him and he perishes, or the wind hurls him into a distant place (makan saḥīq), meaning from afar. This is from their saying: "God has removed him far away and destroyed him (asḥaqahu)." There are two forms: "the wind destroyed him (asḥaqathu al-rīḥ)" and "it crushed him (saḥaqathu)." From this comes the description of a tall palm tree as nakhla saḥūq. And from it is the saying of the poet:

"A neighbour of ours was with us, but a restless, skittish she-camel drove her away,
Hurrying along, covering the stages of her journey swiftly and straight."

[The verse is among what al-Azhari cited in his Tahdhib, transmitting it from his companion (Lisan al-Arab: saḥaqa). He said: al-saḥq is running that is beyond walking but short of full galloping. Al-Azhari recited: "A neighbour of ours was with us..." The verse. The qādhūra of the camels is the one that kneels to one side, shies away and resists being milked. Tasḥaqu means she presses on in her journey. The nawā is the movement from one place to another, or the direction a traveller takes, near or far. Qudum means she does not limp or bend. He means that his neighbour departed from him on a she-camel that pressed on in its journey, paying no heed to anything. The verse is evidence that saḥq means vigorous travel that goes beyond walking but falls short of running.]

It is also related as tasḥaqu. He says: Thus is the likeness of the one who associates others with God, in his distance from his Lord and from reaching the truth, like the distance of this one who has fallen from the sky to the earth, or like the destruction of those whom the birds snatched up among them in the air.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) said things similar to what we have said. 

Those who said this: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and it is as though he had fallen from the sky﴾: He said: This is a parable God struck for one who associates others with God, in his distance from guidance and his destruction, ﴿and the birds snatch him away, or the wind hurls him into a distant place﴾.

Al-Hasan related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, the same.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God: ﴿in a distant place﴾: He said: far away.

Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.

It has been said: ﴿the birds snatch him away﴾. Before it had been said: ﴿and it is as though he had fallen from the sky﴾. "Kharra" (fell) is a past-tense verb, and "takhtafuhu" (snatches him) is in the present (mustaqbal) form. So the present form has been conjoined to the past, as is done in His words: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and hinder [others] from the way of God﴾. I have already explained this there.

That is what I have mentioned to you, O people, and commanded you: avoiding the filth of idols and avoiding false speech, turning to God as people of pure faith (hunafa'), and glorifying the rites of God, which is choosing the finest camels for sacrifice and fattening them, and performing the rites of the Hajj as God, mighty is His praise, has commanded — it is part of the piety of your hearts.

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Layla, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And whoever glorifies the rites of God, indeed it is from the piety of the hearts﴾. He said: its magnification, its good selection, and its fattening.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And whoever glorifies the rites of God﴾. He said: the fattening and the magnifying.

And from him, from Anbasa, from Layth, from Mujahid, the like of it, except that he said: and the good selection.

Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, from Abu Bishr; and Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And whoever glorifies the rites of God﴾. He said: the magnifying of the camels, their fattening, and their good selection.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, who said: Standing at Arafat is among the rites of God, and at Jam'[[Jam': it is al-Muzdalifa.]] is among the rites of God, and throwing the pebbles is among the rites of God, and the camels are among the rites of God, and whoever glorifies them, then indeed it is from the rites of God, in His words: ﴿And whoever glorifies the rites of God﴾; so whoever glorifies them, then indeed it is from the piety of the hearts.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And whoever glorifies the rites of God﴾: The rites are the pebbles, and al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the rites of God, and al-Mash'ar al-Haram and al-Muzdalifa. He said: The rites enter the Sacred Precinct (haram); they are rites, and they are sacred.

The most correct of these sayings is that it should be said: God, dhikruhu, informed that glorifying His rites, which are what He has made as markers for His creatures in the rites of their pilgrimage, namely the places where He commanded them to perform what was obligatory upon them there, and the acts He obligated them to do in their Hajj, is from the piety of their hearts. He did not single out any part of that; so glorifying all of it is from the piety of the hearts, as He, mighty is His praise, said. And it is incumbent upon His believing servants to glorify all of it. He said: ﴿Indeed it is from the piety of the hearts﴾, and He used the feminine and did not say "indeed it is" (masculine), because what is intended is: indeed that glorification, together with avoiding the filth of idols, is from the piety of the hearts, just as He, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿Indeed your Lord after it is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. And by His words "indeed it is from the piety of the hearts" He meant: indeed it is from the trembling of hearts out of fear of God, and the true knowledge of His greatness and the sincere affirmation of His oneness.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 33:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term; then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House﴾ (33).

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of the benefits which God mentioned in this verse, and informed His servants that they are until an appointed term, in the same way as they differed concerning the meaning of the rites (sha'a'ir) which He mentioned, exalted is His praise, in His saying: ﴿And whoever honours the rites of God, indeed it is from the piety of hearts﴾. Those who said that by the rites is meant the camels (al-budn) said: the meaning is, "For you, O people, in the camels are benefits." Then those who said this statement also differed concerning the state in which they have benefits, and concerning the appointed term which He, mighty is His remembrance, mentioned: ﴿until an appointed term﴾. Some of them said: the state in which God, exalted is His praise, informed that they have benefits in it, is the state in which its owner has not made it obligatory, has not designated it as a camel for sacrifice, and has not garlanded it. They said: its benefits in this state are drinking its milk, riding its back, and what God provides them from its offspring and young. They said: the appointed term which He, exalted is His praise, informed is for His believing servants from it, is until they make it obligatory; so when they make it obligatory, that ends, and they have no share of that anymore.

Mention of those who said that:

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, concerning: ﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term﴾, he said: what has not been designated as a camel for sacrifice.

⁕ Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, he said: Ishaq ibn Yusuf informed us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term﴾, he said: riding, milk, and offspring; so when it is designated as a camel or an offering, all of that goes away.

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, concerning this verse: ﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term﴾, he said: for you are its backs, its milk, and its wool, until it becomes a camel for sacrifice.

⁕ He said: Ibn Adi narrated to us, he said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, with the like of it.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Ibn Abi Najih, and Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term﴾, he said: in its hair, its wool, and its milk, before you designate it as a camel for sacrifice.

⁕ He said: Harun ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his saying: ﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term﴾, he said: in the camels are their flesh, their milk, their hair, their wool, and their fleece, before they are designated as offerings.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it, and he added in it: and it is the appointed term.

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj informed us, from Ata, that he said concerning His saying: ﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term, then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House﴾, he said: benefits in their milk, their backs, and their wool, ﴿until an appointed term﴾, until they are garlanded.

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, the like of that.

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Ibn Ulayya said: I heard Ibn Abi Najih say concerning His saying: ﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term﴾, he said: until you make it an offering camel.

⁕ He said: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Qatada: ﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term﴾, he says: in its backs and its milk; so when it is garlanded, then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House.

Others, among those who said that the rites in His saying: ﴿And whoever honours the rites of God﴾ are the camels, and the pronoun in His saying: ﴿For you therein﴾ refers to the rites, and the meaning of His saying: ﴿For you therein are benefits﴾ is: for you in the rites which you honour for God there are benefits after you take them for God as camels or offerings, by riding their backs when you need that, and drinking their milk if you are compelled to it. They said: the appointed term which He, mighty is His praise, mentioned: ﴿until an appointed term﴾ is until they are slaughtered.

Mention of those who said that: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Ata: ﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term﴾, he said: it is the riding of the camels, and drinking their milk if one is in need.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ata ibn Abi Rabah said concerning His saying: ﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term﴾, he said: until they are slaughtered. He said: It is permitted for him to load upon it the one who is in need and the one stranded from necessity; the Prophet ﷺ used to command that when a camel is needed, its owner may load upon it and ride it, at the side of the one exhausted. I said to Ata: What? He said: the man on foot, the one stranded, and the one who follows; and if it gives birth, he may load its young upon it too, and he should not drink its milk except the surplus beyond its young; and if there is a surplus in its milk, let him drink it, whether he has offered it or has not offered it. As for those who said: the meaning of the rites in His saying: ﴿And whoever honours the rites of God﴾ is the rites of the Hajj, which are the places at which worship is performed for God, they also differed concerning the meaning of the benefits which God mentioned: ﴿For you therein are benefits﴾. Some of them said: the meaning is: for you in these rites which you honour there are benefits by your trade there, your selling and buying in its presence, and your marketing. And the appointed term: leaving the rites for other than them, and from the places at which worship is performed to what is other than them, according to the statement of some of them.

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sudda'i narrated to me, he said: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Dabbi, from Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Razin, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿For you therein are benefits﴾, he said: their markets, for He mentioned no benefits except for the world.

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, he said: Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, his saying: ﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term﴾, he said: and the appointed term: leaving it for another.

Others among them said: the benefits which God mentioned in this place are acting for God by what He commanded of the rites of the Hajj. They said: the appointed term is the end of the days of the Hajj in which worship is performed to God.

Mention of those who said that: Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term, then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House﴾, then he recited the saying of God: ﴿And whoever honours the rites of God, indeed it is from the piety of hearts﴾. For you in those rites are benefits until an appointed term; when those days pass, you will not see anyone coming to Arafat to stand there seeking reward, nor to Muzdalifah, nor to the stoning of the pillars; and they have set out from the lands for these days in which there are benefits, and their benefits are only until those days, and that is the appointed term; then their place of sacrifice, when those days end, is at the Ancient House.

Abu Ja'far said: We have already shown that the saying of God: ﴿And whoever honours the rites of God﴾ means: everything that is a deed or a place which God made a sign for the rites of the Hajj of His creation, since He, mighty is His praise, did not specify anything of that in a report or by reason. Since that is so, it is known that the meaning of His saying: ﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term﴾ is that in these rites there are benefits until an appointed term. So whatever of these rites is a camel and an offering, its benefits are for you from the time you own it until you make it obligatory as offerings and camels; and whatever of them is places at which worship is performed for God, its benefits are trade for God there and acting by what He commanded, until one departs from them; and whatever of them is times, in that God is obeyed by performing the deeds of the Hajj and seeking livelihood there by trade, until one circumambulates the House in some of them, or reaches the sacred precinct in some and departs from the sacred precinct in some.

He said: The interpreters whose differences we mentioned differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term﴾ in the interpretation of His saying: ﴿then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House﴾. Those who said the rites in this place means the camels said: the meaning is: then the place of sacrifice of the camels is until they reach Mecca, which is where the Ancient House is.

Mention of those who said that: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hushaym informed us, he said: Hajjaj informed us, from Ata: ﴿then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House﴾, to Mecca.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House﴾, meaning the place of sacrifice of the camels when they are designated, to the Ancient House.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, he said: ﴿Then its place of sacrifice﴾ when it is designated as an offering ﴿is at the Ancient House﴾, he said: the Ka'ba, which He freed from the tyrants. So these people directed the interpretation of that to the place of sacrifice of the camels and offerings which you have made obligatory, to the land of the sacred precinct, and said: by the Ancient House is meant the whole land of the sacred precinct. They said: and that is His saying: ﴿So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque﴾, and the intended meaning is the whole sacred precinct.

Others said: the meaning of that is: then your place of release, O people, from the rites of your Hajj is at the Ancient House, that you circumambulate it on the day of sacrifice after you have fulfilled what God made obligatory upon you in your Hajj.

Mention of those who said that: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, he said: Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa: ﴿then its place of release is at the Ancient House﴾, he said: the release of all these rites is the circumambulation of the House.

Others said: the meaning of that is: then the release of the benefits of the days of the Hajj is at the Ancient House by their ending.

Mention of those who said that: Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿then its place of release is at the Ancient House﴾: when those days, the days of the Hajj, end, [it is] at the Ancient House.

The most preferred of these sayings to me as correct is the saying of the one who said: the meaning of that is: then the release of the rites in which you have benefits until an appointed term is at the Ancient House; so whatever of that is an offering or a camel, then by its reaching the sacred precinct within the sacred precinct, and whatever of it is a rite, then circumambulation of the House.

We have already made clear the correct view in this matter in our explanation of the meaning of the rites.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 34:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And for every community We have appointed rites, that they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided for them of livestock animals. And your God is one God, so submit to Him. And give good tidings to the humble (al-mukhbitin)﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And for every community﴾, meaning for every congregation that preceded you among the people of faith in Allah, O people, We appointed a sacrifice (mansak), a slaughter whose blood they pour out, ﴿that they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided for them of livestock animals﴾, so the word "livestock" (bahimat al-an'am) is used because among beasts (bahima) there are those that are not of the livestock (al-an'am), such as horses, mules and donkeys. It has also been said that beasts were called bahima because they cannot speak.

Similar to what we have said in the interpretation of His words, ﴿We appointed a rite (mansak)﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said:

Those who said this: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And for every community We have appointed a rite﴾, he said: the shedding of blood ﴿that they may mention the name of Allah over them﴾.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So your God is one God﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So avoid the filth of idols, and avoid false speech, for your God is one God with no partner, so worship Him alone and devote the worship to Him alone.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So submit to Him﴾

He says: So submit in obedience to your God, and humble yourselves to Him by acknowledging servitude.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And give good tidings to the humble (al-mukhbitin)﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And give good tidings, O Muhammad, to those who submit to Allah in obedience, who yield to Him in servitude, and who turn to Him in repentance. We have already explained the meaning of ikhbat (humility) with its evidences earlier in this book.

The people of interpretation differed regarding what is meant by it in this place. Some of them said: it means, "give good tidings to those who are at peace in Allah."

Those who said this: Ibn Bashshar narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And give good tidings to the humble﴾, he said: the ones at peace (al-mutma'innin).

Abu Kurayb narrated to me, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And give good tidings to the humble﴾: those at peace in Allah.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And give good tidings to the humble﴾, he said: the ones at peace.

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And give good tidings to the humble﴾, he said: the humble (al-mutawadi'in).

Others said regarding this:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Uthman ibn Abd Allah ibn Aws, from Amr ibn Aws, who said: "The mukhbitun are those who do not wrong, and when they are wronged, they do not seek retribution."

Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Abd Allah ibn Aws narrated to me, from Amr ibn Aws, the like of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 35–36 (part 1 of 2):

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and those who are patient over what afflicts them, and those who establish prayer, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾

This is a description of the humble (al-mukhbitin). Allah, may He be remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And give good tidings, O Muhammad, to the humble (al-mukhbitin), whose hearts are humbled at the remembrance of Allah, and who submit out of fear of Him, trembling at His punishment and fearful of His wrath.

As related by:
- Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿Those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾: "Their hearts do not harden." ﴿And those who are patient over what afflicts them﴾: from hardship in the matter of Allah, and what harm they suffer in His cause. ﴿And those who establish prayer﴾: the obligatory prayer. ﴿And from what We have provided them they spend﴾: from wealth, in what it is obligatory for them to spend it upon: in zakat, in the maintenance of dependants and those whose maintenance is obligatory upon them, and in the way of Allah.

* *

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And the camels — We have made them for you as among the symbols of Allah. For you therein is good. So mention the name of Allah over them while they are lined up. Then when they fall on their sides, eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar. Thus We have subjected them to you that you may be grateful﴾

Allah, may He be remembered, says: "Wa-l-budn" is the plural of badanah, and it may be said of its singular: badan. When it is said badan, it may be both a plural and a singular. That it may be said of the singular is shown by the verse of the rajaz poet:

"Upon me, when I possess affairs, is a fast of months that became obligatory as vows,
and a shaved head, full and plaited, and a camel, armored and abundant."

[This is four lines of the rajaz meter, which the author related from al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an at this place of the tafsir, and he had earlier recited three of them at (7:120), at the explanation of His saying: (Then two others from among those who have a claim should stand in their place) in Surat al-Ma'idah, with some variation in wording from his narration here. The words are: "Upon me, when you possess the affairs..." and "...a camel, adorned and slaughtered." The word "badanan" in that narration may be correct, meaning a large, fat camel, as in Lisan al-Arab (b-d-n): a man is "badin," a woman "badin" or "badinah," and the plural is "badan" (with damma and sukun) and "badan" (with damma and a doubled dal). It may also be that "badanan" is a corruption of "badan" (with fatha), by the evidence of the author's rendering of it with his words "wa-l-budn" (with damma and sukun) as the plural of "badanah" (with fatha), and it is said of its singular "badan" (with fatha), which is shown by the poet's verse "wa-badanan mudarra'an mawfuran." End.
This is also supported by the words of Abu al-Baqa' al-'Ukbari in I'rab al-Qur'an: "al-budn" (with damma and sukun) is the plural of "badan" (with fatha), its singular being "badanah," like khashab (with damma and sukun) and khashab (with fatha). It is said to be the plural of "badanah," like thamarah and thamar (the latter with damma and sukun), and it is read with a damma on the dal. The "badanah," as in Lisan al-Arab (b-d-n), takes the ta' marbutah because of its size and fatness. End. The poet says: I obligated upon myself, when I possess the affairs, using the second person, that I fast months, shave my head, and slaughter a camel, meaning a huge camel.]

"Al-badan" is the large of everything, and for this reason Imru' al-Qays ibn al-Nu'man, the lord of al-Khawarnaq and al-Sadir, was called "al-badan," because of his bulk and the slackness of his flesh; it is said: "qad badna tabdeenan" (he has grown stout). So the meaning of the statement: and the camels, large of body and bulky, We have made them for you, O people, as among the symbols of Allah — that is, among the signs of the command of Allah which He has commanded you in the rites of your pilgrimage, when you garland them, adorn them with the marks of sacrifice, and mark them, so that it is known and recognized that you have done this with the camels and cattle.

As related by:
- Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Yahya related to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: 'Ata' said: ﴿And the camels — We have made them for you as among the symbols of Allah﴾: the cow and the camel.

* *

And His saying: ﴿For you therein is good﴾

That is: for you in the camels there is good. That good is reward in the Hereafter through slaughtering them and giving them in charity, and in this world: riding them when you are in need of riding them.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Among those who said that:
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿For you therein is good﴾: "Reward and benefits in the camels."
- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: ﴿For you therein is good﴾: "Milk and riding when one is in need."
- 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, from Sharik, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: ﴿For you therein is good﴾: "When you are compelled to your camel, ride it and drink its milk."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: ﴿For you therein is good﴾: "Whoever needs the back of the camel rides it, and whoever needs its milk drinks it."

* *

And His saying: ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them while they are lined up﴾

That is, He, may He be remembered, says: So mention the name of Allah over the camels at the time of slaughtering them, while they are lined up (ṣawāff).

The readers differed in the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of the regional centres recited ﴿ṣawāffa⁠﴾ (ṣawāff) meaning "lined up," its singular being ṣāffah, and it is said: "ṣaffat bayna yadayhā" (she was lined up before her). It is narrated from al-Hasan, Mujahid, Zayd ibn Aslam, and a group of others with them that they recited it "ṣawāfiya" with a ya', in the accusative, meaning: sincerely for Allah, having no partner in them, purely for Him.

And some of them recited it "ṣawāff," dropping the ya' and nunating the letter, after the pattern of 'iwar and 'awad. And it is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he recited it "ṣawāfinn," meaning: tied up (mu'aqqalah).

The correct recitation in my view is the recitation of the one who recited it with a doubled fa' and in the accusative, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it, with the meaning we have mentioned for the one who recited it thus.

Among those who interpreted it according to the reading with a doubled fa' and in the accusative:
- Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them while they are lined up﴾: He said: "Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, O Allah, from You and to You." "Ṣawāff": standing on three legs. It was said to Ibn 'Abbas: What do we do with their hides? He said: Give them in charity and benefit from them.
- Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam told me, saying: Ayyub ibn Suwayd related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: "ṣawāff": he said: standing. He said: "Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, O Allah, from You and to You."
- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them while they are lined up﴾: "Standing on three tied legs, in the name of Allah. Allahu akbar, O Allah, from You and to You."
- Ya'qub told me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿ṣawāff﴾: "Tied at one of its forelegs, standing on three legs."
- 'Ali told me, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them while they are lined up﴾: "Standing."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying: ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them while they are lined up﴾: "Ṣawāff": that one leg is tied and it is stood upon three, and it is slaughtered thus.
- Ya'qub related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Yu'la ibn 'Ata' informed us, saying: Bujayr ibn Salim informed us, saying: I saw Ibn 'Umar slaughtering his camel, and he said: "ṣawāff," as Allah said, and he slaughtered it while it was standing, tied at one of its forelegs.
- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Layth informed us, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-ṣawāff": when its leg is tied and it stands on three.
- Layth related to us, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them while they are lined up﴾: "Lined up between its ankles."
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿ṣawāff﴾: "Standing in lines, on three legs."
- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them while they are lined up﴾: "Standing between its hooves."
- Ibn al-Barqi related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Hilal, from Nafi', from 'Abd Allah: that he used to slaughter the camels while they were standing, facing the House, their forelegs lined up with the tethers. He said: These are what Allah mentioned: ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them while they are lined up﴾.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir told me, from Mansur, from a man, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: I said to him: the saying of Allah ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them while they are lined up﴾. He said: "When you want to slaughter the camel, slaughter it and say: Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, O Allah, from You and to You. Then name it and slaughter it." I said: Shall I say that for the sacrifice? He said: "And for the sacrifice."

Among those who interpreted it according to the reading "ṣawāfiya" with the ya':
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, from al-Hasan, that he said: "So mention the name of Allah over them, ṣawāfiya": he said: "Sincerely."
- He said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, who said: al-Hasan said: "ṣawāfiya": "Purely for Allah."
- al-Hasan related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, who said: al-Hasan said: "ṣawāfiya": "purely for Allah."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Shaqiq al-Dabbi: "So mention the name of Allah over them, ṣawāfiya": he said: "Pure."
- He said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Ayman ibn Nabil related to us, who said: I asked Tawus about His saying: "So mention the name of Allah over them, ṣawāfiya": he said: "Pure."
- Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: "So mention the name of Allah over them, ṣawāfiya": "Pure, without any partner, as the polytheists used to do, making for Allah and for their gods ṣawāfi, pure for Allah, the Exalted."

Among those who interpreted it according to the reading "ṣawāfina":
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "So mention the name of Allah over them, ṣawāfin": that is, tied, standing.
- al-Hasan related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "So mention the name of Allah over them, ṣawāfin": that is, tied, standing.
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: "Whoever recites it ṣawāfin says: tied. And whoever recites it ﴿ṣawāff⁠﴾ says: it lines up its feet between its forelegs."
- I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: "So mention the name of Allah over them, ṣawāff": meaning ṣawāfin, and the camel, when slaughtered, has one foreleg tied, so it stands on three, and thus it is slaughtered.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The explanation of the most correct of these sayings concerning His saying ﴿ṣawāff﴾ has already preceded: they are those lined up before their owners, with one of their legs tied.

* *

And His saying: ﴿So when they fall on their sides﴾

That is: when they fall and their sides come down to the ground after slaughter. ﴿Then eat from them﴾ — and it is from the expression: "wajabat al-shams" when the sun has set and falls for its setting. And from it is the saying of Aws ibn Hajar:

"Has the sun not been eclipsed, and the full moon, and the stars, for the fallen mountain?" [This is the verse of Aws ibn Hajar as the author said. "The mountain" here: he means by it a great man, and "al-wajib" is the one who died. It is said in Lisan al-Arab (w-j-b): "wajab al-rajul wajaban": he died. Qays ibn al-Khatim said describing a war which occurred between the Aws and the Khazraj on the day of Bu'ath, when the leader of Banu 'Awf and their commander persisted in fighting and forbade Banu 'Awf from peace until the first slain fell:
"Banu 'Awf obeyed a commander who forbade them peace, until the first fallen one."
And the verse of Aws ibn Hajar is evidence that His saying, the Exalted: "fa-idha wajabat junubuha" means: when they fall and their sides come down to the ground after slaughter, then eat from them. End.]. He means by "al-wajib": the fallen.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Among those who said that:
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿So when they fall on their sides﴾: "They fall to the ground."
- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, concerning His saying: ﴿So when they fall on their sides﴾: "When it has finished and been slaughtered."
- Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid: ﴿So when they fall﴾: "Slaughtered."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying: ﴿So when they fall on their sides﴾: "When it is slaughtered."
- Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿So when they fall on their sides﴾: "When they die."

* *

And His saying: ﴿So eat from them﴾

This is in the form of a command, but its meaning is permission and allowance. Allah says: When it is slaughtered and falls dead after slaughter, then its eating has become lawful for you, and it is not a command of obligation.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i used to say concerning this, as related to us: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, both saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: The polytheists would not eat from their slaughtered animals, so it was permitted for the Muslims, and they ate from them. Whoever wills eats, and whoever wills does not eat.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Husayn, from Mujahid, who said: If he wills he eats, and if he wills he does not eat. It is in the position of: ﴿And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt﴾.
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿So eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar﴾: he says: he eats from it and feeds.
- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Yunus informed us, from al-Hasan; Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim; Hajjaj informed us, from 'Ata'; and Husayn informed us, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿So eat from them﴾: "If he wills he eats, and if he wills he does not eat." Mujahid said: It is a concession, like His saying: ﴿Then when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land﴾, and like His saying: ﴿And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt﴾, and His saying: ﴿and feed the contented and the beggar﴾, meaning: feed from it the contented.

The people of interpretation differed concerning who is meant by "al-qani'" (the contented) and "al-mu'tarr" (the beggar). Some of them said: "al-qani'" is the one who is content with what is given to him or with what he has and does not ask, and "al-mu'tarr" is the one who presents himself to you so that you feed him from the meat without his asking.

Among those who said that:
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And feed the contented and the beggar﴾: he said: "The contented: the one who is self-sufficient with what you have given him while he is in his house, and the beggar: the one who presents himself to you and approaches you that you feed him from the meat without asking. These are the ones he was commanded to feed from the camels."
- Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "The contented: your neighbour who is content with what you have given him, and the beggar: the one who presents himself to you and does not ask you."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verses 35–36 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, on the authority of al-Qurazi, that he used to say about this verse: ﴿And feed the contented and the beggar﴾. "The contented (al-qani') is the one who is content with a little thing and is satisfied with it. The beggar (al-mu'tarr) is the one who passes by your side and does not ask anything; that is the beggar."

And others said: "The contented is the one who is content with what he has and does not ask. The beggar is the one who approaches you and asks you."

Mention of those who said that: Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿the contented and the beggar﴾: "He means the contented is the one who abstains (al-mutacaffif), and the beggar is the one who asks."

⁕ Ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, saying: Abd al-Wahid told us, saying: Khusayf told us, saying: I heard Mujahid say: "The contented: the people of Makkah. The beggar: the one who approaches you and asks you."

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Ata told us, on the authority of Khusayf, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Ka'b ibn Farukh told me, saying: I heard Qatada narrate, on the authority of Ikrima, regarding His saying ﴿the contented and the beggar﴾: "The contented: the one who sits in his house. The beggar: the one who asks."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Sa'id told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: "The contented: the abstaining one who sits in his house. The beggar: the one who approaches you and asks you."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: "The contented and the beggar. [He said:] The contented: the one who covets what is with you but does not ask you. The beggar: the one who approaches you and asks you."

⁕ Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman related to me, saying: al-Muharibi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid and Ibrahim, who both said: "The contented: the one who sits in his house. The beggar: the one who asks you."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Sa'id told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding the contented and the beggar, who said: "The contented: the one who is content with what is in his hands. The beggar: the one who approaches you. And both of them have a right upon you, O son of Adam."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding ﴿So eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar﴾: "The contented: the one who sits in his house. The beggar: the one who approaches you."

And others said: "The contented: he is the one who asks, and the beggar: he is the one who approaches you without asking."

Mention of those who said that: Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Yunus told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: "The contented: the one who comes to you in supplication and asks you. The beggar: the one who presents himself to you and does not ask you."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'ba told us, on the authority of Mansur ibn Zadhan, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding this verse ﴿and feed the contented and the beggar﴾, who said: "The contented: the one who is content. The beggar: the one who approaches you." He said: "And al-Kalbi said: The contented: the one who asks you; and the beggar: the one who approaches you, presenting himself and not asking you."

⁕ Nasr Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi related to me, saying: al-Muharibi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿and feed the contented and the beggar﴾, who said: "The contented: the one who asks you. The beggar: the one who presents himself to you."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The contented: the one who asks."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi related to me, saying: Ghalib told me, saying: Shurayk told me, on the authority of Furat al-Qazzaz, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying ﴿the contented﴾, who said: "He is the one who asks." Then he said: "Have you not heard the verse of al-Shammakh:

"The wealth of a man, when it sets him right, makes him rich
and keeps him from poverty, is more chaste than begging."

[[The line is by al-Shammakh ibn Dirar (Lisan al-Arab: q-n-'). He said: In the revelation: ﴿and feed the contented and the beggar﴾; so the contented is the one who asks, and the beggar is the one who presents himself without asking. Al-Shammakh said: "The wealth of a man..." meaning from asking people. Ibn al-Sikkit said: Some Arabs permit al-qunu' in the sense of qana'a (contentment), but the good Arabic usage is the first. It is also transmitted as "min al-kunu'," and al-kunu' means contraction and humbling oneself. It was also said: al-qani' is the asker; it was said: the abstainer; and each is suitable. The man is qani' and qanii'. Al-Farra' said: he is the one who asks you, and you give him before he asks. It was also said: al-qunu' is covetousness. The verb: qana, with a fatha, yaqna'u qunu'an, meaning he humbled himself in asking; it was also said: he asked. Mafaqira: the aspects of his poverty; it was said it is the plural of faqr on an irregular pattern, like al-mushabih and al-malamih. It may also be the plural of mufaqqira, the verbal noun of afqarahu, or the plural of mufaqqar (active participle).]]

He said: "From asking."

⁕ Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya told us, saying: Yunus informed us, on the authority of al-Hasan, that he said regarding His saying ﴿and feed the contented and the beggar﴾: "The contented: the one who comes to you in supplication and asks you. The beggar: the one who shows you his condition and presents himself to you without asking."

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hisham told us, saying: Mansur and Yunus informed us, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: "The contented: the asker. The beggar: the one who presents himself and does not ask."

⁕ Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ayyash informed me, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam said: "The contented: the one who asks people."

And others said: "The contented: the neighbour; the beggar: the one who approaches you from among the people."

Mention of those who said that: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris told us, saying: I heard Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: "The contented: your neighbour, even if he is rich. The beggar: the one who approaches you."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, who said: Mujahid said, regarding His saying ﴿and feed the contented and the beggar﴾: "The contented: your wealthy neighbour. The beggar: whoever approaches you from among the people."

⁕ Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Mughira informed us, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding His saying ﴿and feed the contented and the beggar﴾, that he said: "One of them is the asker, and the other is the neighbour."

And others said: "The contented: the wanderer (al-tawwaf); the beggar: the visiting friend."

Mention of those who said that: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam related to me, saying: My father and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth told me, on the authority of al-Layth, on the authority of Khalid ibn Yazid, on the authority of Ibn Abi Hilal, who said: Zayd ibn Aslam said, regarding the words of God Almighty ﴿the contented and the beggar﴾: "The contented: the poor man who goes around (from door to door). The beggar: the friend and the weak person who visits."

And others said: "The contented: the covetous; the beggar: the one who comes to you with his body (in need of the meat)."

Mention of those who said that: Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿the contented﴾: "The covetous. And the beggar: the one who comes to you with his body, whether rich or poor."

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Umar ibn Ata informed me, on the authority of Ikrima, who said: "The contented: the covetous."

And others said: "The contented: he is the destitute, and the beggar: the one who comes to the meat."

Mention of those who said that: Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and feed the contented and the beggar﴾: "The contented: the destitute. The beggar: the one who comes to a people for their meat, and he is not destitute, and he has no sacrificial animal; he comes to the people for the sake of their meat. And the wretched poor man: he is the contented."

And others said, with what Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Furat, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The contented: the one who is content. The beggar: the one who approaches you."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Hasan, the same.

⁕ He said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim and Mujahid, regarding ﴿the contented and the beggar﴾: "The contented: the one who sits in his house. The beggar: the one who presents himself to you."

The most correct of these opinions is the view of the one who said: what is meant by the contented is the asker. For if what was meant by "the contented" in this place were the one who is satisfied with what he has and is self-sufficient, it would have been said: "and feed the contented and the asker," not "and feed the contented and the beggar." Following it with His words "and the beggar" is clear proof that the contented means the asker, from the expression qana'a fulan ila fulan, meaning he asked him and humbled himself before him; he qan'a qunu'an. From this is the verse of Labid:

"The master gave me when I was in poverty,
when he said: 'Look at my need and my humbling (qunu'i).'"

[[The line is by Labid, as the author said; I did not find it in his diwan in the Leiden edition of 1891. Al-khulla with a fatha means need and poverty. Al-Lihyani said: khulla bihi shadida, meaning destitution. Al-qunu' means asking; we have explained it in the preceding witness.]]

As for the contented in the sense of the self-sufficient, it comes from qanit (with the nun vowelled with a kasra), aqna'u, qana'atan, qan'an, and qan'anan. As for the beggar (al-mu'tarr), he is the one who comes to you presenting himself as needy of you, so that you give him and feed him.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Thus We have subjected them to you﴾: it means: "Thus We have subjected the camels to you, O people, so that you may give thanks to Me for subjecting them to you."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 35–36 (part 1 of 2):

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and those who are patient over what afflicts them, and those who establish prayer, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾

This is a description of the humble (al-mukhbitin). Allah, may He be remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And give good tidings, O Muhammad, to the humble (al-mukhbitin), whose hearts are humbled at the remembrance of Allah, and who submit out of fear of Him, trembling at His punishment and fearful of His wrath.

As related by:
- Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿Those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾: "Their hearts do not harden." ﴿And those who are patient over what afflicts them﴾: from hardship in the matter of Allah, and what harm they suffer in His cause. ﴿And those who establish prayer﴾: the obligatory prayer. ﴿And from what We have provided them they spend﴾: from wealth, in what it is obligatory for them to spend it upon: in zakat, in the maintenance of dependants and those whose maintenance is obligatory upon them, and in the way of Allah.

* *

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And the camels — We have made them for you as among the symbols of Allah. For you therein is good.
