He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to the idolaters of your people who dispute with you about God without knowledge, following every rebellious devil: ﴿O mankind, I am only a clear warner to you﴾ — I warn you of God's punishment descending upon you in this world, and of His torment in the Hereafter that you will burn in, clearly; meaning: I make my warning to you plain and manifest, so that you may repent of your polytheism and beware of what I warn you of. I have no power over anything for you beyond that. As for hastening or delaying the punishment with which you urge me, that rests with God, not with me, and I have no power over it. Then He described his warning and his good tidings, though no mention of good tidings had preceded; and since the warning was mentioned with a specific action, it is understood that the good tidings are its opposite. So He said: those who believed in God and His Messenger and did righteous deeds, among you, O people, and among others — ﴿for them is forgiveness﴾ — meaning: for them, from God, is the covering of the sins they committed in this world, so that they are concealed from them in the Hereafter; ﴿and noble provision﴾ — meaning: a goodly provision in Paradise.

As related:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding His words: ﴿So those who believed and did righteous deeds — for them is forgiveness and noble provision﴾ — he said: Paradise.

* *

And His words: ﴿And those who strove against Our signs, seeking to frustrate [them]﴾

Meaning: those who worked against Our proofs, turning people away from following Our Messenger and from acknowledging Our Book which We sent down. He said "against Our signs," and the preposition "fi" (in/against) is used here as in the expression "so-and-so strove in the matter of so-and-so."

The exegetes differed on the interpretation of His words ﴿mu'ajjizin﴾ (seeking to frustrate). Some of them said: its meaning is "opposing" (mushaqqin).

Those who said this: Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Uthman ibn 'Ata', from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he recited it as ﴿mu'ajizin﴾ throughout the Qur'an, meaning with an alif, and said: opposing.

Others said: rather, the meaning is that they thought they could overcome God, so that He could not prevail over them.

Those who said this: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿against Our signs, seeking to frustrate﴾ — he said: they denied God's signs and thought they could overcome God, but they will never overcome Him.

⁕ al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, the like of it.

These two interpretations are based on the reading of those who recite it ﴿mu'ajizin﴾ with an alif, which is the common reading of the reciters of Medina and Kufa. As for some reciters of Mecca and Basra, they read it "mu'ajjizin" with a doubled jim and without an alif, meaning that they rendered people incapable and deterred them from following the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and believing in the Qur'an.

Those who interpreted it in accordance with this reading: Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words "mu'ajjizin," he said: those who slow people down, slowing them from following the Prophet (ﷺ).

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

The correct position on this matter is to say that both are well-known readings, each recited by scholars among the reciters, and their meanings are close. For whoever is incapable regarding God's signs has effectively been incapable before God, and to strive against God is to render people incapable of God's signs and to act in disobedience to Him and in opposition to His command. The people about whom these verses were revealed were of the kind who slowed people down from faith in God and following His Messenger, and who contended against the Messenger of God (ﷺ), supposing that they could frustrate and overcome him, while God had guaranteed him victory over them; that was their striving against God. Given this, whichever of the two readings the reciter uses, he is correct.

As for "mu'ajaza," it is the form of mufa'ala from "ajz" (incapacity), and its meaning is the contest of two parties, each seeking to render the other incapable, so that one overcomes and subdues the other.

As for "ta'jiz," it is the intensive form, the tafil form of "ajz."

* *

And His words: ﴿Those are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾

Meaning: those who have this description are the inhabitants of Hell on the Day of Resurrection, and its people who are its rightful people.

**Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he spoke Satan cast into his wish. But Allah abolishes what Satan casts, then Allah makes His verses firm. And Allah is Knowing, Wise.﴾ (22:52)**

It has been said: The reason this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was that Satan had cast onto his tongue, in some of what he recited of the Qur'an that Allah had sent down to him, something Allah had not sent down. This grieved the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and troubled him, so Allah consoled him regarding what he was experiencing through these verses.

Mention of those who said this: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat in one of the assemblies of Quraysh, whose people were numerous. He wished on that day that nothing would come to him from Allah that would cause them to flee from him. So Allah revealed to him: ﴿By the star when it sets, your companion has not strayed, nor has he erred﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it until he reached: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾. Then Satan cast upon him two phrases: "Those are the exalted cranes (gharaniq), and their intercession is to be hoped for." He spoke them. Then he went on and recited the entire surah. He prostrated at the end of the surah, and all the people prostrated with him. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughira raised a handful of dust to his forehead and prostrated upon it, for he was an elderly man who could not prostrate. They were pleased with what he had spoken and said: "We know that Allah gives life and causes death, and He is the Creator and the Provider, but these gods of ours intercede for us with Him, since you have given them a share, so we are with you." They said: When evening came, Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and presented the surah to him. When he reached the two phrases that Satan had cast upon him, he said: "I did not bring you these two." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have fabricated against Allah and said about Allah what He did not say." Then Allah revealed to him: ﴿And indeed they almost tempted you away from that which We revealed to you, to fabricate against Us other than it; and then they would have taken you as a friend. And had We not strengthened you, you might have inclined to them a little. Then We would have made you taste double in life and double in death. Then you would not find for yourself against Us any helper﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Then you would not find for yourself against Us any helper﴾. He remained grieved and troubled until this was revealed to him: ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he spoke Satan cast into his wish. But Allah abolishes what Satan casts, then Allah makes His verses firm. And Allah is Knowing, Wise.﴾ He said: The Muslims who were in the land of Abyssinia heard that the people of Mecca had all accepted Islam, so they returned to their clans and said: "They are dearer to us." They found the people had reverted after Allah abolished what Satan had cast.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ziyad al-Madani, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw his people turn away from him, and it grieved him to see their distance from what he had brought them from Allah, he wished within himself that something would come to him from Allah that would bring him and his people closer together. He loved them and was eager for them, and he was pleased that some of what had been harsh upon him in their affair would be softened for him, when he spoke this to himself and wished it and desired it. So Allah revealed: ﴿By the star when it sets, your companion has not strayed, nor has he erred﴾. When he reached the words of Allah: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾, Satan cast upon his tongue, because of what he was saying to himself and wishing that his people would come to it: "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be approved." When Quraysh heard that, they rejoiced and were pleased, and they were delighted by the mention of their gods, so they gave ear to it. The believers trusted their Prophet in what he had brought them from their Lord and did not accuse him of error, mistake, or slip. When he reached the prostration in it and concluded the surah, he prostrated, and the Muslims prostrated with the prostration of their Prophet, affirming what he had brought and following his command. The polytheists in the mosque, from Quraysh and others, prostrated when they heard the mention of their gods. None remained in the mosque, believer or unbeliever, but prostrated, except al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, for he was an elderly man and could not. So he took a handful of gravel from al-Batha' and prostrated upon it. Then the people dispersed from the mosque, and Quraysh went out, pleased with what they had heard of the mention of their gods, saying: "Muhammad has mentioned our gods in the best manner, and he has claimed in what he recites that they are the exalted cranes, and that their intercession is approved." The prostration reached those in the land of Abyssinia from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it was said that Quraysh had accepted Islam. Some men rose up from among them, and others remained behind. Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, what have you done? You have recited to the people what I did not bring you from Allah, and you said what was not said to you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was saddened at that and feared Allah with a great fear. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to him: ﴿And He was ever Merciful to the believers﴾, consoling him and easing the matter for him, and informing him that there was no messenger or prophet before him who wished as he wished or loved as he loved, except that Satan cast into his wish, just as he had cast onto the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ. Allah abolished what Satan cast and made His verses firm. That is, you are like some of the prophets and messengers. Then Allah revealed: ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he spoke Satan cast into his wish﴾ ... the verse. So Allah removed grief from His Prophet and granted him security from what he had feared, and abolished what Satan had cast upon his tongue of the mention of their gods, that they are the exalted cranes and that their intercession is approved. Allah says, when He mentioned al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other, up to His saying: ﴿And how many angels are there in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all, except after Allah gives permission to whom He wills and approves﴾, meaning: how then can the intercession of your gods be considered with Him? When there came to him from Allah what abolished what Satan had cast upon the tongue of His Prophet, Quraysh said: "Muhammad has regretted what he said about the status of your gods with Allah. He has changed it and brought something else." Those two phrases that Satan had cast upon the tongue of His messenger had fallen into the mouth of every polytheist, so they increased in evil beyond what they had been upon.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: I heard Dawud, from Abu al-Aliya, who said: Quraysh said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Your companions are only the slave of such-and-such a clan and the freedman of such-and-such a clan. If you mentioned our gods with something, we would sit with you, for the nobles of the Arabs will come to you, and when they see your companions are the nobles of your people, it will be more desirable for them regarding you." He said: Satan cast into his wish, and this verse was revealed: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾. He said: Satan made to flow upon his tongue: "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is hoped for; their like is not forgotten." He said: The Prophet prostrated when he recited it, and the Muslims and the polytheists prostrated with him. When he learned of what had been made to flow upon his tongue, it grieved him greatly, so Allah revealed: ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he spoke Satan cast into his wish﴾ ... up to His saying: ﴿And Allah is Knowing, Wise﴾.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu al-Aliya, who said: Quraysh said: "O Muhammad, only the poor, the needy, and the weak of the people sit with you. If you mentioned our gods with good, we would sit with you, for the people come to you from every horizon." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited Surah al-Najm. When he reached this verse: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾, Satan cast upon his tongue: "And they are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is hoped for." When he finished it, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated, and the Muslims and the polytheists prostrated, except Abu Uhayha Sa'id ibn al-As, who took a handful of dust and prostrated upon it, and said: "It is time for the son of Abi Kabsha to mention our gods with good." Then it reached the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among the Muslims who were in Abyssinia that Quraysh had accepted Islam. What Satan had cast upon the tongue of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ weighed heavily upon him, so Allah revealed: ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he spoke Satan cast into his wish﴾ ... to the end of the verse.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it and said: "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is indeed to be hoped for." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated. The polytheists said: "He has not mentioned our gods with good before today," so the polytheists prostrated with him. Then Allah revealed: ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he spoke Satan cast into his wish﴾ ... up to His saying: ﴿the punishment of a barren day﴾.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad narrated to me, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza﴾, then he mentioned something similar.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he spoke Satan cast into his wish﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And Allah is Knowing, Wise﴾. That was because the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, while he was praying, had the account of the gods of the Arabs revealed to him, and he began to recite it. The polytheists heard him and said: "We hear him mentioning our gods with good." They drew near to him, and while he was reciting and saying: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾, Satan cast: "Indeed, those are the exalted cranes, from them the intercession is to be hoped for." He began to recite it, and Jibril (peace be upon him) came down and abrogated it, then said to him: ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he spoke Satan cast into his wish﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And Allah is Knowing, Wise﴾.

It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet﴾ ... the verse: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, while he was in Mecca, had the account of the gods of the Arabs revealed to him, and he began to recite al-Lat and al-'Uzza and repeat them often. The people of Mecca heard the Prophet of Allah mentioning their gods and rejoiced at that, and drew near to listen. So Satan cast into the recitation of the Prophet ﷺ: "Those are the exalted cranes, from them the intercession is to be hoped for." The Prophet ﷺ recited it that way, and Allah revealed to him: ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet﴾ up to: ﴿And Allah is Knowing, Wise﴾.

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that he was asked about the words: ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet﴾ ... the verse. Ibn Shihab said: Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith told me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while in Mecca, recited to them: ﴿By the star when it sets﴾. When he reached: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾, he said: "Indeed their intercession is to be hoped for." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ erred, and the polytheists whose hearts had disease met him, greeted him, and rejoiced at that. He said to them: "That was only from Satan." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet﴾ ... until He reached: ﴿then Allah abolishes what Satan casts﴾.

The meaning of the statement is: O Muhammad, We did not send before you any messenger to a nation of the nations, nor any prophet who was not a messenger, except that when he wished (tamanna)...

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) differed regarding the meaning of His saying "tamanna" (wished) in this place. I have mentioned the view of a group who said that this wishing from the Prophet ﷺ was that:

- something occurred to his soul out of love for his people to draw near to them in the mention of their gods with some of what they love, and whoever said this said that it was out of his love, in some circumstances, that they not be mentioned with evil.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: when he recited, or recounted, or spoke.

Mention of those who said that: Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿when he wished, Satan cast into his wish﴾, he said: when he spoke, Satan cast into his speech.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿when he wished﴾, he said: when he said.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿except when he wished﴾, that by wishing is meant recitation and reading.

This view is closer to the meaning of the statement, by the evidence of His words: ﴿then Allah abolishes what Satan casts, then Allah makes His verses firm﴾, for the verses which Allah, His praise be exalted, informed that He makes firm are without doubt verses of His revelation. It is known that what Satan cast into is what Allah, the Exalted, informed was abolished and nullified from it (naskh, abrogation or nullification), and then made firm by the abrogation of it.

So the meaning of the statement is: We did not send before you, O Muhammad, any messenger or prophet except that when he recited the Book of Allah and read, or spoke and related, Satan cast into the Book of Allah that he recited and read, or into his speech that he related and spoke. ﴿Then Allah abolishes what Satan casts﴾: He says, may He be exalted, that Allah removes what Satan casts of that upon the tongue of His Prophet and nullifies it.

As:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Then Allah abolishes what Satan casts﴾, meaning Allah nullifies what Satan cast.

- It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿Then Allah abolishes what Satan casts﴾: Jibril, by Allah's command, abrogated what Satan had cast upon the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah made His verses firm.

* *

And His saying: ﴿then Allah makes His verses firm﴾.

He says: Then Allah purifies the verses of His Book from the falsehood that Satan cast upon the tongue of His Prophet. ﴿And Allah is Knowing, Wise﴾ regarding what occurs in His creation of every occurrence, nothing of which is hidden from Him. ﴿Wise﴾ in His management of them and His turning of them as He wills and loves.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease and whose hearts are hardened, and indeed the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension﴾ (22:53).

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Then God abrogates what Satan casts, then God makes His verses firm, so that He may make what Satan casts into the wish of His Prophet of falsehood, like the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Those are the exalted cranes, and indeed their intercession is to be hoped for." A trial: that is, a test by which He tests those in whose hearts is a disease of hypocrisy, and that is doubt about the truthfulness of the Messenger of God ﷺ and the reality of what he informs them of.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the like of what we have said about this.

Those who said that: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: that the Prophet ﷺ used to wish that God would not disparage the gods of the polytheists. So Satan cast into his wish, and he said: "Indeed the gods that you claim, their intercession is to be hoped for, and indeed they are the exalted cranes." Then God abrogated that, and God made His verses firm: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza?﴾ until ﴿any authority﴾. Qatadah said: When Satan cast what he cast, the polytheists said: "He has mentioned their gods with good," and they rejoiced at that. So He mentioned His saying: ﴿That He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾.

al-Hasan related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, with the like of it.

al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿That He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, he says: "And for those whose hearts have hardened [[His saying: "And for those whose hearts have hardened": an conjunction upon what is implied from the context, meaning for those in whose hearts is a disease, and those whose hearts have hardened.]] from belief in God, so they do not soften nor refrain, and they are the polytheists of God."

The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.

Those who said that: al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿And those whose hearts have hardened﴾, he said: the polytheists.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And indeed the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: And indeed the polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, are in opposition to God in His command, far from the truth.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 22, verses 54–55**

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, so that they believe in it and their hearts humble themselves to it. Indeed, Allah is the guide of those who believe to a straight path.﴾ (22:54)

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: And so that those with knowledge of God may know that what Allah has sent down from His verses, which He made firm for His Messenger, and abrogated what Satan had cast into it, is the truth from your Lord, O Muhammad. That is, they may affirm it. That is, their hearts may submit to the Qur'an and yield in acknowledging it and affirming what is in it.

And indeed Allah guides those who believe in Allah and His Messenger to the right and direct path, and to the clear truth, by abrogating what Satan cast into the wish of His Messenger, so that the plotting of Satan and his casting of falsehood upon the tongue of their Prophet does not harm them.

And those of the people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:
Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord﴾: He said: It means the Qur'an.

* *

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it until the Hour comes upon them suddenly or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day.﴾ (22:55)

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Those who disbelieved in Allah will not cease to be in doubt.

Then the people of ta'wil differed regarding the pronoun in His words "minhu" (about it): what does it refer to? Some of them said: it refers to the statement of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for."

Mention of those who said that: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it﴾: from his saying: "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for."

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it﴾: "From what Iblis brought; it does not leave their hearts, and it increased them in misguidance."

And others said: Rather, it refers to the Prophet's (ﷺ) prostration at the Surah of the Star (al-Najm).

Mention of those who said that: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it﴾: He said: "In doubt about your prostration."

And others said: Rather, it refers to the Qur'an.

Mention of those who said that: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it﴾: He said: "From the Qur'an."

The most correct of these opinions regarding this matter is the view of the one who said: it is a pronoun referring to the Qur'an whose verses Allah made firm. This is because its reference to His saying ﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord﴾ is closer than its reference to His saying ﴿Then Allah abrogates what Satan casts﴾. The pronoun in His saying "annahu" (that it) refers to the Qur'an. Therefore, attaching the pronoun in His saying ﴿in doubt about it﴾ to the pronoun in His saying ﴿that it is the truth from your Lord﴾ is more appropriate than attaching it to "ma" in His saying ﴿what Satan casts﴾, given the distance between them.

* *

And His saying: ﴿until the Hour comes upon them﴾

He says: These disbelievers will not cease to be in doubt about the matter of this Qur'an until the Hour comes upon them ﴿suddenly﴾. It is the hour when people are gathered for the standing of reckoning, coming suddenly, that is, unexpectedly.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding which day this is. Some of them said: It is the Day of Resurrection.

Mention of those who said that: Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: a shaykh from the people of Khurasan, from the Azd, known as Abu Sasan, narrated to us, saying: I asked al-Dahhak about His saying ﴿the punishment of a barren day﴾, and he said: "The punishment of a day with no night after it."

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir, from 'Ikrimah, that the Day of Resurrection has no night.

And others said: Rather, it refers to the Day of Badr. They said: It was only called a "barren day" because they did not see the night, so it was barren for them.

Mention of those who said that: Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: ﴿the punishment of a barren day﴾: the Day of Badr.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day﴾: Ibn Jurayj said: "A day in which there is no night; they did not look to the night." Mujahid said: "The punishment of a great day."

⁕ He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir, who said: Mujahid said: "The Day of Badr."

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Idris narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash informed us, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying ﴿the punishment of a barren day﴾: He said: "The Day of Badr."

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿the punishment of a barren day﴾: He said: "It is the Day of Badr." He attributed this to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿the punishment of a barren day﴾: He said: "It is the Day of Badr," from Ubayy ibn Ka'b.

This second opinion is closer to the interpretation of the verse, because there is no sense in saying: "They will not cease to be in doubt about it until the Hour comes upon them suddenly, or the Hour comes upon them." The Day of Resurrection is the Hour. If the "barren day" were also the Day of Resurrection, its meaning would be what we mentioned, namely repeating the mention of the Hour twice with different wording, and that has no meaning. Since this is the case, the more correct of the two interpretations is the one that is most sound in meaning and most consistent with the familiar usage of discourse, which is what we have mentioned regarding its meaning.

Thus the interpretation of the statement is: And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it, until the Hour comes upon them suddenly, and they arrive at the barren punishment, or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day, in which they will not be given respite to look toward the night, nor be delayed until evening, but they will be killed before evening.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 22, verses 54–55**

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, so that they believe in it and their hearts humble themselves to it. Indeed, Allah is the guide of those who believe to a straight path.﴾ (22:54)

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: And so that those with knowledge of God may know that what Allah has sent down from His verses, which He made firm for His Messenger, and abrogated what Satan had cast into it, is the truth from your Lord, O Muhammad. That is, they may affirm it. That is, their hearts may submit to the Qur'an and yield in acknowledging it and affirming what is in it.

And indeed Allah guides those who believe in Allah and His Messenger to the right and direct path, and to the clear truth, by abrogating what Satan cast into the wish of His Messenger, so that the plotting of Satan and his casting of falsehood upon the tongue of their Prophet does not harm them.

And those of the people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:
Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord﴾: He said: It means the Qur'an.

* *

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Those who disbelieved in Allah will not cease to be in doubt.

Then the people of ta'wil differed regarding the pronoun in His words "minhu" (about it): what does it refer to? Some of them said: it refers to the statement of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for."

Mention of those who said that: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it﴾: from his saying: "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for."

And others said: Rather, it refers to the Prophet's (ﷺ) prostration at the Surah of the Star (al-Najm).

And others said: Rather, it refers to the Qur'an.

Mention of those who said that: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it﴾: He said: "From the Qur'an."

The most correct of these opinions regarding this matter is the view of the one who said: it is a pronoun referring to the Qur'an whose verses Allah made firm. The pronoun in His saying "annahu" (that it) refers to the Qur'an. **The interpretation of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿The dominion on that Day belongs to God; He will judge between them. As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in Gardens of Bliss. But as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, they will have a humiliating punishment.﴾ (22:56–57)

Interpretation (ta'wil) of the verse: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Sovereignty and dominion, when the Hour comes, belong to God alone, with no partner and no rival. On that Day no one will contend with Him. In this world there were kings who were called by this name, but on that Day no one will claim sovereignty except Him. ﴿He will judge between them﴾ means: He will separate His creatures, the polytheists who associated others with Him and the believers. ﴿Those who believed﴾ in this Qur'an, in the One who sent it down and the one who brought it, and ﴿did righteous deeds﴾ by acting upon what it contains of its lawful and unlawful matters, its limits and its obligations, ﴿will be in Gardens of Bliss﴾ on that Day. ﴿Those who disbelieved﴾ in God and His Messenger, and ﴿denied His signs﴾ in His Book and its revelation, and said: "This is not from God; it is only a lie that Muhammad fabricated, and other people helped him with it," ﴿for them there is a humiliating punishment﴾. It means: those who have this description will have, with God on the Day of Resurrection, a humiliating punishment, that is, a punishment that degrades them in Hell.

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿And those who emigrated in the way of God and were then killed or died, God will surely provide for them a goodly provision. Indeed, God is the best of providers.﴾ (22:58)

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Those who left their homelands and their clans, abandoning these for the sake of God's pleasure and obedience to Him and for striving against His enemies, and who were then killed or died while in that state, God will surely provide for them on the Day of Resurrection in His Gardens a goodly provision. By "goodly" is meant "noble," and by "provision" is meant "abundant reward." ﴿Indeed, God is the best of providers﴾ means: Indeed, God is the best of those who extend His bounty to the people of His obedience and honor them.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning some of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ who disagreed about the ruling on one who dies in the way of God. Some of them said: the one who was killed and the one who died are equal. Others said: the one who was killed is superior. So God sent down this verse to His Prophet ﷺ, teaching them that the one who dies in His way and the one who is killed in it are equal in reward with Him.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh informed me, from Salaman ibn Amir, who said: Fadalah was in Burudus as commander over the quarters. He went out with the funerals of two men, one of whom had been killed and the other had died naturally. He saw people inclining toward the funeral of the one who had been killed as they went to his grave, so he said: "I see you, O people, inclining toward the one who was killed and preferring him over his brother who died?" They said: "This one was killed in the way of God." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, I do not care in which of the two graves I am raised! The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verses 61–62:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and because Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾ (61).

By His, the Exalted's, words ﴿That﴾, He means: this victory which I grant to the one who was wronged over the transgressor, because I am capable of whatever I will. From His power is that Allah causes the night to enter into the day, meaning: He makes what is lost from the hours of the night enter into the hours of the day, so what is lost from this is added to that. ﴿And causes the day to enter into the night﴾, meaning: He makes what is diminished from the hours of the day enter into the hours of the night, so what is lost from the length of this is added to the length of that. By the power that does this, He gives victory to Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions over those who transgressed against them, who expelled them from their homes and their wealth. ﴿And that Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾, meaning: He does that also because He is possessed of hearing for whatever they say of speech; nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He is Seeing of what they do; nothing of it is absent from Him. All of that is before Him in sight and hearing, and He is the Guardian of all of it, until He recompenses all of them for what they said and did of speech and action, as their recompense.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they call upon besides Him is the falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Great﴾ (62).

By His, the Exalted's, words ﴿That﴾, He means: this act which I have done, of causing the night to enter into the day and the day to enter into the night, because I am the Truth, having no like, no partner, and no equal; and that what these polytheists call upon as gods besides Him is the falsehood, which is not able to create anything, but is itself created. He, the Exalted, says to them: Do you, O ignorant ones, abandon the worship of One from whom benefit comes and in whose hand is harm, who is capable of everything while everything is beneath Him, and worship the falsehood, whose worship does not benefit you?

* *

And His words: ﴿And that Allah is the Most High, the Great﴾

By His words ﴿al-ʿAliyy﴾ (the Most High) He means: possessed of elevation over everything; He is above everything and everything is beneath Him. ﴿al-Kabir﴾ (the Great) means the magnificent, beside whom everything is lesser and nothing is greater than Him.

Ibn Jurayj used to say, regarding His words ﴿And that what they call upon besides Him is the falsehood﴾, that it is:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding His words ﴿And that what they call upon besides Him is the falsehood﴾: "It is Satan."

The reciters differed in reading His words ﴿And that what they call upon besides Him﴾. The majority of the reciters of Iraq and Hijaz read "tadʿūna" (you call upon) with the letter taʾ, in the form of address; and the majority of the reciters of Iraq other than ʿAsim read it with the letter yāʾ (yadʿūna), in the form of report. The yāʾ reading is the more pleasing of the two readings to me, because the beginning of the statement is in the form of address.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verses 61–62:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and because Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾ (61).

By His, the Exalted's, words ﴿That﴾, He means: this victory which I grant to the one who was wronged over the transgressor, because I am capable of whatever I will. From His power is that Allah causes the night to enter into the day, meaning: He makes what is lost from the hours of the night enter into the hours of the day, so what is lost from this is added to that. ﴿And causes the day to enter into the night﴾, meaning: He makes what is diminished from the hours of the day enter into the hours of the night, so what is lost from the length of this is added to the length of that. By the power that does this, He gives victory to Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions over those who transgressed against them, who expelled them from their homes and their wealth. ﴿And that Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾, meaning: He does that also because He is possessed of hearing for whatever they say of speech; nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He is Seeing of what they do; nothing of it is absent from Him. All of that is before Him in sight and hearing, and He is the Guardian of all of it, until He recompenses all of them for what they said and did of speech and action, as their recompense.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they call upon besides Him is the falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Great﴾ (62).

By His, the Exalted's, words ﴿That﴾, He means: this act which I have done, of causing the night to enter into the day and the day to enter into the night, because I am the Truth, having no like, no partner, and no equal; and that what these polytheists call upon as gods besides Him is the falsehood, which is not able to create anything, but is itself created. He, the Exalted, says to them: Do you, O ignorant ones, abandon the worship of One from whom benefit comes and in whose hand is harm, who is capable of everything while everything is beneath Him, and worship the falsehood, whose worship does not benefit you?

* *

And His words: ﴿And that Allah is the Most High, the Great﴾

By His words ﴿al-ʿAliyy﴾ (the Most High) He means: possessed of elevation over everything; He is above everything and everything is beneath Him. ﴿al-Kabir﴾ (the Great) means the magnificent, beside whom everything is lesser and nothing is greater than Him.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding His words ﴿And that what they call upon besides Him is the falsehood﴾: "It is Satan."

The yāʾ reading is the more pleasing of the two readings to me, because the beginning of the statement is in the form of address.

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green? Indeed Allah is Subtle, All-Aware.﴾ (63)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿Have you not seen﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿that Allah sends down water from the sky﴾, meaning rain, ﴿and the earth becomes green﴾ with what grows in it of plants. ﴿Indeed Allah is Subtle﴾ in bringing forth plants from the earth by that water and in other things, by originating whatever He wills to originate, ﴿All-Aware﴾ of what comes forth from that plant of grain. He also said: ﴿and the earth becomes﴾, with the verb in the nominative (raf'), although it is preceded by His words ﴿Have you not seen﴾. This is because the meaning of the statement is a report, as if it were said: "Know, O Muhammad, that Allah sends down water from the sky, so the earth becomes green." A parallel to this is the verse of the poet:

Did you not ask the old abode, and it speaks? Or does the smooth desert tell you today?[[The verse opens a qasida by Jamil ibn Ma'mar al-Udhri (al-Khizana al-Kubra by al-Baghdadi, 3:602). It is cited by grammarians as evidence that the verb after the fa' may remain in the nominative for a while, being an independent (mustani'af) clause. He said: Sibawayh cited this verse and said: "He did not make the first the cause of the second, but made it [the second] speak in every case, as if he said: 'and it is among the things that speak.'" Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas said, citing Abu Ishaq: "It is an affirmation (taqrir), meaning: you have asked it, so it speaks," so the accusative is ugly. I say: that is, because the interrogation (istifham) before it is not pure, but is for affirmation, so it resembles a report, and this is like what the author (al-Tabari) said: its meaning is: you have already asked it, so it spoke. The reading of the verse in al-Khizana has "al-qawa" in place of "al-qadim," which is the place that has been emptied of its inhabitants. The nominative of the verb yanṭiqu (speaks) is like the verb tuṣbiḥu (becomes) in His words: "Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green."]]

Because its meaning is: you have already asked it, so it spoke.

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: To Him belongs dominion over whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of things, who are His servants, His possessions, and His creation, with no partner to Him in that, nor in any part of it. And indeed Allah is the Free of need from all that is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of His creation, while they are the ones in need of Him, and He is the Praiseworthy in the sight of His servants for His bounty upon them and His favours they have received from Him.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 65:

Discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that God has subjected to you whatever is on the earth, and the ships that run upon the sea by His command? And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission. Indeed, God is Most Kind and Merciful to mankind.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Have you not seen, O people, that God has subjected to you what is on the earth of beasts and livestock, so all of that is yours, to use for whatever your needs require. (﴿and the ships that run upon the sea by His command﴾) means: And He has subjected to you the ships that run upon the sea by His command, meaning by His power, and His making them subservient to you in the same way.

The reciters differed over the recitation of His words ﴿wal-Fulka tajri﴾. The majority of the reciters of the great cities read ﴿wal-Fulka﴾ with a fatha (accusative), meaning: He has subjected to you what is on the earth, and the ships (al-Fulk) are in the accusative as a conjunction with "má" (what), or with the repetition of "anna" (that), meaning that the ships run. It is narrated from al-A'raj that he recited it with a damma (nominative), as a new sentence (al-ibtida'). The accusative is the recitation we adopt in this matter, because the consensus of the authoritative reciters rests upon it. ﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth﴾ means: He holds the sky by His power so that it does not fall upon the earth except by His permission. The meaning of His words ﴿an taqa'﴾ (that it fall) is "that it not fall."

﴿Indeed, God is Most Kind and Merciful to mankind﴾ means: He is truly possessed of compassion (ra'fa) and mercy (rahma) toward them. Because of His compassion for them and His mercy toward them, He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission, and He has subjected to you what is described in this verse as a bounty from Him upon you.

The Exposition of the Words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who gave you life, then causes you to die, then gives you life again. Indeed, mankind is ungrateful.﴾ (66) ﴿For every community We have appointed rites which they perform, so let them not dispute with you over the matter, and invite to your Lord. Indeed, you are upon right guidance, a straight path.﴾ (67)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: It is Allah who bestowed upon you these blessings. It is He who made for you bodies that live by a life He brought into being within you, when you were nothing. Then He causes you to die after your lives, bringing you to an end when your appointed terms arrive. Then He gives you life again after your deaths, when He resurrects you for the establishment of the Hour. ﴿Indeed, mankind is ungrateful﴾ means: Indeed, the son of Adam is ungrateful for the blessings of Allah which He has bestowed upon him, such as the goodness of the form He gave him, His subjugation for him of what is in the earth, the land and the sea, and His withholding of destruction from him by holding up the sky lest it fall upon the earth, despite his worship of other than Him, of gods and rivals, and his failure to single Him out for worship and to devote the Oneness to Him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿For every community We have appointed rites﴾

He says: For every group of people who came before you, We have appointed a place they frequent and a locale they habitually visit to worship Me therein, to perform My obligations, and an act to which they are bound. The original meaning of "mansak" in the speech of the Arabs is the familiar place a man frequents and is accustomed to, whether for good or for evil. It is said: "So-and-so has a mansak he frequents," meaning a place he visits and is accustomed to, for good or for evil. The rites of the Hajj are called "manasik" only because people repeatedly go to the places where the acts of Hajj and 'Umrah are performed. There are two dialects for it: "mansik" with a kasra on the sin and a fatha on the mim, which is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, and "mansak" with a fatha on both the mim and the sin, which is the dialect of the Banu Asad. Both have been recited.

The commentators (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed concerning what is meant by His saying: ﴿For every community We have appointed rites﴾, which of the rites is intended? Some of them said: It means their festival which they frequent.

Mention of those who said this: 'Ali related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿For every community We have appointed rites which they perform﴾, he said: a festival.

Others said: It means the slaughter they perform and the blood they shed.

Mention of those who said this: Abu Kurayb related to me, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿For every community We have appointed rites which they perform﴾, he said: the shedding of blood in Makkah.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿they perform﴾, he said: the spilling of the blood of the sacrificial animals.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿a rite﴾, he said: slaughter and pilgrimage.

The correct view on this matter is that it should be said: What is meant is the shedding of blood on the days of sacrifice at Mina, because the rites about which the polytheists disputed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were the shedding of blood on these days. Moreover, they disputed with him concerning the shedding of the blood of slaughtered livestock, as Allah related about them in Surat al-An'am. However, those were not rites; rather, the rites are offerings and sacrifices. For this reason we said: the rite intended in this place is the slaughter that has the description we have mentioned.

* *

And His saying: ﴿So let them not dispute with you over the matter﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So let these polytheists not dispute with you, O Muhammad, over your slaughter and your rite, by their saying: "Do you eat what you have slaughtered yourselves, and not what Allah has killed?" You are more deserving of the truth than they are, for you are upon the truth and they are upon falsehood.

The commentators (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿So let them not dispute with you over the matter﴾, he said: the slaughter.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿So let them not dispute with you over the matter﴾, meaning: do not avoid eating its meat.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And invite to your Lord﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And invite, O Muhammad, those who dispute with you among the polytheists concerning your sacrifice and your slaughter, to follow the command of your Lord in this matter, by not eating except what they have slaughtered after following you and after affirming what you have brought them from Allah, and to avoid slaughtering for the gods and idols and to disavow them. Indeed, you are upon a straight path, not deviating from the road of truth and correctness in your rite, which your Lord has made for you and your community, while they are the astray, having departed from the right way, by opposing Allah's command regarding their slaughter and their worship of gods.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verses 68–69:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And if they dispute with you, say: "Allah knows best what you do."﴾ ﴿Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein you used to differ.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And if these polytheists dispute with you, O Muhammad, concerning your rites (nusuk), then say: "Allah knows best what you do, and what we do."

As follows:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And if they dispute with you﴾, he said: It is the saying of the people of polytheism: "As for what Allah has slaughtered with His right hand..." ﴿So say: "Allah knows best what you do."﴾ "For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds." And His saying: ﴿Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein you used to differ.﴾ He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Allah will decide between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning the matter of your religion in which you used to differ, so that you will know then, O polytheists, who is in the right and who is in the wrong.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verses 68–69:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And if they dispute with you, say: "Allah knows best what you do."﴾ ﴿Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein you used to differ.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And if these polytheists dispute with you, O Muhammad, concerning your rites (nusuk), then say: "Allah knows best what you do, and what we do."

As follows:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And if they dispute with you﴾, he said: It is the saying of the people of polytheism: "As for what Allah has slaughtered with His right hand..." ﴿So say: "Allah knows best what you do."﴾ "For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds." And His saying: ﴿Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein you used to differ.﴾ He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Allah will decide between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning the matter of your religion in which you used to differ, so that you will know then, O polytheists, who is in the right and who is in the wrong.

The Exalted says: Did you not know, O Muhammad, that Allah knows everything in the seven heavens and the seven earths, and nothing of that is hidden from Him? He is the judge among His creatures on the Day of Resurrection, with knowledge of all that they did in this world, so He will recompense the good-doer for his good and the wrongdoer for his wrong. ﴿Indeed that is in a Book﴾: the Exalted says, His knowledge of that is in a Book, which is the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab), in which our Lord, may His majesty be exalted, wrote, before He created His creation, whatever will happen until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Indeed that is easy for Allah﴾.

As follows:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Maysar ibn Isma'il al-Halabi narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, from Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah, who said: Allah knew what He would create and what the creation would do, then He wrote it down, then He said to His Prophet: ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and the earth? Indeed that is in a Book; indeed that is easy for Allah﴾.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Maysar narrated to me, from Artah ibn al-Mundhir, who said: I heard Damrah ibn Habib say: Indeed Allah was upon His Throne, over the water, and He created the heavens and the earth with truth, and He created the Pen and wrote with it what would happen of His creation. Then that Book glorified and praised Allah for a thousand years, before He began any of the creation.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to me, from his father, from Sayyar, from Ibn Abbas, that he asked Ka'b al-Ahbar about the Mother of the Book. He said: Allah knew what He would create and what His creation would do, then He said to His knowledge: Be a book.

Ibn Juraij used to say, regarding His words ﴿Indeed that is in a Book﴾: He said, referring to His words ﴿Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein you used to differ﴾.

We have chosen the view we stated, because His words ﴿Indeed that﴾ up to His words ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and the earth﴾ are closer to one another than to His words ﴿Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein you used to differ﴾. So attaching it to what is closer to it is more appropriate than attaching it to what comes after.

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed that is easy for Allah﴾:

Scholars differ regarding it. Some of them said: Its meaning is: the judging between those who differed in this world on the Day of Resurrection is easy for Allah.

Those who said this: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding ﴿Indeed that is easy for Allah﴾: He said: His judgment on the Day of Resurrection. Then He said, explaining that: ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and the earth? Indeed that is in a Book﴾.

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: that the writing of the Pen, which Allah commanded to write in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) whatever will happen, is easy for Allah, meaning effortless. This second view is more appropriate as an interpretation of this, because His words ﴿Indeed that is easy for Allah﴾ up to His words ﴿Indeed that is in a Book﴾ are closer and adjacent to it, whereas His words ﴿Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection﴾ are distant from it, with His words ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and the earth﴾ intervening between them. So attaching it to what is closer is more appropriate, as far as the context allows, and this is an interpretation that is sound and valid.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they worship besides Allah that for which He has sent down no authority and about which they have no knowledge. And for the wrongdoers there will be no helpers.﴾

Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says: These polytheists worship, besides Allah, what Allah, exalted is His praise, has not sent down any proof for them from the heaven, in any of His books which He sent down to His messengers, that they are gods fit to be worshipped, so that they might worship them on the basis that Allah has permitted them to worship them. And [they worship] what they have no knowledge of, that they are gods. ﴿And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers﴾ means: and there is no helper for the disbelievers in Allah who worship these idols, on the Day of Resurrection, who will rescue them from the punishment of Allah and repel His retribution from them when He wishes to punish them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 72:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you can recognize denial in the faces of those who disbelieve. They almost assault those who recite Our verses to them. Say, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve; and wretched is the destination."﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And when Our verses are recited to the polytheists of Quraysh, who worship other than Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, ﴿Our verses﴾, meaning: the verses of the Qur'an, ﴿clear﴾, meaning: manifest in their proofs and evidences regarding what has been sent down concerning them, ﴿you recognize denial in the faces of those who disbelieve﴾, meaning: you can discern in their faces what the people of faith in Allah disapprove of, of change, upon hearing the Qur'an.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They almost assault those who recite Our verses to them﴾

Meaning: they almost lash out against those who recite to them the verses of the Book of Allah from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, out of their intense aversion to hearing the Qur'an recited to them.

Concerning the interpretation of His saying ﴿yasţūna (they assault)﴾, the people of interpretation have said what we have said.

Those who said this:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muawiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿They almost assault﴾, that he said: they lash out.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿They almost assault﴾, that he said: they fall upon those who mentioned them.

Muhammad ibn Amara narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Israil informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid: ﴿They almost assault those who recite Our verses to them﴾, he said: they almost fall upon them.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿They almost assault﴾, he said: the disbelievers of Quraysh lash out.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿They almost assault those who recite Our verses to them﴾, that he said: they almost seize them by their hands, seizing.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Shall I inform you of something worse than that?﴾

Meaning: Shall I inform you, O polytheists, of something more hateful to you than these people whose recitation of the Qur'an to you you detest? It is ﴿the Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve﴾. It has been reported from some of them that he used to say: the polytheists said, "By Allah, Muhammad and his Companions are the worst of Allah's creation!" So Allah said to them: Say, "Shall I inform you, O you who say this statement, of something worse than Muhammad ﷺ? You, O polytheists, whom Allah has promised the Fire." The word "the Fire" is in the nominative as the subject of a predication (mubtada'), and because it is a definite noun it cannot be described by the word "evil" (sharr), which is indefinite, just as one says: "I passed by two men: your brother and your father." If it were in the genitive it would be permissible; likewise if it were in the accusative, referring back to it through the pronoun in "promised it" (wa'adaha), while intending its connection to what precedes. The meaning, exalted is His remembrance: these are the worst of creation, not Muhammad and his Companions.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And wretched is the destination﴾

Meaning: and wretched is the place to which these polytheists who associate others with Allah will return on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 73–74:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it. And if the fly should snatch away from them something, they could not recover it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought.﴾ (73) ﴿They have not appraised Allah with His true appraisal. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.﴾ (74)

His, the Exalted's, saying: O mankind, a parable has been made of Allah and a mention has been made. The meaning of "ḍaraba" (presented, made) in this place is "ja'ala" (made), from their saying: the ruler "ḍaraba" the dispatch (al-ba'th) upon the people, meaning: imposed it upon them; and "ḍaraba" the jizya (poll tax) upon the Christians, meaning: imposed that upon them. And "al-mathal" (the parable) is "al-shabah" (the likeness). His, may His praise be mentioned, says: "He has made a likeness for Me, O people," meaning by "al-shabah" and "al-mathal": the gods. He says: the polytheists and the idols have made likenesses for Me, so they worship them along with Me, and associate them in My worship. "So listen to it": he says: so listen to the state of what they have made, and to their likening to Me, in their worship of them, and its description. ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly﴾: he says: indeed, all that you worship besides Allah, of gods and idols, even if they were gathered, would not create a fly, in its smallness and insignificance, because they are not able to do that and cannot manage it, even if all of them gathered together to create it. "Dhubab" (fly) is singular; its plural for few is "adhibah" and for many is "dhibbān," like "ghurāb" (crow), whose plural for few is "aghriba" and for many is "ghirbān."

* *

And His saying: ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them something﴾

He says: and if the fly should snatch from the gods and idols something of what is upon them, of perfume or the like of some thing, they could not recover it from it: he says: the gods are not able to rescue that from it.

There is difference concerning the meaning of His saying: ﴿Weak are the seeker and the sought﴾. Some of them said: by "the seeker" is meant the gods, and by "the sought" is meant the fly.

Mention of those who said that: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Weak is the seeker﴾, said: "their gods"; ﴿and the sought﴾: "the fly."

And some of them would say: the meaning of that is: ﴿Weak is the seeker﴾, from among the children of Adam, toward the idol his need; ﴿and the sought﴾, toward which the idol is (asked) to give its petitioner from among the children of Adam what he asked for. He says: it is weak in that and incapable.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is what I have mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas, that its meaning is: the seeker, who is the gods, is incapable of rescuing from the fly what it has snatched from them, which is the perfume and the like; and the sought is the fly.

I have said that this statement is more appropriate as an interpretation of that, because it is within the context of a report about the gods and the fly. For it to be a report about what is connected to it is more fitting than for it to be a report about what is disconnected from it. The Exalted has only informed about the gods, with what He has informed about them in this verse of their weakness and humiliation, as a rebuke by Him to their worshippers among the polytheists of Quraysh. He, may His mention be exalted, says: How can a likeness be made in worship, and there be associated with Me in it what has no power to create a fly, and if the fly takes from it and snatches from it something upon it, it cannot defend itself from it nor avenge itself; whereas I am the Creator of what is in the heavens and the earth, and the Owner of all of that, and the Giver of life to whom I will, and the Causer of death to what I will and whom I will. Indeed, the one who does that, there is no doubt, is in the utmost ignorance.

* *

And His saying: ﴿They have not appraised Allah﴾

He says: these who made the gods partners to Allah in worship did not magnify Allah with the true magnification when they associated others with Him, nor did they single Him out in worship, nor did they know Him with the true knowledge, from their saying: "I did not know the worth (qadr) of so-and-so," when they address by that one who fell short in his due, while they mean to glorify him.

The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said in this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them something﴾ ... to the end of the verse, said: This is a parable which Allah struck for their gods, and he recited: ﴿Weak are the seeker and the sought. They have not appraised Allah with His true appraisal﴾, when they worship along with Allah what cannot defend itself against a fly nor protect itself from it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Powerful﴾

He says: indeed Allah is powerful to create whatever He wills of the small and large of His creation which He wills; Mighty: he says: unassailable in His dominion, no thing besides Him can snatch from His dominion anything, and He is not like your gods, O polytheists, whom you invoke besides Him, who have no power to create a fly, nor to defend themselves from a fly if it snatches something from them, being weak and humiliated.

**The commentary on the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind. Indeed, Allah is Hearing, Seeing.﴾ (75)**

He, the Exalted, says: Allah chooses from among the angels messengers, such as Jibril and Mika'il, whom He sends to His prophets, and [He chooses] from among His servants and from mankind [messengers], such as His prophets whom He sent to His servants among the children of Adam. The meaning of the speech is: Allah chooses from among the angels messengers, and from among mankind also messengers. It has been said: this verse was revealed when the polytheists said: "Has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us?" So Allah said to them: that is up to Me and in My hand, not in the hand of My creation; I choose whom I will of them for the message.

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing, Seeing﴾:

He says: Indeed Allah hears what the polytheists say about Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought from his Lord, and sees who He chooses for His message from among His creation.

* *

**The commentary on the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and to Allah are all matters returned﴾ (76)**

He, the Exalted, says: Allah knows what was before His angels and messengers, before He created them, and what is behind them, meaning: He knows what will be after their passing away. ﴿And to Allah are all matters returned﴾.

He says: To Allah in the Hereafter all the affairs of this world will come back, and to Him they will return, just as the beginning came from Him.

* *

**The commentary on the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, bow and prostrate and worship your Lord and do good that you may succeed﴾ (77)**

He, the Exalted, says: O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger: ﴿bow﴾ to Allah in your prayer, ﴿and prostrate﴾ to Him therein, ﴿and worship your Lord﴾, meaning: humble yourselves before your Lord and submit to Him in obedience, [by doing] what your Lord has commanded you to do, ﴿that you may succeed﴾, meaning: that you may thereby succeed, attaining your requests before your Lord.
