Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 78:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty; it is the religion of your father Abraham. He named you "Muslims" before [this] and in this [revelation], that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people﴾

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: "And strive against the polytheists in the cause of Allah with the striving due to Him."

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Sulayman ibn Bilal informed me, from Thawr ibn Zayd, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him﴾: "As you strove the first time." Then Umar said: "Who commanded the jihad?" He said: "Two tribes of Quraysh, Makhzum and Abd Shams." Then Umar said: "You have spoken truly."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "Do not fear the blame of any blamer in Allah's cause." They said: "And that is the due striving."

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His words ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him﴾: "Do not fear the blame of a blamer in Allah."

Others said: The meaning of that is: "Act upon the truth with its due action." This is a view attributed to al-Dahhak by someone in whose narration there is scrutiny.

The correct view on this matter is the view of the one who said: it refers to striving (jihad) in the cause of Allah, because the known meaning of jihad is that, and it is the predominant sense in the saying of one who says: "I strove in Allah," and the due striving (haqq al-jihad) is exhausting one's capacity in it.

* *

His words ﴿He has chosen you﴾

He says: He chose you for His religion and selected you to wage war against His enemies and to strive in His cause.

Ibn Zayd said about this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿He has chosen you﴾: "He guided you."

* *

His words ﴿and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾

The Exalted says: Your Lord has not placed upon you, in the religion by which He has made you worship Him, any constriction, with no way out for you from what you have been tested with in it; rather He has made it broad for you, making repentance a way out for some [sins], expiation for others, and retaliation (qisas) for others. So there is no sin that the believer commits except that there is for him an exit from it in the religion of Islam.

The interpreters said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan asked Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas about this verse ﴿and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾. Ali ibn Abdullah said: "Haraj (difficulty) is constriction; so Allah made the expiations an exit from that. I heard Ibn Abbas say this."

He said: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyayna narrated to me, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas being asked about ﴿and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾. He said: "Is there anyone here from Hudhayl?" A man said: "Yes." He said: "What do you call the harja among you?" He said: "The constricted thing." Ibn Abbas said: "So it is."

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ibn Uyayna, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: Ibn Abbas said: "Is there anyone here from Hudhayl?" A man said: "I am." He again said: "What do you call the haraj?" and the rest of the narration is like it.

Imran ibn Bakkar al-Kala'i narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hamza narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Abdullah, who said: I heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrating, from Aisha, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this verse (and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty), and he said: "It is constriction."

Humayd ibn Mas'ada narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalda narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Aliyah said to me: "Do you know what haraj is?" I said: "I do not know." He said: "Constriction," and he recited this verse ﴿and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Sa'da narrated to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾, he said: "From constriction."

Amr ibn Bundar narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Abu Khalda, who said: Abu al-Aliyah said to me: "Do you know what haraj is?" I said: "No." He said: "Constriction. Allah has not constricted you; He has not placed upon you in the religion any haraj."

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Ibn Awn, from al-Qasim, that he recited this verse ﴿and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾ and said: "Do you know what haraj is?" He said: "Constriction."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "If anything in the Qur'an is foreign to you, then look into poetry, for poetry is Arabic." Then Ibn Abbas summoned a Bedouin and said: "What is haraj?" He said: "Constriction." He said: "You have spoken truly."

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿in the religion any difficulty﴾, he said: "From constriction."

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, the like of it.

Others said: The meaning of that is ﴿and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾: "constriction in the times of your obligations when they are unclear to you; but He has made it broad for you until you are certain of their proper time."

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughira, from Uthman ibn Bashshar, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾, he said: "This concerns the crescent of the month of Ramadan when people doubt it, and in the Hajj when they doubt the crescent, and in the Fitr and the Adha when it is unclear to them, and the like of that."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "He has not placed in Islam any constriction; rather He has made it broad."

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾, he said: "He has not placed in Islam any constriction; it is broad." It is like His words in al-An'am: ﴿Whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam; and whomever He wills to leave astray, He makes his breast tight and constricted (harajan)﴾. He says: whomever Allah wills to lead astray, He constricts his breast until Islam becomes constricted for him, while Islam is broad.

I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words "and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty": "From constriction," meaning: He made the religion broad and did not make it constricted.

* *

His words ﴿the religion of your father Abraham﴾

The accusative of millah (religion) is in the sense of: "and He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty, but has made it broad, like the religion of your father." Since the particle of comparison (ka) was not present, it was connected to the verb before it and so took the accusative. Its accusative may also be understood as an imperative to adhere to it, since the preceding speech is a command. As if it were said: "Bow and prostrate, and hold fast to the religion of your father Abraham."

* *

His words ﴿He named you Muslims before [this] and in this﴾

The Exalted says: He named you, O assembly of those who believed in Muhammad ﷺ, "Muslims" before [this].

The interpreters said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿He named you Muslims﴾, he said: "Allah named you."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ata ibn Abi Rabah informed me that he heard Ibn Abbas say: "Allah named you Muslims before."

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada; and al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, both from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿He named you Muslims﴾, he said: "Allah named you Muslims before."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿He named you Muslims﴾, he said: "Allah named you."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿He named you Muslims before﴾: "Allah named you Muslims."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: Abraham named you Muslims; and they said it refers back to the mention of Abraham, peace be upon him.

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "Do you not see the words of Abraham ﴿And make us two Muslims to You, and from our descendants a Muslim nation to You﴾?" He said: "This is the words of Abraham, ﴿He named you Muslims﴾." And Allah did not mention the name "Muslim" and "believer" together for any nation other than this one, which was named with both faith and Islam together, and we have not heard of a nation named only with faith. There is no basis for what Ibn Zayd said in this, because it is known that Abraham did not name the community of Muhammad "Muslims" in the Qur'an, since the Qur'an was revealed long after him, and Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿He named you Muslims before and in this﴾. Rather, the One who named us Muslims before the revelation of the Qur'an and in the Qur'an is Allah, who has not ceased and does not cease. As for His words ﴿before﴾, its meaning is: before the revelation of this Qur'an in the books revealed before it; and "in this" means: in this Book.

The interpreters said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿He named you Muslims before﴾, "and in this Qur'an."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Juraij said, Mujahid said regarding ﴿before﴾: "In all the books and the reminder." And "in this" means the Qur'an. As for His words ﴿that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people﴾, the Exalted says: Allah has chosen you and named you, O believers in Allah and His signs, from the community of Muhammad ﷺ, Muslims, so that Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, may be a witness over you on the Day of Resurrection that he has conveyed to you what he was sent with, and that you, at that time, may be witnesses over all the messengers, that they conveyed to their peoples what they were sent with to them.

The interpreters said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿He named you Muslims before﴾, he said: "Allah named you Muslims before," ﴿and in this, that the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾, that he has conveyed to you, ﴿and you may be witnesses over the people﴾, that their messengers have conveyed to them. And from him, from Qatada, who said: "This community was given what no prophet was given: it was said to the Prophet, 'Go, there is no difficulty upon you,' and Allah said ﴿and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾. And it was said to the Prophet ﷺ, 'You are a witness over your people,' and Allah said ﴿that you may be witnesses over the people﴾. And it was said to the Prophet ﷺ, 'Ask and you will be given,' and Allah said ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾."

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, who said: "This community was given three things which no one was given except a prophet. It was said to the Prophet ﷺ, 'Go, there is no difficulty upon you,' and Allah said ﴿and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾. And it was said to the Prophet ﷺ, 'You are a witness over your people,' and Allah said ﴿that you may be witnesses over the people﴾. And it was said to the Prophet ﷺ, 'Ask and you will be given,' and Allah said ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾."

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So establish prayer, give zakat, and hold fast to Allah. He is your protector; how excellent is the protector and how excellent is the helper﴾ (78)

The Exalted means by His words ﴿So establish prayer and give zakat﴾: He says: Perform the prayer prescribed for you by Allah within its limits, and give the zakat obligatory upon you in your wealth. ﴿And hold fast to Allah﴾: He says: trust in Allah and rely upon Him in your affairs. ﴿How excellent is the protector﴾: He says: How excellent is Allah as protector for whoever among you does that, establishes prayer, gives zakat, strives in the cause of Allah with the striving due to Him, and holds fast to Him. ﴿And how excellent is the helper﴾: He says: and how excellent is He as a helper for whoever seeks harm against him.
